grammar.point: Possessives take the article and agree with the thing owned
grammar.explain: Italian says 'the my car' (la mia macchina), and the possessive matches the thing, not the owner.

examples.it: il mio amico, la mia amica, i miei amici, le mie amiche
examples.en: my friend (m), my friend (f), my friends (m), my friends (f)
This is his house. / This is her house.

examples.it: Il loro appartamento è al terzo piano.
examples.en: Their flat is on the third floor.

grammar.trap: suo/sua doesn't tell you whether the owner is a man or a woman: a woman's husband is suo marito, a man's wife is sua moglie. loro never changes and always keeps its article.

grammar.point: No article with one family member
grammar.explain: With a single, plain family word the article drops (mia madre), but it comes back in the plural, with loro, with an added adjective or a pet form, and with partners.

examples.it: mia madre, tuo fratello, sua figlia
examples.en: my mother, your brother, his/her daughter

examples.it: i miei figli, la loro figlia, la mia sorella maggiore
examples.en: my children, their daughter, my older sister

examples.it: la mia compagna, il mio ragazzo, la mia mamma
examples.en: my partner, my boyfriend, my mum

grammar.trap: la mia madre sounds wrong; loro madre (without la) is just as wrong. i miei on its own means 'my parents'.

grammar.point: Whose? di chi è? and possessive pronouns
grammar.explain: Ask 'of whom is it?' (Di chi è?), and answer with mio, tuo, suo, usually without the article after essere.

examples.it: Di chi è questa borsa? — È mia.
examples.en: Whose bag is this? — It's mine.

examples.it: Di chi sono questi occhiali? — Sono di Anna.
examples.en: Whose glasses are these? — They're Anna's.

examples.it: La tua casa è grande, la mia è piccola.
examples.en: Your house is big, mine is small.

grammar.trap: Chi è questa borsa? asks who the bag is; you need di chi. Italian has no 's: Anna's bag = la borsa di Anna.

grammar.point: Describing people: essere, avere and agreement
grammar.explain: Use essere with adjectives that agree with the person, and avere for hair and eyes.

examples.it: Mio fratello è alto e magro; mia sorella è bassa.
examples.en: My brother is tall and thin; my sister is short.

examples.it: Ha i capelli grigi e gli occhi azzurri.
examples.en: He has grey hair and blue eyes.

examples.it: Com'è il tuo vicino? — È gentile ma un po' timido.
examples.en: What's your neighbour like? — He's kind but a bit shy.

grammar.trap: è capelli biondi is wrong: hair is something you have (ha i capelli biondi). And capelli is plural: i capelli sono lunghi.

vocabulary.en: son (la figlia = daughter; i figli = children)

pronunciation: gli is one soft sound, like the 'lli' in million, never a hard g: figlio, figlia, moglie, famiglia.
Hold double consonants: nonno (grandfather) vs nono (ninth), nonna, sorella, fratello.

common_errors.wrong: La mia madre vive a Londra.
common_errors.why: No article with one plain family word.
loro always keeps its article.
The possessive agrees with the thing owned (marito), not with the woman who owns it.
'Whose' is di chi.

common_errors.right: Mia sorella ha i capelli lunghi.
common_errors.why: Hair and eyes go with avere, and need the article.

common_errors.wrong: Come sta tua sorella? — È alta e simpatica.
common_errors.right: Com'è tua sorella? — È alta e simpatica.
common_errors.why: Come sta asks about health; Com'è asks what someone is like.

units.culture: Questions like Ha figli? or È sposato? and showing family photos on your phone are normal small talk with neighbours, not prying; expect them early, answer briefly and ask back.
recycles: a1-11: Ti piace …? / Mi piace molto
units.evidence: Without help, the learner says who is in their family with correct possessives (mia figlia, i miei figli, la mia compagna), answers Com'è? with two agreeing adjectives, and settles whose something is with di chi è? / è mio.
sources: P1B U6 A–B (possessives, family; Di chi è questa bici? È mia.)
P1a U1 F (describing people)
P1a U3 (mio / tuo / suo)
Proudfoot U10
EGSI ch.35, 45

units.title: Settling in: routine and how you're getting on
units.can_do: Describe your daily routine and say how you're settling in: what you've got used to and what's still hard.
situations: the question every newcomer gets: Si trova bene?
chatting with a barista or neighbour about your day
comparing daily life here and at home
telling someone you got lost again

frames.it: Si trova bene qui?
frames.en: Are you settling in well here?
frames.note: To a friend: Ti trovi bene?

frames.it: Sì, mi trovo benissimo.
frames.en: Yes, I'm getting on really well.

frames.it: La mattina mi alzo presto e faccio due passi.
frames.en: In the morning I get up early and go for a little walk.
frames.note: due passi = a short walk, not literally two steps.

frames.it: Di solito vado al mercato il sabato.
frames.en: I usually go to the market on Saturdays.

frames.it: Mi sto abituando agli orari dei negozi.
frames.en: I'm getting used to the shop hours.

frames.it: Non mi sono ancora abituato a cenare alle nove.
frames.en: I still haven't got used to having dinner at nine.
frames.note: A woman says abituata.

frames.it: Mi sono perso un'altra volta!
frames.en: I got lost again!
frames.note: A woman says persa.

frames.it: Ogni tanto mi manca casa.
frames.en: Now and then I miss home.
frames.note: mi manca works like mi piace: the thing missed is the subject (mi mancano i miei figli).

model_exchanges.situation: the regular question at the bar counter (Lei)

lines.speaker: barista
lines.it: Allora, si trova bene qui?
lines.en: So, are you settling in well here?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Sì, mi trovo benissimo, grazie.
lines.en: Yes, really well, thanks.

lines.speaker: barista
lines.it: E c'è qualcosa di difficile?
lines.en: And is anything hard?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Gli orari! Non mi sono ancora abituato a cenare alle nove.
lines.en: The times! I still haven't got used to having dinner at nine.

lines.speaker: barista
lines.it: Eh, qui si cena tardi. E la mattina?
lines.en: Well, people eat late here. And in the morning?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: La mattina mi alzo presto, faccio due passi e vengo qui per il caffè.
lines.en: In the morning I get up early, go for a little walk and come here for coffee.

lines.speaker: barista
lines.it: Bravo, così si comincia bene la giornata!
lines.en: Good for you, that's the way to start the day!

model_exchanges.situation: meeting a neighbour on the stairs (Lei)

lines.speaker: vicino
lines.it: Buongiorno! Tutto bene? È stanco?
lines.en: Good morning! All well? Are you tired?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Un po'. Mi sono perso un'altra volta!
lines.en: A bit. I got lost again!

lines.speaker: vicino
lines.it: Nel centro storico? Succede a tutti.
lines.en: In the old town? It happens to everyone.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Le strade sono tutte uguali! Però mi sto abituando.
lines.en: The streets all look the same! But I'm getting used to it.

lines.speaker: vicino
lines.it: Tra un mese le conosce tutte, vedrà.
lines.en: In a month you'll know them all, you'll see.

model_exchanges.situation: a friend asks about your week (tu)

lines.speaker: amica
lines.it: Cosa fai di solito la domenica?
lines.en: What do you usually do on Sundays?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Di solito mi sveglio tardi e vado al mercato.
lines.en: I usually wake up late and go to the market.

lines.speaker: amica
lines.it: La domenica? Ma il mercato è il sabato!
lines.en: On Sundays? But the market's on Saturdays!

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Ah, è vero, il sabato. La domenica mi riposo.
lines.en: Oh, that's right, Saturdays. On Sundays I rest.

lines.speaker: amica
lines.it: E ti trovi bene qui?
lines.en: And are you happy here?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Sì, molto. Ogni tanto mi manca casa, ma mi trovo bene.
lines.en: Yes, very. Now and then I miss home, but I'm happy here.

grammar.explain: Many everyday verbs come with mi, ti, si, ci, vi, si in front, because the action falls back on you.

examples.it: Mi alzo alle sette, ti alzi tardi, si alza presto.
examples.en: I get up at seven, you get up late, he gets up early.
We're happy here.

examples.it: A che ora si svegliano i bambini?
examples.en: What time do the children wake up?

grammar.trap: The pronoun can't be dropped: alzo alle sette means nothing. trovarsi bene (to be happy somewhere) isn't trovare (to find).

grammar.point: Reflexives in the past take essere
grammar.explain: In the passato prossimo a reflexive verb always uses essere, and the participle agrees with you.

examples.it: Mi sono alzato presto. / Mi sono alzata presto.
examples.en: I got up early (man / woman).
We had a great time.
Did you get lost?

grammar.trap: mi ho alzato is wrong: reflexives never use avere.

grammar.point: abituarsi a: getting used to something
grammar.explain: abituarsi takes a, which joins the article (al, agli) before a noun, or comes straight before an infinitive.

examples.it: Mi sto abituando al caffè ristretto.
examples.en: I'm getting used to short espresso.

examples.it: Non mi sono ancora abituata a cenare tardi.
examples.en: I haven't got used to eating late yet.

grammar.trap: English 'I used to' (a past habit) is not abituarsi; that's the imperfetto (a2-04). And it's abituarsi a, never di.

grammar.point: How often: di solito, spesso, ogni tanto, non … mai
grammar.explain: Frequency words usually sit near the verb, and mai needs non before the verb.

examples.en: I usually have dinner at eight.
I go to the cinema now and then.

examples.it: Non bevo mai il cappuccino dopo pranzo.
examples.en: I never drink cappuccino after lunch.
on Saturdays, on Sundays

grammar.trap: Bevo mai is wrong; it's non bevo mai (double negative). sabato alone = this Saturday; il sabato = every Saturday.

grammar.point: stare + gerund only for what's happening right now
grammar.explain: Sto + -ando / -endo describes something in progress at this moment or changing now; the plain present covers most English -ing.

examples.en: I'm getting used to it (it's happening).
What are you doing? — I'm cooking.
I've been studying Italian for six months.

grammar.trap: Don't use sto + -ando for habits or plans: 'I'm studying Italian this year' is studio l'italiano, and 'I'm going out tonight' is stasera esco.

vocabulary.en: to be happy somewhere, to settle in well
to be missed (mi manca = I miss)
to go for a short walk

pronunciation: sv in svegliarsi is voiced, like a buzzing 'zv', then gli: SVE-glio.
In the 'they' form the stress stays early: si alzano = AL-za-no, si svegliano = SVE-glia-no, never al-ZA-no.

common_errors.why: Reflexive verbs need their pronoun.
Reflexives use essere in the past, and the participle agrees.

common_errors.wrong: Sto andando al mercato ogni sabato.
common_errors.why: Habits take the plain present.
mai needs non before the verb.
With mancare the people or things you miss are the subject, like piacere.
abituarsi takes a.

units.culture: Lunch is around 1 and dinner around 8 or 9 (later in the south), and in many towns small shops close from about 1 to 4 and on Sunday; plan errands for the morning or late afternoon.
recycles: a1-15: passato prossimo with essere and agreement (sono andato / andata)
a1-03: mi chiamo as the first reflexive
a1-08: times and days (alle nove, il sabato)
a1-11: mi piace (pattern for mi manca)
units.evidence: Asked Si trova bene?, the learner answers and adds one thing they're used to and one they aren't, using a reflexive in the present and one in the past with the right agreement, plus a frequency word.
sources: P1B U9 A (reflexives, reciprocals; workbook si trova bene vs trova)
Proudfoot U7 (routine, frequency), U6 (stare + gerund), U20 (ci ha chiesto se ci trovassimo bene in Italia)
EGSI ch.21 (progressive), ch.30 (reflexives)

units.title: Eating out
units.can_do: Book a table, order a full meal, ask what to choose, mention allergies and diets, and ask for and settle the bill.
situations: eating with a food allergy or a vegetarian friend

frames.it: Buonasera, avete un tavolo per due?
frames.en: Good evening, do you have a table for two?

frames.it: Vorrei prenotare per stasera alle otto e mezza.
frames.en: I'd like to book for tonight at half past eight.

frames.it: Cosa ci consiglia?
frames.en: What do you recommend?
frames.note: ci = to us; alone, mi consiglia?

frames.it: Come primo prendo le tagliatelle al ragù.
frames.en: For my first course I'll have tagliatelle with ragù.

frames.it: Il mio amico è vegetariano: cosa gli consiglia?
frames.en: My friend is vegetarian: what would you suggest for him?
frames.note: gli = to him; for a woman, le.

frames.it: Sono celiaco: avete la pasta senza glutine?
frames.en: I'm coeliac: do you have gluten-free pasta?
frames.note: A woman says celiaca.

frames.it: Ci porta il conto, per favore?
frames.en: Could you bring us the bill, please?

frames.it: Possiamo pagare separatamente?
frames.en: Can we pay separately?

frames.it: Era tutto buonissimo, grazie!
frames.en: Everything was delicious, thanks!

model_exchanges.situation: booking by phone

lines.speaker: ristoratore
lines.it: Pronto, buonasera!
lines.en: Hello, good evening!

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Buonasera, vorrei prenotare un tavolo per stasera.
lines.en: Good evening, I'd like to book a table for tonight.

lines.speaker: ristoratore
lines.it: Per quante persone?
lines.en: For how many people?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Per due, alle otto e mezza.
lines.en: For two, at half past eight.

lines.speaker: ristoratore
lines.it: Va bene. A che nome?
lines.en: Fine. What name?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: A nome …
lines.en: In the name of …

lines.speaker: ristoratore
lines.it: Perfetto, a stasera!
lines.en: Perfect, see you tonight!

model_exchanges.situation: ordering in a trattoria (the waiter uses voi)

lines.speaker: cameriere
lines.it: Avete deciso?
lines.en: Have you decided?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Cosa ci consiglia?
lines.en: What do you recommend?

lines.speaker: cameriere
lines.it: Le tagliatelle al ragù sono la nostra specialità.
lines.en: The tagliatelle with ragù are our speciality.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Allora le prendo. Però sono celiaco: avete la pasta senza glutine?
lines.en: Then I'll have them. But I'm coeliac: do you have gluten-free pasta?

lines.speaker: cameriere
lines.it: Sì, certo. E per la signora?
lines.en: Yes, of course. And for the lady?

lines.speaker: amica
lines.it: Per me cacio e pepe, e come secondo niente, grazie.
lines.en: Cacio e pepe for me, and no main course, thanks.

lines.speaker: cameriere
lines.it: Da bere?
lines.en: To drink?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Una bottiglia d'acqua frizzante e mezzo litro di vino della casa.
lines.en: A bottle of sparkling water and half a litre of house wine.

model_exchanges.situation: paying at the end

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Scusi, ci porta il conto, per favore?
lines.en: Excuse me, could you bring us the bill, please?

lines.speaker: cameriere
lines.it: Subito. Tutto bene?
lines.en: Right away. Was everything all right?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Era tutto buonissimo, grazie!
lines.en: Everything was delicious, thanks!

lines.speaker: amica
lines.it: Possiamo pagare separatamente?
lines.en: Can we pay separately?

lines.speaker: cameriere
lines.it: Mi dispiace, facciamo un conto unico.
lines.en: Sorry, we only do one bill.

lines.speaker: amica
lines.it: Va bene, allora facciamo alla romana.
lines.en: OK, then we'll split it down the middle.

grammar.explain: Say which course with come primo, come secondo, per dolce, and use prendere for what you'll have.

examples.en: As a starter we'll have bruschetta.

examples.it: Come secondo prendo il pollo, con un contorno di patate.
examples.en: As a main I'll have the chicken, with a side of potatoes.
For dessert, a tiramisù.

grammar.trap: Don't translate 'for the first course' word for word (per il primo corso); and il primo is pasta, rice or soup, not the starter.

grammar.point: mi, ci, gli, le before the verb: 'to me, to us, to him, to her'
grammar.explain: Short pronouns meaning 'to someone' go before the verb as fixed chunks: ci porta? mi consiglia? gli piace?

examples.en: Could you bring us another bottle of water?
Can you recommend a red wine?

examples.it: A mia moglie non piace il pesce: le piace la carne.
examples.en: My wife doesn't like fish: she likes meat.

grammar.trap: Porta il conto a noi? is heavy; say Ci porta il conto? And watch gli (to him) vs le (to her) vs Le (to you, formal).

grammar.point: lo, la, li, le prendo: 'I'll have it / them'
grammar.explain: To say 'I'll have it', put lo, la, li or le before prendo, matching the dish.

examples.en: The risotto? Yes, I'll have it.
The tagliatelle? I'll have them too.

grammar.trap: Pasta names are plural (le tagliatelle, gli spaghetti), so 'it' becomes le or li.

grammar.point: era: 'it was' at the end of a meal
grammar.explain: era, the past of essere for description, is the natural way to say how the food was.

examples.en: Everything was delicious.

examples.it: La carne era un po' salata.
examples.en: The meat was a bit salty.

grammar.trap: è stato buonissimo is possible but less natural for describing food; use era.

vocabulary.en: pasta with pecorino and black pepper

pronunciation: zz in pizza and pizzeria sounds like 'ts', held: PIT-tsa.
Hold the double consonants: tagliatelle, cotto (cooked) vs coto (not a word), frizzante.

common_errors.wrong: Per il primo corso prendo la lasagna.
common_errors.why: Courses are come primo / come secondo; lasagne is usually plural on menus.

common_errors.wrong: Gli piace il pesce? (about a woman)
common_errors.why: le = to her; gli = to him.

common_errors.wrong: La carne ben fatta, per favore.
common_errors.right: La carne ben cotta, per favore.
common_errors.why: Well done is ben cotto.

common_errors.wrong: Il conto, per favore. (then waiting for it to arrive by itself)
common_errors.why: You must ask; Italian waiters don't bring the bill unasked.
Cappuccino is a morning drink; after a meal Italians have an espresso.
Separati is common in speech, but the correct adverb is separatamente; or simply say facciamo alla romana.

units.culture: The bill usually has a coperto (cover charge) per person and service is normally included, so tipping is optional (round up or leave a few euros); and the bill only comes when you ask for it.
recycles: a1-05: Quant'è? Posso pagare con la carta?
units.evidence: In a restaurant scene the learner books for a number of people and a time, orders by course with come primo / come secondo, mentions a diet or allergy, and asks for the bill with Ci porta il conto?, without falling back to English.
sources: P1B U6 C (restaurant and menu; Lei cosa consiglia?; Ben cotta), U6 culture 'Dove mangiano gli italiani?'
P1a U4 (era as a chunk; bar ordering)
Proudfoot U14 (vorremmo), U16 (piacere for others)
gap: bill, coperto, allergies, splitting (P1a §5, P1B §5)

units.title: Stories: how things were
units.can_do: Tell a short story with background and events, and talk about your life before you came to Italy.
functions: tell a story with background and events
situations: telling a new friend about your life before Italy
telling a neighbour what happened on the way home
remembering an evening with a friend

frames.it: Cosa facevi prima di venire in Italia?
frames.en: What did you do before you came to Italy?
frames.note: Lei: Cosa faceva …?

frames.it: Prima di trasferirmi qui, abitavo a …
frames.en: Before I moved here, I lived in …

frames.it: Da piccolo andavo al mare ogni estate.
frames.en: As a child I went to the sea every summer.
frames.note: A woman says da piccola.

frames.it: Mentre aspettavo l'autobus, ho incontrato la vicina.
frames.en: While I was waiting for the bus, I ran into my neighbour.

frames.it: C'era tantissima gente in piazza.
frames.en: There were loads of people in the square.
frames.note: la gente is singular in Italian: c'era, not c'erano.

frames.it: Pioveva, e così siamo rimasti a casa.
frames.en: It was raining, so we stayed home.

frames.it: Ti ricordi quella sera?
frames.en: Do you remember that evening?

frames.it: Ero stanchissimo!
frames.en: I was exhausted!
frames.note: A woman says stanchissima.

model_exchanges.situation: a new friend asks about your life before (tu)

lines.speaker: amico
lines.it: Cosa facevi prima di venire in Italia?
lines.en: What did you do before you came to Italy?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Lavoravo in un ufficio. Adesso sono in pensione.
lines.en: I worked in an office. Now I'm retired.

lines.speaker: amico
lines.it: E dove abitavi?
lines.en: And where did you live?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: In una città grande, vicino al mare. Ho abitato lì per trent'anni.
lines.en: In a big city, near the sea. I lived there for thirty years.

lines.speaker: amico
lines.it: E da piccolo andavi in vacanza?
lines.en: And as a child did you go on holiday?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Sì, andavo al mare ogni estate con i miei.
lines.en: Yes, I went to the sea every summer with my parents.

lines.speaker: amico
lines.it: Che bei tempi!
lines.en: Those were the days!

model_exchanges.situation: telling a neighbour about last night (tu)

lines.speaker: vicina
lines.it: Allora, com'è andata ieri sera?
lines.en: So, how did last night go?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Che serata! Mentre aspettavo l'autobus, ha cominciato a piovere.
lines.en: What an evening! While I was waiting for the bus, it started to rain.

lines.speaker: vicina
lines.it: E non avevi l'ombrello?
lines.en: And you didn't have an umbrella?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: No! Ero stanchissimo e non c'erano taxi.
lines.en: No! I was exhausted and there weren't any taxis.

lines.speaker: vicina
lines.it: E allora cosa hai fatto?
lines.en: So what did you do?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Sono tornato a piedi. Alla fine sono arrivato a casa tutto bagnato!
lines.en: I walked home. In the end I got home soaking wet!

lines.speaker: vicina
lines.it: Poverino!
lines.en: Poor thing!

model_exchanges.situation: remembering an evening with a friend (tu)

lines.speaker: amica
lines.it: Ti ricordi quella sera in piazza?
lines.en: Do you remember that evening in the square?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Quale? Non mi ricordo.
lines.en: Which one? I don't remember.

lines.speaker: amica
lines.it: Quella del concerto! C'era tantissima gente.
lines.en: The one with the concert! There were loads of people.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Ah sì! Faceva caldo e tutti ballavano.
lines.en: Oh yes! It was hot and everyone was dancing.

lines.speaker: amica
lines.it: E tu non volevi ballare…
lines.en: And you didn't want to dance…

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: È vero, ma poi ho ballato tutta la sera!
lines.en: True, but then I danced all evening!

grammar.explain: Take the infinitive, drop -re and add -vo, -vi, -va, -vamo, -vate, -vano; essere is irregular (ero, eri, era…), and fare, bere, dire use older stems.

examples.en: I lived / I used to live, I read / was reading, I slept / was sleeping

examples.it: ero, eri, era, eravamo, eravate, erano
examples.en: I was, you were, he/she was, we were, you were, they were
I did, I drank, I said (used to / was -ing)

grammar.trap: The stress doesn't move to the end: abitàvano (a-bi-TA-va-no), not abitavàno.

grammar.explain: The imperfetto sets the scene (background, what used to happen, what things were like); the passato prossimo tells what happened next.

examples.en: It was raining and it was cold.

examples.it: Da piccola andavo al mare ogni estate. (habit)
examples.en: As a child I went to the sea every summer.

examples.it: Ieri sono andata al mare. (one event)
examples.en: Yesterday I went to the sea.

grammar.trap: English 'went' gives no clue: ask yourself whether it's a habit or background (andavo) or a single event (sono andato). 'Used to' and 'was -ing' are always imperfetto.

grammar.explain: mentre (while) takes the imperfetto for the background action, and c'era / c'erano describe what was there.

examples.it: Mentre cucinavo, è suonato il telefono.
examples.en: While I was cooking, the phone rang.

examples.it: C'era un bel sole. C'erano tanti turisti.
examples.en: It was sunny. There were lots of tourists.

grammar.trap: c'è stato is an event ('there was an accident'); for a description use c'era.

grammar.explain: 'Before doing' is prima di + infinitive, with any pronoun attached to the end.

examples.it: Prima di trasferirmi qui, lavoravo a Londra.
examples.en: Before I moved here, I worked in London.

examples.it: Prima di uscire, chiudo il gas.
examples.en: Before going out, I turn off the gas.

grammar.trap: Not prima di mi trasferisco or prima di trasferendo: the infinitive, with mi on the end.

grammar.explain: 'To remember' is usually reflexive, mi ricordo, ti ricordi; before an infinitive it needs di (ricordati di chiamare), and before a noun di is optional (mi ricordo di lui / mi ricordo il nome).

examples.en: Do you remember that evening?

examples.it: Non mi ricordo il suo nome.
examples.en: I don't remember his name.
Remember to call Grandma!

grammar.trap: English remember has no pronoun; Italian adds mi, ti, si: non mi ricordo, not non ricordo me.

pronunciation: Imperfetto stress sits on the same syllable for every person: abitAvo, abitAvi, abitAvano; parlAvo, parlAvano.
c'era has a soft c, like 'ch' in church: CHE-ra.

common_errors.wrong: Da piccolo sono andato al mare ogni estate.
common_errors.right: Da piccolo andavo al mare ogni estate.
common_errors.why: A repeated past habit takes the imperfetto.

common_errors.wrong: Mentre ho aspettato l'autobus, ho visto Marco.
common_errors.right: Mentre aspettavo l'autobus, ho visto Marco.
common_errors.why: The background action after mentre is imperfetto.
gente is grammatically singular.

common_errors.wrong: Ho abitato a Boston da trent'anni.
common_errors.right: Ho abitato a Boston per trent'anni.
common_errors.why: A finished period takes per; da + present is for something still going on (abito qui da un anno).
prima di takes the infinitive, with the pronoun attached.
ricordarsi is reflexive; the pronoun goes before the verb.

units.culture: Italians often tell a story in the present to make it vivid (Allora, arrivo a casa e … chi trovo?); don't be thrown, it still means the past, and you can stick to the past tenses yourself.
recycles: a1-15: passato prossimo (sono andato, ho fatto)
units.evidence: Telling what happened yesterday or describing life before Italy, the learner uses the imperfetto for at least one background or habit and the passato prossimo for the events, without being corrected on the choice.
sources: P1B U7 A–C (imperfetto, vs passato prossimo, memories: Ti ricordi…? Che bei tempi!)
Proudfoot U11 (per vs da), U12 (describing the past)
EGSI ch.23 (past tenses)

units.title: At the deli counter: pronouns and quantities
units.can_do: Shop at a deli counter with ease: take a number, ask by weight, refer back with pronouns, taste, and ask for things cut your way.
situations: a busy deli with a number machine
checking the cupboard with a friend before shopping

frames.it: Ho il quarantasette. Tocca a me?
frames.en: I'm number 47. Is it my turn?

frames.it: Il prosciutto lo vorrei tagliato sottile.
frames.en: I'd like the prosciutto sliced thin.

grammar.explain: To avoid repeating a thing, use lo (m), la (f), li (m pl), le (f pl) right before the verb.

examples.en: The pecorino? I'll take it.
Green apples? I prefer them.

examples.it: Il prosciutto lo vorrei tagliato sottile.
examples.en: I'd like the prosciutto sliced thin.

grammar.trap: Not prendo lo: the pronoun goes before the verb. Its gender follows the Italian noun (la mozzarella → la, i grissini → li).

grammar.explain: With a modal verb, the pronoun goes either before it or on the end of the infinitive, never in between.

examples.en: Can I taste it?
I have to buy them.

grammar.trap: posso lo assaggiare is wrong.

grammar.point: ne: 'of it, of them' with quantities
grammar.explain: When you give a number or amount without repeating the noun, add ne before the verb.

examples.it: Quanto ne vuole? — Ne prendo tre etti.
examples.en: How much do you want? — I'll take three hundred grams.
I'd like two (of them).
Eggs? I've got six.

grammar.trap: Vorrei due on its own sounds unfinished; say ne vorrei due. And lo prendo tre etti is wrong: a quantity takes ne, not lo.

grammar.point: ce l'ho, ce l'avete; ce n'è, ce ne sono
grammar.explain: To say you have 'it', Italians add ce before l'ho; to say there is 'some', ce n'è (one thing) or ce ne sono (several).

examples.it: Il pane ce l'hai? — Sì, ce l'ho. / No, non ce l'ho.
examples.en: Have you got bread? — Yes, I have. / No, I haven't.
Do you have it in a jar?

examples.it: C'è latte? — Sì, ce n'è un litro.
examples.en: Is there milk? — Yes, there's a litre.

grammar.trap: Sì, l'ho alone sounds wrong in speech; say Sì, ce l'ho. With plural things: ce li ho, ce le ho.

grammar.point: After lo, la, li, le the past participle agrees (recognise)
grammar.explain: In the passato prossimo with avere, the participle takes the ending of a lo/la/li/le that comes before it.

examples.en: The mozzarella? I bought it yesterday.

examples.it: I pomodori? Li ho comprati al mercato.
examples.en: The tomatoes? I bought them at the market.

grammar.trap: l'ho preso for la mozzarella will be understood, but you'll hear l'ho presa; notice it rather than worry about it yet.

pronunciation: sc before i or e is 'sh': prosciutto = pro-SHOOT-to; but sc before o is 'sk': scontrino.
ce in ce l'ho, ce n'è sounds 'che' (as in check); don't confuse it with che (ke): ce n'è = che-NEH, stressed on the è.

common_errors.why: Object pronouns go before the verb.

common_errors.wrong: Vorrei due. / Lo prendo tre etti.
common_errors.right: Ne vorrei due. / Ne prendo tre etti.
common_errors.why: A quantity without the noun needs ne.
In speech 'I've got it' is ce l'ho.
The pronoun goes before the modal or on the end of the infinitive.
The pronoun matches the noun's gender.
Not wrong, but at the counter everyone counts in etti.

units.culture: At a busy deli or supermarket counter you take a numbered ticket from the machine and wait to be called; at the fruit and veg section of a supermarket, put on the plastic gloves before touching anything and weigh and label it yourself.

units.evidence: At a counter the learner asks for a product, answers Quanto ne vuole? with ne + an amount, refers back to the product with lo/la/li/le, and asks Ce l'avete …? or Ce n'è ancora? without being prompted.
sources: P1B U8 A (supermarket), C (deli counter: desidera? quanto ne vuole? ne prendo tre), G (ce l'ho, ce n'è), grammar on pronouns with modals and participle agreement
Proudfoot U3 (ce n'è, ce ne sono), U14 (lo/la vs ne)
P2 U8 (numbered tickets)
gap: queue and number machine (P1B §5.8)

units.title: Clothes and shops: sizes, fit and returns
units.can_do: Buy clothes or a gift: ask for a colour and size, try it on, say how it fits, ask about a discount, and exchange it if needed.

frames.it: La posso provare?

frames.it: Come mi sta? — Ti sta benissimo!

grammar.explain: Clothes are nouns with a gender, so 'it' and 'them' follow them: la giacca → la provo, i pantaloni → li prendo.

examples.en: The jacket? I'll take it.
Can I try these trousers on?

examples.it: Il maglione lo vorrei in blu.
examples.en: I'd like the jumper in blue.

grammar.trap: pantaloni, jeans and occhiali are plural, so 'them' (li), even though English says 'a pair'.

grammar.point: stare bene a qualcuno: how something looks on you
grammar.explain: The clothes are the subject of stare: mi sta (it suits me), mi stanno (they suit me), ti sta, Le sta.

examples.en: This jacket really suits you.
How do the shoes fit you?
It's a bit loose on me.

grammar.trap: Sto bene con questa giacca is not how it's said; the jacket does the 'standing': questa giacca mi sta bene.

grammar.explain: Colours in -o change like adjectives (rosso, rossa, rossi, rosse), colours in -e have two forms, and blu, rosa, viola never change.

examples.it: una sciarpa rossa, due sciarpe rosse
examples.en: a red scarf, two red scarves
a green coat, green shoes
blue trousers, a pink shirt

grammar.trap: pantaloni blui and camicie rose are wrong: blu and rosa don't change.

grammar.point: quello and bello before a noun change like the article
grammar.explain: Before a noun, 'that' and 'beautiful' copy the ending of il, lo, l', i, gli: quel, quello, quell', quei, quegli; bel, bello, bell', bei, begli.

examples.en: that jumper, that backpack, that suit

examples.it: quei pantaloni, quegli stivali, quella gonna
examples.en: those trousers, those boots, that skirt

examples.it: un bel cappotto, dei begli occhiali
examples.en: a nice coat, some nice glasses

grammar.trap: quello maglione is wrong (il maglione → quel maglione). After the noun the form doesn't change: un cappotto bello.

grammar.point: si può + infinitive: is it allowed?
grammar.explain: si può asks whether something can generally be done, without saying who.

examples.en: Can it be exchanged?

examples.it: Si può pagare con la carta?
examples.en: Can you pay by card?

grammar.trap: Posso cambiarla? asks for you, now; si può cambiare? asks about the shop's rule. Both are fine, but si può is the safer question before you pay.

vocabulary.en: to suit, to fit (mi sta bene)

pronunciation: scarpe (shoes) has a hard 'sk'; sciarpa (scarf) has a soft 'sh': SKAR-pe vs SHAR-pa. Mixing them up changes the word.
gi in giacca is 'j', and the cc is held: JAK-ka.

common_errors.why: giacca is feminine, so 'it' is la.

common_errors.right: Che taglia porta? / Che taglia hai?
common_errors.why: Size is la taglia (shoes: il numero), and the verb is portare or avere.
blu, rosa and viola don't change.
Before a noun quello changes like the article: il → quel.
The clothes are the subject of stare bene.
To exchange is cambiare; to return is restituire. ritornare means to go back.

units.culture: Shops only have to take back faulty goods; for something that simply doesn't fit, many offer an exchange or a voucher (buono) but no refund, so ask Si può cambiare? before paying and keep the scontrino. The big sales start in early January and early July.
recycles: a2-05: lo / la / li / le, ce l'abbiamo
a1-05: Quanto costa? Posso pagare con la carta?
a2-02: reflexive mettersi (mi metto la giacca)
units.evidence: In a clothes shop the learner asks for a colour and size, uses the right pronoun for the item (la provo, li prendo), says how it fits with mi sta / è stretto, and, in a return, says what's wrong and asks to exchange it.
sources: P1B U9 B–D (clothes shop with the commessa, colours, opinions, impersonal si; the decalogue of the sales); U6 (quello and bello)
Proudfoot U5 (quello forms; clothes shopping)
gap: returns and exchanges (P1B §5.9)

grammar.point: Indirect pronouns: 'to me, to you, to him, to her'
grammar.explain: mi, ti, gli (to him), le (to her), Le (to you, formal), ci, vi, gli (to them) go before the verb and replace a + person.

examples.en: Can you lend me a pen?

examples.it: Gli telefono domani. / Le telefono domani.
examples.en: I'll call him tomorrow. / I'll call her tomorrow.

examples.it: Signora, Le posso chiedere un favore?
examples.en: Signora, can I ask you a favour?

grammar.trap: Italian verbs, not English ones, decide: telefonare takes a, so 'call her' is le telefono, not la telefono. Watch gli (him) vs le (her).

grammar.point: Le dispiace se …? / Ti dispiace se …?
grammar.explain: To ask permission politely, use dispiacere + se + present, or + infinitive when asking someone to do something.

examples.it: Le dispiace se apro la finestra?
examples.en: Do you mind if I open the window?
Do you mind waiting for me a moment?

grammar.trap: As in English 'do you mind?', the yes answer is no: No, prego / No, figurati. Answering Sì means you do mind.

grammar.explain: In the passato prossimo the participle agrees with lo/la/li/le but never with gli, le, Le meaning 'to someone'.

examples.en: I gave her the keys.
We gave him a book.

grammar.trap: le ho data le chiavi is wrong: here le means 'to her', so dato stays as it is.

grammar.point: Lei and tu: darsi del tu
grammar.explain: dare del Lei / del tu means to address someone as Lei or tu, and darsi del tu means to agree to use tu with each other.

examples.en: Shall we use tu?
Let's use tu!

examples.it: Mi dà del Lei, ma io gli do del tu.
examples.en: He calls me Lei, but I call him tu.

grammar.trap: With older people and in shops, wait for them to offer tu, or ask; switching on your own can sound cheeky. Once tu is agreed, keep it.

vocabulary.en: to use tu with each other
Not at all! (Lei form of Figurati!)

pronunciation: The pronoun gli is a single soft sound, like 'lli' in million: gli telefono = lyee te-LE-fo-no, never 'glee'.
le (to her) is one short syllable; lei (she) has two vowels: le do = I give her, lei dà = she gives.

common_errors.why: telefonare takes a + person, so the pronoun is le (to her).
gli = to him; le = to her.
The participle doesn't agree with an indirect pronoun.
The pronoun goes in one place only.

common_errors.wrong: Le dispiace se apro? — Sì, prego.
common_errors.right: Le dispiace se apro? — No, prego.
common_errors.why: As with 'do you mind?', no means go ahead.
The fixed phrase is darsi del tu.

units.culture: The older person, or the one with more standing (a landlady, an older neighbour), usually offers tu; once you're on tu with someone it's a sign you belong, so don't slip back to Lei.
