lines.it: A che piano?
lines.en: Which floor?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Al terzo. Suona il campanello e sali! Se non trovi la strada, chiamami.
lines.en: The third. Ring the bell and come up! If you can't find the way, call me.

model_exchanges.situation: a friend teaches you to cook pasta (tu)

lines.speaker: amica
lines.it: Prima metti l'acqua sul fuoco.
lines.en: First put the water on the stove.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: E il sale?
lines.en: And the salt?

lines.speaker: amica
lines.it: Quando l'acqua bolle, metti il sale e poi butta la pasta. Mescola ogni tanto.
lines.en: When the water boils, add the salt and then throw in the pasta. Stir now and then.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: La scolo dopo otto minuti?
lines.en: Do I drain it after eight minutes?

lines.speaker: amica
lines.it: Sì, ma prima assaggiala! E non toccare la pentola, scotta!
lines.en: Yes, but taste it first! And don't touch the pan, it's hot!

model_exchanges.situation: a passer-by gives directions (Lei)

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Scusi, per la chiesa di San Francesco?
lines.en: Excuse me, how do I get to the church of San Francesco?

lines.speaker: passante
lines.it: Allora, attraversi la piazza, prenda la prima a sinistra e vada sempre dritto. La chiesa è proprio di fronte.
lines.en: So, cross the square, take the first left and keep going straight. The church is right opposite.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: La prima a sinistra, poi sempre dritto. È lontano?
lines.en: First left, then straight on. Is it far?

lines.speaker: passante
lines.it: Cinque minuti a piedi. Ma non si preoccupi, l'accompagno io.
lines.en: Five minutes on foot. But don't worry, I'll walk you there.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Grazie, è molto gentile!
lines.en: Thank you, that's very kind!

grammar.point: The imperative for tu, noi and voi
grammar.explain: For tu, -are verbs end in -a (gira, aspetta) and -ere / -ire verbs in -i (prendi, scendi, senti); noi and voi are the same as the present.

examples.en: Turn right! Take the bus!
Let's go! Shall we eat something?

examples.it: Ragazzi, venite qui! Scendete alla terza fermata.
examples.en: Guys, come here! Get off at the third stop.

grammar.trap: To a friend it's gira; giri is the Lei form you hear from strangers.

grammar.explain: andare, fare, dare, dire and stare have short tu commands: va', fa', da', di', sta'; vai, fai, dai and stai are also used.

examples.en: Keep going straight.
Be careful!
Don't worry! / Relax!

grammar.trap: di' (say) has an apostrophe so it isn't confused with di (of).

grammar.explain: To tell a friend not to do something, use non + the infinitive; with noi and voi just add non.

examples.en: Don't touch!
Don't forget the keys!
Don't make noise! (to several)

grammar.trap: non tocca! is wrong (it means 'he doesn't touch'); it's non toccare!

grammar.point: Pronouns join the end of the command
grammar.explain: With tu, noi and voi commands, pronouns attach to the verb as one word; after va', fa', da', di', sta' the consonant doubles.

examples.en: Wait for me! Call me! Taste it!
Tell me! Let me see!
Don't worry!

grammar.trap: mi aspetta! is a statement ('he waits for me'), not an order: say aspettami! And it's dimmi, not dimi (except gli: digli).

grammar.explain: Strangers, shopkeepers and doctors use the Lei form, where -are verbs end in -i and -ere / -ire verbs in -a, the reverse of the tu form.

examples.it: Giri a sinistra, prenda la seconda strada.
examples.en: Turn left, take the second street.

examples.it: Vada sempre dritto. Attraversi la piazza.
examples.en: Keep going straight. Cross the square.
Don't worry!

grammar.trap: The endings look swapped: giri (from girare), prenda (from prendere). You'll produce these at B1; for now just recognise them.

vocabulary.en: on the right, to the right (a sinistra = left)
to get on, to come up
to go with, walk someone there

pronunciation: After va', fa', da', di', sta' the pronoun's first consonant doubles and is held: dimmi, fammi, dallo, vacci; but digli.
va' sounds just like va; the apostrophe is only in writing.

common_errors.why: A negative tu command is non + infinitive.
giri is the Lei form; to a friend -are verbs end in -a.
With a tu command the pronoun goes on the end.
After di' the consonant doubles.
The pronoun joins the command as one word.
Negative tu = non + infinitive; non si preoccupi is the Lei form.

units.culture: Italians give directions by landmarks (the pharmacy, the church, the traffic lights) more than by street names, and a passer-by will often say ti accompagno and walk you there; listen for the landmarks.
recycles: a1-07: dov'è …? per andare a …? a destra, a sinistra, accanto a
a1-13: prendere l'autobus, scendere, la fermata
units.evidence: The learner tells a friend how to reach a place in three or more steps using tu commands (prendi, scendi, gira, va'), attaches a pronoun at least once (aspettami, chiamami), uses non + infinitive for a warning, and follows Lei directions from a stranger.
sources: P1B U10 E–F (imperative with pronouns; directions in Rome; workbook: prendi l'autobus 60 … scendi alla quarta fermata … aspettami!)
Proudfoot U9 (imperatives incl. Lei; directions dialogue: attraversi la piazza e la stazione è proprio di fronte)
EGSI ch.27 (imperative)

units.title: Plans, predictions and holidays
units.can_do: Talk about plans and predictions, make guesses, say what you'll do if …, and join in the year's holidays.
situations: planning a trip around the forecast
Christmas and Easter with Italian friends

frames.it: Quest'estate andrò in Sicilia.
frames.en: This summer I'll go to Sicily.

frames.it: Domani pioverà, dicono.
frames.en: It'll rain tomorrow, they say.

frames.it: Se fa bel tempo, andiamo al mare.
frames.en: If the weather's nice, we'll go to the sea.

frames.it: Sarà chiuso per ferie.
frames.en: It must be closed for the holidays.
frames.note: The future can be a guess about now.

frames.it: Che fai a Ferragosto?
frames.en: What are you doing for Ferragosto?
frames.note: 15 August.

frames.it: Cosa farai per Natale?
frames.en: What will you do for Christmas?

frames.it: Ti chiamo appena arrivo.
frames.en: I'll call you as soon as I arrive.

frames.it: Buone feste! — Grazie, altrettanto!
frames.en: Happy holidays! — Thanks, same to you!

model_exchanges.situation: the bakery has been shut for days in August (tu)

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Il panificio è chiuso da tre giorni!
lines.en: The bakery's been shut for three days!

lines.speaker: amica
lines.it: Sarà chiuso per ferie. In agosto chiudono in tanti.
lines.en: It must be closed for the holidays. Lots of places close in August.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: E quando riapre?
lines.en: And when does it reopen?

lines.speaker: amica
lines.it: Riaprirà dopo Ferragosto, credo. Ma tu che fai a Ferragosto?
lines.en: After Ferragosto, I think. But what are you doing for Ferragosto?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Niente di speciale. Resterò in città.
lines.en: Nothing special. I'll stay in town.

lines.speaker: amica
lines.it: Ma no! Vieni al mare con noi!
lines.en: Oh, come on! Come to the sea with us!

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Volentieri, se non piove!
lines.en: I'd love to, if it doesn't rain!

model_exchanges.situation: planning a day out around the forecast (tu)

lines.speaker: amico
lines.it: Sabato andiamo in montagna?
lines.en: Shall we go to the mountains on Saturday?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Sabato pioverà, dicono. Ci sarà anche un temporale.
lines.en: It'll rain on Saturday, they say. There'll be a storm too.

lines.speaker: amico
lines.it: Allora domenica? Le previsioni dicono sole.
lines.en: Sunday, then? The forecast says sun.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Va bene. Se fa bel tempo, partiamo presto.
lines.en: OK. If the weather's nice, we'll leave early.

lines.speaker: amico
lines.it: Ti chiamo sabato sera e decidiamo.
lines.en: I'll call you on Saturday evening and we'll decide.

model_exchanges.situation: Christmas wishes at a shop (Lei)

lines.speaker: negoziante
lines.it: Ecco a Lei. E buone feste!
lines.en: Here you are. And happy holidays!

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Grazie, altrettanto! Lei cosa farà a Natale?
lines.en: Thanks, same to you! What will you do for Christmas?

lines.speaker: negoziante
lines.it: Starò con i miei figli. E Lei? Tornerà a casa?
lines.en: I'll be with my children. And you? Will you go home?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: No, quest'anno resterò qui. Farò un Natale italiano!
lines.en: No, this year I'll stay here. I'll have an Italian Christmas!

lines.speaker: negoziante
lines.it: Allora buon Natale e buon anno!
lines.en: Then merry Christmas and happy new year!

grammar.explain: Drop the final -e of the infinitive (-are verbs change a to e) and add -ò, -ai, -à, -emo, -ete, -anno.

examples.en: I'll speak, I'll take, I'll leave
We'll stay at home.
When will you come back?

grammar.trap: -are verbs take -er-: parlerò, not parlarò. Spelling: cercherò, pagherò (add h); mangerò, comincerò (drop i).

grammar.explain: A handful of everyday verbs shorten or change the stem but keep the same endings.

examples.en: I'll go, I'll be, I'll have, I'll do, I'll stay
I'll come, I'll want, I'll be able to, I'll have to, I'll see

grammar.trap: venirò and andarò don't exist: verrò, andrò.

grammar.point: The future as a guess about now
grammar.explain: Italians use the future to say what is probably true right now, where English says 'must be' or 'probably'.

examples.en: It must be closed for the holidays.

examples.it: Che ore sono? — Saranno le otto.
examples.en: What time is it? — It must be about eight.
She's not answering: she's probably at work.

grammar.trap: This sarà is about the present, not the future.

grammar.explain: With a likely condition, use se + present and then the present or the future; quando and appena work the same way.

examples.it: Se fa bel tempo, andiamo al mare.
examples.en: If the weather's nice, we'll go to the sea.

examples.it: Se vieni anche tu, ci divertiremo.
examples.en: If you come too, we'll have fun.
I'll call you as soon as I arrive.

grammar.trap: Never the conditional after se here: se farebbe bel tempo is wrong.

grammar.point: The present is still fine for plans
grammar.explain: For fixed plans in the near future, Italians mostly use the present; the future adds intention, distance or a promise.

examples.en: I'm leaving for Rome tomorrow.
I promise: I'll write to you.

grammar.trap: 'I'm going to …' is not vado a … (that means physically going somewhere to do it); say farò or faccio.

vocabulary.en: New Year's Day / New Year's Eve
best wishes (Auguri! = Happy birthday / Happy holidays)

pronunciation: Stress the last syllable of the io and lui/lei forms: andrò, farò, pioverà. Without that final stress the word sounds foreign, and in some verbs it changes the tense: parlo (I speak) vs parlò (he spoke).
Ferragosto has a held rr: fer-ra-GO-sto.

common_errors.why: venire has an irregular future stem: verr-.

common_errors.wrong: Se farebbe bel tempo, andiamo al mare.
common_errors.right: Se fa bel tempo, andiamo al mare.
common_errors.why: A real condition takes se + present (or future), never the conditional.

common_errors.wrong: Vado a visitare mia figlia l'anno prossimo. (meaning 'I'm going to')
common_errors.right: L'anno prossimo andrò a trovare mia figlia.
common_errors.why: andare a means physically going; for plans use the future or present. Visiting a person is andare a trovare.
'In two weeks' from now is tra; in due settimane means 'taking two weeks'.

common_errors.right: Buone feste! — Grazie, altrettanto! / Grazie, anche a te!
common_errors.why: The set reply is altrettanto or anche a te / anche a Lei.
Not wrong, but the future of guessing is what Italians usually say.

units.culture: In August many shops, bakeries and even doctors' surgeries close for two or three weeks around Ferragosto (15 August), with a sign saying chiuso per ferie and the reopening date; check before you need something, and stock up.
recycles: a1-12: present for plans (domani vado al mare), Volentieri!
a2-04: past tenses to compare last year and this year
units.evidence: Asked about the summer or a holiday, the learner answers with two or three future verbs including an irregular (andrò, farò, starò), makes one guess with sarà, sets one condition with se + present, and replies to holiday wishes with altrettanto.
sources: P1a U5 (future, uses of the future, weather forecast, Christmas; moved from A1 to A2)
P1B U10 (sarà già cominciata)
Proudfoot U13 (future, present for future, 'going to' ≠ andare a), U22 (real conditions)
EGSI ch.25

units.title: Opinions and comparisons
units.can_do: Give and ask for opinions, agree or disagree politely, and compare places, food and things.
situations: choosing a wine with the shopkeeper
arguing about the best gelato in town
talking about a film or a book

frames.it: Secondo me, questo vino è migliore di quello.
frames.en: In my opinion, this wine is better than that one.
frames.note: più buono di is just as common in speech.

frames.it: Cosa ne pensi? / Che ne pensa?
frames.en: What do you think of it? (tu / Lei)

frames.it: Mi sembra un po' caro.
frames.en: It seems a bit expensive to me.

frames.it: Sono d'accordo. / Non sono d'accordo.
frames.en: I agree. / I don't agree.

frames.it: Hai ragione, ma …
frames.en: You're right, but …

frames.it: Bologna è più tranquilla di Roma.
frames.en: Bologna is quieter than Rome.

frames.it: È la gelateria più buona della città.
frames.en: It's the best gelateria in town.

frames.it: Questa pizza è buonissima!
frames.en: This pizza is really good!

model_exchanges.situation: choosing a wine in a wine shop (Lei)

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Buongiorno, cerco un vino rosso per una cena. Che ne pensa di questo?
lines.en: Good morning, I'm looking for a red wine for a dinner. What do you think of this one?

lines.speaker: enotecaio
lines.it: È buono, ma secondo me questo è migliore: è più morbido.
lines.en: It's good, but in my opinion this one is better: it's smoother.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Mi sembra un po' caro.
lines.en: It seems a bit expensive to me.

lines.speaker: enotecaio
lines.it: Ha ragione, costa di più. Ma è il migliore della zona.
lines.en: You're right, it costs more. But it's the best in the area.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Va bene, mi ha convinto. Lo prendo.
lines.en: All right, you've convinced me. I'll take it.

model_exchanges.situation: comparing cities with a local friend (tu)

lines.speaker: amico
lines.it: Allora, ti piace più Bologna o Roma?
lines.en: So, do you like Bologna or Rome better?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Bologna è più tranquilla di Roma, ma Roma è più bella.
lines.en: Bologna is quieter than Rome, but Rome is more beautiful.

lines.speaker: amico
lines.it: Non sono d'accordo! Bologna è bellissima.
lines.en: I don't agree! Bologna is gorgeous.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Hai ragione, è bella, ma è meno grande e meno caotica.
lines.en: You're right, it is beautiful, but it's smaller and less chaotic.

lines.speaker: amico
lines.it: E si mangia meglio!
lines.en: And the food's better!

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Su questo sono d'accordo.
lines.en: I agree on that.

model_exchanges.situation: arguing about gelato (tu)

lines.speaker: amica
lines.it: Questa è la gelateria più buona della città.
lines.en: This is the best gelateria in town.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Secondo me no. Quella in piazza è migliore.
lines.en: I don't think so. The one in the square is better.

lines.speaker: amica
lines.it: Davvero? Cosa ne pensi del pistacchio qui?
lines.en: Really? What do you think of the pistachio here?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: È buonissimo, ma in piazza è meno dolce e più cremoso.
lines.en: It's really good, but in the square it's less sweet and creamier.

lines.speaker: amica
lines.it: Allora andiamo a provarlo!
lines.en: Then let's go and try it!

grammar.point: Giving an opinion: secondo me, per me
grammar.explain: secondo me and per me ('in my opinion') are followed by a normal sentence, with no special verb form.

examples.it: Secondo me, è un ottimo ristorante.
examples.en: In my opinion, it's an excellent restaurant.
For me it's too expensive.
Do you think it's open?

grammar.trap: Penso che … needs a different verb form (the subjunctive, B1); secondo me + an ordinary verb is the safe way to give an opinion now.

grammar.explain: To say how something seems to you, use mi sembra with one thing and mi sembrano with several.

examples.en: It seems a bit expensive to me.
These shoes seem tight to me.
Does that seem fair to you?

grammar.trap: The thing is the subject, like piacere: mi sembrano cari, not mi sembra cari.

grammar.point: Che ne pensi?: ne means 'of it'
grammar.explain: To ask someone's opinion of something already mentioned, use ne pensi / ne pensa.

examples.it: Che ne pensi di questo vino?
examples.en: What do you think of this wine?
The film? What do you think of it?

grammar.trap: Cosa pensi? alone asks 'what are you thinking?'; add ne for 'what do you think of it?'

grammar.explain: 'More … than' is più … di, 'less … than' is meno … di, and 'as … as' is (così) … come; di joins the article.

examples.it: Roma è più grande di Bologna.
examples.en: Rome is bigger than Bologna.

examples.it: Il treno è meno caro della macchina.
examples.en: The train is cheaper than the car.
Florence is as beautiful as Rome.

grammar.trap: 'Than' before a noun or name is di, not che: più grande di Roma.

grammar.point: The most and the very: il più … di, -issimo, migliore
grammar.explain: 'The best in town' is il più buono della città (or il migliore); 'really good' is buonissimo; migliore and peggiore are 'better' and 'worse'.

examples.it: È il ristorante più caro della città.
examples.en: It's the most expensive restaurant in town.
This coffee is excellent!

examples.it: Questo vino è migliore; quello è peggiore.
examples.en: This wine is better; that one is worse.

grammar.trap: 'In town' after a superlative is della città, not in città; and più migliore is wrong: migliore already means 'more good'.

grammar.explain: Being right or wrong is something you 'have' in Italian.

examples.en: You're right.
You're wrong, madam.

grammar.trap: sono giusto doesn't mean 'I'm right'; say ho ragione.

pronunciation: Hold the double s of -issimo: buonissimo, bellissimo, carissimo; a single s sounds like a different word.
più is one syllable with the stress on the final ù: PYOO.

common_errors.wrong: Roma è più grande che Bologna.
common_errors.right: Roma è più grande di Bologna.
common_errors.why: Before a noun or name, 'than' is di.

common_errors.wrong: È il ristorante più buono in città.
common_errors.right: È il ristorante più buono della città.
common_errors.why: After a superlative, 'in' a place is di.
migliore already means 'better'.
Being right is avere ragione.
The things are the subject: plural verb.
'Of it' is ne, before the verb.

units.culture: Italians argue about food, wine, football and whose city is best with real passion, and it's friendly: saying Non sono d'accordo is fine. Just go gently on someone's hometown dish or their mother's cooking.
recycles: a1-11: mi piace / mi piacciono, anche a me / a me no
a2-03: food and wine words, era buonissimo
units.evidence: In a conversation about places or food, the learner gives an opinion with secondo me or mi sembra, asks Che ne pensi?, agrees or disagrees with a reason, and makes at least one correct comparison with più / meno … di or a superlative.
sources: P1B U7 D (agree / disagree box), U9 D (Che ne pensi? Mi sembra un po' pesante), U10 (mi sembra / mi pare)
P2 U3 (comparatives; core moved down to A2)
Proudfoot U17 (opinion chunks), Appendix 3 (comparison)
EGSI ch.34

units.title: Polite requests, wishes and advice
units.can_do: Make polite requests, say what you'd like to do, and give and take advice.
situations: asking a bookseller or a wine seller for advice
saying you'd like to learn something

frames.it: Potrebbe consigliarmi un buon libro italiano?
frames.en: Could you recommend a good Italian book?

frames.it: Mi farebbe un favore?
frames.en: Would you do me a favour?

frames.it: Ti dispiacerebbe chiudere la finestra?
frames.en: Would you mind closing the window?
frames.note: Lei: Le dispiacerebbe …?

frames.it: Volevo chiederLe una cosa.
frames.en: I wanted to ask you something.
frames.note: volevo is a polite 'I'd like', not really past.

frames.it: Mi piacerebbe imparare a fare la pasta fresca.
frames.en: I'd love to learn to make fresh pasta.

frames.it: Dovresti assaggiare la ribollita.
frames.en: You should try the ribollita.

frames.it: Al posto tuo, prenderei il treno.
frames.en: If I were you, I'd take the train.

frames.it: Preferirei di no.
frames.en: I'd rather not.

model_exchanges.situation: in a bookshop (Lei)

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Buongiorno, volevo chiederLe una cosa. Potrebbe consigliarmi un buon libro italiano? Non troppo difficile.
lines.en: Good morning, I wanted to ask you something. Could you recommend a good Italian book? Not too difficult.

lines.speaker: libraio
lines.it: Le piacerebbe un romanzo o un giallo?
lines.en: Would you like a novel or a crime story?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Un giallo, direi.
lines.en: A crime story, I think.

lines.speaker: libraio
lines.it: Allora proverei questo: è facile e divertente.
lines.en: Then I'd try this one: it's easy and fun.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Perfetto, lo prendo.
lines.en: Perfect, I'll take it.

model_exchanges.situation: a friend asks for advice (tu)

lines.speaker: amica
lines.it: Domenica vorrei andare a Firenze in macchina.
lines.en: On Sunday I'd like to drive to Florence.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Al posto tuo, prenderei il treno: è più comodo, e in centro non si può entrare in macchina.
lines.en: If I were you, I'd take the train: it's easier, and you can't drive into the centre.

lines.speaker: amica
lines.it: Hai ragione. Dovrei prenotare?
lines.en: You're right. Should I book?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Sì, dovresti comprare il biglietto online.
lines.en: Yes, you should buy the ticket online.

lines.speaker: amica
lines.it: Mi accompagneresti?
lines.en: Would you come with me?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Mi piacerebbe, ma domenica ho un impegno. Mi dispiace!
lines.en: I'd love to, but I've got something on on Sunday. Sorry!

model_exchanges.situation: an offer from an older neighbour (tu)

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Mi piacerebbe imparare a fare la pasta fresca.
lines.en: I'd love to learn to make fresh pasta.

lines.speaker: vicina
lines.it: Ti insegno io! Verresti sabato mattina?
lines.en: I'll teach you! Would you come on Saturday morning?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Volentieri! Cosa dovrei portare?
lines.en: I'd love to! What should I bring?

lines.speaker: vicina
lines.it: Niente, solo la voglia di lavorare!
lines.en: Nothing, just the will to work!

grammar.explain: Use the future stem and add -ei, -esti, -ebbe, -emmo, -este, -ebbero; the irregular stems are the same as the future.

examples.en: I'd take, you'd prefer, he/she would recommend

examples.it: vorrei, potrei, dovrei, sarei, avrei, farei, verrei
examples.en: I'd like, I could, I should, I'd be, I'd have, I'd do, I'd come
We could go together.

grammar.trap: potremmo (we could) and potremo (we'll be able to) differ only by a double m; listen for it.

grammar.explain: Use it to ask politely, to say what you'd like, to give advice and to soften a no.

examples.it: Mi farebbe un favore? / Potrebbe aiutarmi?
examples.en: Would you do me a favour? / Could you help me?
I'd love to see Venice.

examples.it: Dovresti riposare. / Al posto tuo, andrei dal medico.
examples.en: You should rest. / If I were you, I'd see a doctor.
I'd rather not.

grammar.trap: 'You should' is dovresti; devi means 'you must' and sounds like an order. 'If I were you' at this level is al posto tuo (se fossi in te comes at B1).

grammar.explain: In shops and offices, volevo ('I wanted') is a soft way of saying what you'd like now.

examples.en: Good morning, I'd like some information.
I'd like to see that jumper.

grammar.trap: It isn't about the past: volevo una pizza means 'I'd like a pizza'.

grammar.explain: Some verbs need a small word before the next infinitive: imparare a, provare a, cominciare a; cercare di, decidere di, finire di.

examples.en: I'm learning to cook.
Try calling tomorrow.
I try to speak only Italian.

grammar.trap: imparo cucinare is wrong; and English -ing after 'try', 'stop', 'start' becomes the infinitive: prova a chiamare.

vocabulary.en: to be able to (potrebbe = could you)
to please (mi piacerebbe = I'd love to)
if I were you (al posto Suo with Lei)

pronunciation: Conditional noi has a double m, future noi a single one: potremmo (we could) vs potremo (we'll be able to); andremmo vs andremo.
-ei in vorrei, potrei is two vowels gliding together, stressed on the e: vor-REI.

common_errors.why: Advice takes the conditional; devi sounds like an order.
The thing you'd like (imparare) is the subject, so the verb is third person.
imparare takes a before an infinitive.

common_errors.wrong: Se io sarei te, prenderei il treno.
common_errors.right: Al posto tuo, prenderei il treno.
common_errors.why: Never the conditional after se; al posto tuo is the A2 way.
volere has the irregular stem vorr-.
'Could' is the conditional, with a double m.

units.culture: In shops and offices, Buongiorno, volevo … or Vorrei … is all the politeness you need; long English-style hedging ('I was just wondering if you could possibly …') isn't expected and can sound odd.
recycles: a1-04: vorrei as a chunk, now one form of the conditional
a2-09: the future stems (andr-, sar-, vorr-)
units.evidence: The learner makes a polite request with potrebbe / mi farebbe, says what they'd like with mi piacerebbe or vorrei + infinitive, and gives advice with dovresti or al posto tuo + conditional, choosing the conditional rather than the present.
sources: P1B U11 (conditional forms and uses: Potresti …? Dovresti … Al posto tuo … Mi piacerebbe … Preferirei di no), appendix (volevo)
Proudfoot U12 (polite imperfect), U14 (verb + a / di + infinitive), U20 (polite requests)
EGSI ch.29

units.title: Seeing a doctor
units.can_do: Make a doctor's appointment, describe symptoms and how long you've had them, and understand the instructions and the prescription.
situations: a sprain or a bad cold

frames.it: Vorrei prendere un appuntamento con il medico.
frames.en: I'd like to make an appointment with the doctor.

frames.it: Il dottore riceve il martedì e il giovedì.
frames.en: The doctor sees patients on Tuesdays and Thursdays.

frames.it: Da tre giorni ho la tosse e mi fa male il petto.
frames.en: I've had a cough for three days and my chest hurts.

frames.it: Mi sono fatto male alla caviglia.
frames.en: I've hurt my ankle.
frames.note: A woman says fatta.

frames.it: Prenda una compressa due volte al giorno, dopo i pasti.
frames.en: Take one tablet twice a day, after meals.

frames.it: Serve la ricetta?
frames.en: Do I need a prescription?

frames.it: Ogni quanto devo prenderlo?
frames.en: How often should I take it?

frames.it: Il medico mi ha detto di riposare.
frames.en: The doctor told me to rest.

model_exchanges.situation: phoning the surgery (Lei)

lines.speaker: segretaria
lines.it: Pronto, studio medico, buongiorno.
lines.en: Hello, doctor's surgery, good morning.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Buongiorno, vorrei prendere un appuntamento con il dottore.
lines.en: Good morning, I'd like to make an appointment with the doctor.

lines.speaker: segretaria
lines.it: È un paziente del dottore?
lines.en: Are you one of the doctor's patients?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Sì, sono iscritto da un mese.
lines.en: Yes, I've been registered for a month.

lines.speaker: segretaria
lines.it: Il dottore riceve il martedì e il giovedì. Va bene giovedì alle dieci?
lines.en: The doctor sees patients on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Is Thursday at ten all right?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Sì, perfetto. Grazie.
lines.en: Yes, perfect. Thank you.

model_exchanges.situation: at the doctor's (Lei)

lines.speaker: medico
lines.it: Allora, mi dica. Cosa c'è?
lines.en: So, tell me. What's the matter?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Da tre giorni ho la tosse e mi fa male il petto.
lines.en: I've had a cough for three days and my chest hurts.

lines.speaker: medico
lines.it: Ha la febbre?
lines.en: Do you have a temperature?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Sì, ieri sera avevo trentotto.
lines.en: Yes, last night I had a temperature of 38.

lines.speaker: medico
lines.it: Vediamo… Respiri. Non è niente di grave. Prenda una compressa due volte al giorno, dopo i pasti, e beva molta acqua.
lines.en: Let's see… Breathe in. It's nothing serious. Take one tablet twice a day, after meals, and drink plenty of water.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Serve la ricetta?
lines.en: Do I need a prescription?

lines.speaker: medico
lines.it: Sì, ecco la ricetta. Se non va meglio, torni lunedì.
lines.en: Yes, here's the prescription. If it doesn't get better, come back on Monday.

model_exchanges.situation: at the pharmacy after a sprain (Lei)

lines.speaker: farmacista
lines.it: Buongiorno, mi dica.
lines.en: Good morning, how can I help?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Mi sono fatto male alla caviglia. Il medico mi ha detto di riposare e di mettere questa pomata.
lines.en: I've hurt my ankle. The doctor told me to rest and to put on this cream.

lines.speaker: farmacista
lines.it: Ecco la pomata. La metta tre volte al giorno.
lines.en: Here's the cream. Put it on three times a day.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: E per il dolore? Ogni quanto devo prendere l'antidolorifico?
lines.en: And for the pain? How often should I take the painkiller?

lines.speaker: farmacista
lines.it: Una compressa ogni otto ore, solo se ha dolore.
lines.en: One tablet every eight hours, only if you're in pain.

grammar.point: da + present: how long you've had it
grammar.explain: For something that started in the past and is still going on, Italian uses the present + da.

examples.en: I've had a temperature since yesterday.

examples.it: Da tre giorni mi fa male la schiena.
examples.en: My back has been hurting for three days.

grammar.trap: Not ho avuto la tosse per tre giorni (that means it's over); if it's still going on, it's ho la tosse da tre giorni.

grammar.explain: 'I've hurt my …' is mi sono fatto male a + the body part, with essere and agreement.

examples.it: Mi sono fatto male al ginocchio.
examples.en: I've hurt my knee.

examples.it: Si è fatta male alla mano.
examples.en: She's hurt her hand.

grammar.trap: ho fatto male alla caviglia is wrong (no si); and Italian says 'to the ankle' (alla caviglia), not 'my ankle'.

grammar.explain: Doctors and pharmacists give instructions in the Lei form: prenda, beva, torni, respiri, metta.

examples.it: Prenda queste compresse e beva molto.
examples.en: Take these tablets and drink a lot.
Come back in a week.
Don't go out for two days.

grammar.trap: The endings look swapped (-are → -i, -ere → -a): prenda comes from prendere, torni from tornare. Understand them; you'll produce them at B1.

grammar.explain: With devo or posso, put lo / la before the verb or on the end of the infinitive.

examples.it: Ogni quanto devo prenderlo? / Ogni quanto lo devo prendere?
examples.en: How often do I have to take it?
Can I take it on an empty stomach?

grammar.trap: devo lo prendere is wrong: never between the two verbs.

grammar.point: dire di + infinitive: what you were told to do
grammar.explain: To report an instruction, use dire a qualcuno di + infinitive.

examples.it: Il medico mi ha detto di riposare.
examples.en: The doctor told me to rest.

examples.it: Mi ha detto di non bere alcol.
examples.en: She told me not to drink alcohol.

grammar.trap: mi ha detto riposare is wrong: you need di.

pronunciation: Hold the double consonants that carry the meaning: febbre, tosse, ricetta, compressa, petto.
gli in caviglia is the soft 'lli' of million: ca-VEE-lya.

common_errors.wrong: Ho la tosse per tre giorni.
common_errors.right: Ho la tosse da tre giorni.
common_errors.why: Still going on: present + da.

common_errors.right: Mi sono fatto male alla caviglia.
common_errors.why: Hurting yourself is reflexive farsi male, with essere.
dire takes di before the infinitive.
The pronoun goes before devo or on the end of the infinitive.
With several things that hurt, the verb is plural.
An appointment is something you take (prendere) or fix (fissare).

units.culture: Once you're registered with the national health service you choose a medico di base at the local health office (ASL), and visits to them are free; at night, at weekends and on holidays you call the guardia medica (116117 in many regions) instead, and the pronto soccorso is for real emergencies.
recycles: a1-14: ho mal di …, mi fa male …, ho la febbre, the pharmacy
a1-08: days and times (il martedì, alle dieci)
units.evidence: In a doctor or pharmacy scene the learner books a time, says what's wrong and for how long with da + present, uses farsi male correctly, follows the doctor's Lei instructions, and asks Ogni quanto devo prenderlo? or Serve la ricetta?
sources: P2 U6 (the flu; phone call to the family doctor; moved down from the B1/B2 hinge)
P3 U17 (medico di base)
P1B U7, U9 (febbre, raffreddore)
Proudfoot U9 (Lei imperatives), U20 (dire a qualcuno di)
gap: P1B §5.5, Proudfoot §5.5

units.title: Problems, complaints and lost things
units.can_do: Explain politely that something is wrong (a bill, an order, a repair, a purchase), ask for it to be put right, and report something lost or stolen.

frames.it: Scusi, nel conto c'è un errore: abbiamo preso due caffè, non tre.
frames.en: Excuse me, there's a mistake in the bill: we had two coffees, not three.

frames.it: Ho ordinato un'acqua frizzante, non naturale.
frames.en: I ordered sparkling water, not still.

frames.it: Potrebbe controllare, per favore?
frames.en: Could you check, please?

frames.it: Il riscaldamento non funziona da ieri sera.
frames.en: The heating hasn't worked since last night.

frames.it: Quando può venire l'idraulico?
frames.en: When can the plumber come?

frames.it: L'ho comprata ieri e non funziona: posso cambiarla?
frames.en: I bought it yesterday and it doesn't work: can I exchange it?

frames.it: Mi hanno rubato il portafoglio sull'autobus.
frames.en: My wallet was stolen on the bus.

frames.it: Dove posso fare la denuncia?
frames.en: Where can I report it to the police?

model_exchanges.situation: a wrong bill at a bar table (Lei)

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Scusi, nel conto c'è un errore: abbiamo preso due caffè, non tre.
lines.en: Excuse me, there's a mistake in the bill: we had two coffees, not three.

lines.speaker: cameriere
lines.it: Davvero? Mi faccia vedere…
lines.en: Really? Let me see…

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: E poi ho ordinato un'acqua frizzante, ma era naturale.
lines.en: And I ordered sparkling water, but it was still.

lines.speaker: cameriere
lines.it: Ha ragione, mi scusi. Le porto subito il conto giusto.
lines.en: You're right, I'm sorry. I'll bring you the right bill straight away.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Grazie, non c'è problema.
lines.en: Thanks, no problem.

model_exchanges.situation: calling the landlady about the heating (Lei)

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Signora, buongiorno. Scusi il disturbo, ma il riscaldamento non funziona da ieri sera.
lines.en: Good morning, signora. Sorry to bother you, but the heating hasn't worked since last night.

lines.speaker: padrona di casa
lines.it: Oddio! Ha provato a spegnere e riaccendere la caldaia?
lines.en: Oh dear! Have you tried turning the boiler off and on again?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Sì, ma non si accende. In casa fa molto freddo.
lines.en: Yes, but it won't come on. It's very cold in the flat.

lines.speaker: padrona di casa
lines.it: Chiamo subito l'idraulico.
lines.en: I'll call the plumber right away.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Grazie. Quando può venire?
lines.en: Thank you. When can he come?

lines.speaker: padrona di casa
lines.it: Domani mattina, credo. Le faccio sapere.
lines.en: Tomorrow morning, I think. I'll let you know.

model_exchanges.situation: reporting a theft at the carabinieri (Lei)

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Buongiorno, mi hanno rubato il portafoglio sull'autobus.
lines.en: Good morning, my wallet was stolen on the bus.

lines.speaker: carabiniere
lines.it: Quando è successo?
lines.en: When did it happen?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Stamattina, verso le nove. C'era tantissima gente e non ho visto niente.
lines.en: This morning, around nine. It was very crowded and I didn't see anything.

lines.speaker: carabiniere
lines.it: Cosa c'era nel portafoglio?
lines.en: What was in the wallet?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: La carta d'identità, la carta di credito e cinquanta euro.
lines.en: My ID card, my credit card and fifty euros.

lines.speaker: carabiniere
lines.it: Va bene, facciamo la denuncia. Ha un altro documento?
lines.en: All right, let's make the report. Do you have another ID?

grammar.point: Passato prossimo and imperfetto together in an explanation
grammar.explain: Say what happened with the passato prossimo and what the situation was with the imperfetto.

examples.it: Ho ordinato un'acqua frizzante, ma era naturale.
examples.en: I ordered sparkling water, but it was still.

examples.it: C'era tanta gente e non ho visto niente.
examples.en: There were lots of people and I didn't see anything.

grammar.trap: Background (c'era, era) stays imperfetto even in a complaint; the action you took (ho ordinato) is passato prossimo.

grammar.point: mi hanno rubato: 'they' instead of a passive
grammar.explain: Where English says 'my wallet was stolen', Italian says 'they stole me the wallet': mi hanno rubato il portafoglio.

examples.en: My bike's been stolen.
Someone broke into our car.

grammar.trap: sono stato rubato means 'I was stolen'. Use mi hanno rubato + the thing, with no possessive (il portafoglio, not il mio portafoglio).

grammar.explain: A problem that started and is still going on takes the present + da.

examples.it: Il riscaldamento non funziona da ieri sera.
examples.en: The heating hasn't worked since last night.

examples.it: Non c'è acqua calda da due giorni.
examples.en: There's been no hot water for two days.

grammar.trap: non ha funzionato da ieri is wrong; English present perfect becomes the Italian present.

grammar.point: Polite fixes: potrebbe …? and pronouns with posso
grammar.explain: Ask for a fix with the conditional, and refer to the item with lo / la on posso or the infinitive.

examples.en: Could you check, please?
Can I exchange it?

grammar.trap: Keep the pronoun's gender: la lampada → cambiarla; il telefono → cambiarlo.

vocabulary.en: out of order, faulty (also il guasto = fault)
to switch on (non si accende = it won't come on)
bother (Scusi il disturbo = sorry to bother you)

pronunciation: Hold the double consonants: errore and carrozzeria have a long rolled rr, and rotto (broken) a long tt.
Stress idraulico on the second syllable: i-DRAU-li-co.

common_errors.why: 'My wallet was stolen' = they stole me the wallet.

common_errors.wrong: Mi hanno rubato il mio portafoglio.
common_errors.why: mi already says whose it is.

common_errors.wrong: Il riscaldamento non ha funzionato da ieri.
common_errors.right: Il riscaldamento non funziona da ieri.
common_errors.why: Still broken: present + da.
Sparkling water is frizzante (or gassata); still is naturale.

common_errors.right: C'è uno sbaglio. / C'è un errore.
common_errors.why: s + consonant takes uno.

common_errors.wrong: Questo è rotto. (for a TV that won't switch on)
common_errors.why: rotto is physically broken; for a machine that doesn't work, say non funziona.

units.culture: To replace stolen documents or cards you need a copy of the denuncia, made at any carabinieri station or police office; it's free, takes a while, and you should keep the copy.
recycles: a2-04: imperfetto vs passato prossimo (c'era, ho ordinato)
a1-10: non funziona, non c'è acqua calda
units.evidence: The learner states a problem politely (Scusi, …), explains what happened with the right past tenses, asks for a fix with potrebbe or posso + pronoun, and reports a theft with mi hanno rubato + object.
sources: P1a U4 video (wrong order: Che confusione!)
P1B U11 C (the TV wouldn't turn on: non si accendeva, c'era un guasto), U9 (pickpocket description)
P2 U3 (complaint story), U10 (furti, denuncia)

units.title: Phone, post and getting set up
units.can_do: Handle a phone call to a business, spell your name, get a SIM card, send or collect a parcel, and ask what documents an office needs.
situations: getting a phone number in the first week
phoning an office or a business
asking what to bring for the codice fiscale

frames.it: Pronto, buongiorno, chiamo per prendere un appuntamento.
frames.en: Hello, good morning, I'm calling to make an appointment.

frames.it: Potrei parlare con la signora Bianchi?
frames.en: Could I speak to Mrs Bianchi?

frames.it: Mi dispiace, è uscita. Vuole lasciare un messaggio?
frames.en: Sorry, she's gone out. Would you like to leave a message?

frames.it: La richiamo più tardi.
frames.en: I'll call you back later.
frames.note: La = you (Lei); to a friend, ti richiamo.

frames.it: Il cognome è …: M come Milano, A come Ancona …
frames.en: The surname is …: M as in Milano, A as in Ancona …
frames.note: Spell your own name with Italian city names.

frames.it: Vorrei una SIM con tanti giga al mese.
frames.en: I'd like a SIM with plenty of data a month.

frames.it: Vorrei spedire questo pacco negli Stati Uniti.
frames.en: I'd like to send this parcel to the United States.

frames.it: Devo ritirare una raccomandata.
frames.en: I have to collect a registered letter.

frames.it: Che documenti servono?
frames.en: What documents are needed?

model_exchanges.situation: phoning an office (Lei)

lines.speaker: impiegata
lines.it: Pronto?
lines.en: Hello?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Pronto, buongiorno. Potrei parlare con la signora Bianchi?
lines.en: Hello, good morning. Could I speak to Mrs Bianchi?

lines.speaker: impiegata
lines.it: Mi dispiace, è uscita. Vuole lasciare un messaggio?
lines.en: Sorry, she's gone out. Would you like to leave a message?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: No, grazie, la richiamo più tardi. A che ora torna?
lines.en: No thanks, I'll call her back later. What time will she be back?

lines.speaker: impiegata
lines.it: Verso le tre. Chi la cerca?
lines.en: Around three. Who shall I say called?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Sono …, il cognome è …: M come Milano, A come Ancona …
lines.en: This is …, the surname is …: M as in Milano, A as in Ancona …

lines.speaker: impiegata
lines.it: Perfetto, le dico che ha chiamato.
lines.en: Perfect, I'll tell her you called.

model_exchanges.situation: buying a SIM in a phone shop (Lei)

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Buongiorno, vorrei una SIM con tanti giga al mese.
lines.en: Good morning, I'd like a SIM with plenty of data a month.

lines.speaker: commesso
lines.it: Certo. Abbiamo un'offerta con cento giga a dieci euro al mese.
lines.en: Of course. We have a deal with a hundred gigabytes for ten euros a month.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Va bene. Che documenti servono?
lines.en: Fine. What documents are needed?

lines.speaker: commesso
lines.it: Il passaporto e il codice fiscale.
lines.en: Your passport and your tax code.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Ecco. E la ricarica, come si fa?
lines.en: Here you are. And how do I top up?

lines.speaker: commesso
lines.it: Con l'app, o in tabaccheria.
lines.en: With the app, or at a tobacconist's.

model_exchanges.situation: at the post office counter (Lei)

lines.speaker: impiegato
lines.it: Buongiorno, prego.
lines.en: Good morning, go ahead.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Buongiorno. Devo ritirare una raccomandata: ecco l'avviso.
lines.en: Good morning. I have to collect a registered letter: here's the notice.

lines.speaker: impiegato
lines.it: Mi serve anche un documento.
lines.en: I need some ID as well.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Ecco il passaporto. E vorrei spedire questo pacco negli Stati Uniti.
lines.en: Here's my passport. And I'd like to send this parcel to the United States.

lines.speaker: impiegato
lines.it: Deve compilare questo modulo. Ci vogliono circa dieci giorni.
lines.en: You need to fill in this form. It takes about ten days.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Va bene, grazie.
lines.en: OK, thank you.

grammar.explain: Answer with Pronto?, say who you are with sono …, give your reason with chiamo per …, and use La / Le for 'you' with Lei.

examples.it: Pronto? — Buongiorno, sono … Chiamo per l'appuntamento.
examples.en: Hello? — Good morning, this is … I'm calling about the appointment.
Who's speaking?

examples.it: La richiamo domani. / Ti richiamo dopo.
examples.en: I'll call you back tomorrow (Lei). / I'll call you back later (tu).

grammar.trap: 'This is John' on the phone is sono John, not questo è John.

grammar.explain: potrei ('could I') is the polite way to ask to do something.

examples.en: Could I speak to the manager?
Could I have a form?

grammar.trap: It's parlare con someone, not parlare a, when you mean 'speak to' on the phone.

grammar.explain: With servire the things needed are the subject, so the verb agrees with them; mi serve = I need.

examples.en: What documents are needed?
You need a passport photo.
I need a pen.

grammar.trap: Che documenti serve? is wrong: documenti is plural, so servono.

grammar.explain: Italians spell over the phone with cities: A come Ancona, B come Bologna, C come Como …; letters not in Italian have their own names.

examples.it: M come Milano, R come Roma, T come Torino
examples.en: M as in Milano, R as in Roma, T as in Torino

examples.it: doppia vu, ipsilon, kappa, i lunga, ics
examples.en: W, Y, K, J, X
with a double L

grammar.trap: Say the letter names the Italian way: h is acca, q is cu, and double letters are doppia (doppia esse).

grammar.point: in with countries: the article with plural ones
grammar.explain: Countries take in, but plural ones also take the article: negli Stati Uniti, nei Paesi Bassi; cities take a.

examples.en: I'm sending a parcel to England.

examples.it: Mio figlio vive negli Stati Uniti.
examples.en: My son lives in the United States.
I'm sending it to London.

grammar.trap: in Stati Uniti and a America are wrong: negli Stati Uniti.

vocabulary.en: to be needed (mi serve = I need)

pronunciation: Letter names for spelling: acca (h), cu (q), doppia vu (w), ipsilon (y), i lunga (j), kappa (k), ics (x); a double letter is doppia: doppia esse.
raccomandata and francobollo have held double consonants: rac-co-man-DA-ta, fran-co-BOL-lo.

common_errors.why: On the phone you say 'I am', not 'this is'.
servire agrees with the plural thing needed.

common_errors.wrong: Vorrei spedire un pacco in Stati Uniti.
common_errors.right: Vorrei spedire un pacco negli Stati Uniti.
common_errors.why: A plural country takes the article.
With Lei, 'you' is La.

common_errors.right: Ho bisogno di una SIM. / Mi serve una SIM.
common_errors.why: avere bisogno takes di.

common_errors.wrong: Posso parlare a la signora Bianchi?
common_errors.right: Potrei parlare con la signora Bianchi?
common_errors.why: On the phone you speak con someone.

units.culture: If you miss a registered letter, the postman leaves an avviso in your letterbox; take it with your ID to the post office named on it within the days shown. Buying a SIM needs your passport and codice fiscale, so get the codice fiscale first.
recycles: a1-08: times (verso le tre, più tardi)
a2-07: indirect and direct pronouns (la richiamo, le dico)

units.title: Offices and documents: codice fiscale, residence, permit
units.can_do: Deal with an Italian office: ask what's needed, understand formal instructions, fill in a form, and come back with the right papers.
functions: ask about progress on an application
situations: registering residence at the comune's anagrafe
getting a codice fiscale at the Agenzia delle Entrate
a residence-permit appointment at the questura
a queue with numbered tickets at an office counter
phoning an office to chase an application

frames.it: Buongiorno, devo richiedere la residenza: cosa devo portare?
frames.en: Good morning, I need to apply for residence: what do I need to bring?

frames.it: Deve compilare questo modulo e firmare qui in fondo.
frames.en: You need to fill in this form and sign here at the bottom.

frames.it: Serve una marca da bollo da sedici euro.
frames.en: You need a sixteen-euro revenue stamp.
frames.note: A marca da bollo is a tax stamp you buy at a tabaccheria and stick on the form.

frames.it: Bisogna prendere l'appuntamento online?
frames.en: Do you have to book the appointment online?

frames.it: Mi scusi, devo tornare con l'originale o basta la fotocopia?
frames.en: Sorry, do I come back with the original or is a photocopy enough?

frames.it: Quanto tempo ci vuole?
frames.en: How long does it take?

frames.it: A che punto è la mia pratica?
frames.en: How far along is my application?

frames.it: Torni con la ricevuta fra trenta giorni.
frames.en: Come back with the receipt in thirty days.
frames.note: Torni is a polite Lei command; you'll learn to make these in b1-09.

frames.it: Per l'anagrafe, che numero devo prendere?
frames.en: For the registry office, which ticket do I take?

grammar.explain: Bisogna never changes and is followed by a verb, while serve and servono agree with the thing that's needed, which is their subject.

examples.en: You have to take a ticket.
You need a passport photo.
You need two passport photos.

grammar.trap: Bisogna can't take a noun: say serve un documento or c'è bisogno di un documento, never bisogna un documento.

grammar.explain: Basta means 'X is enough' or 'all you have to do is', and like serve it agrees with a plural noun (bastano).

examples.en: A photocopy is enough.
You just need to sign here.
Two lines are enough.

grammar.trap: On its own, Basta! means 'Stop it!' or 'That's enough!', so don't use it alone as an answer to an official.

grammar.point: ci vuole / ci vogliono for time and things needed
grammar.explain: Ci vuole goes with one thing or amount and ci vogliono with a plural, to say how long something takes or what it needs.

examples.en: How long does it take?
It takes a month.
It takes two weeks.

grammar.trap: It must agree: ci vogliono due settimane, not ci vuole due settimane. For the time a particular person takes, use metterci (ci ho messo un'ora).

grammar.explain: Officials give instructions with polite Lei commands, which end in -i for -are verbs and in -a for -ere and -ire verbs.

examples.en: Fill in the form.
Sign here.
Take a ticket and wait.

grammar.trap: Firmi looks like 'you sign' but it's a command; the endings look swapped compared with the tu command (firma, prendi).

grammar.point: question words in full: quale, quanto tempo, come mai, a che punto
grammar.explain: Quale asks 'which' from a set, quanto tempo asks 'how long', come mai asks 'how come' and a che punto asks 'how far along'.

examples.en: Which form do I have to fill in?
Which documents are needed?

examples.it: Come mai ci vuole così tanto?
examples.en: How come it takes so long?

grammar.trap: Qual è is written without an apostrophe, and 'what documents?' from a list is quali documenti, not cosa documenti.

pronunciation: The z in residenza and scadenza is a 'ts' sound (re-si-DEN-tsa), and every -zione word, like autocertificazione, ends -TSIO-ne.
Modulo, pratica and anagrafe are stressed on the third syllable from the end: MO-du-lo, PRA-ti-ca, a-NA-gra-fe. With stress on the wrong syllable, a clerk may not recognise the word.

common_errors.why: Bisogna only takes a verb; for a thing use serve / servono or c'è bisogno di.
Ci vuole agrees with what's needed, and due settimane is plural.

common_errors.wrong: Ho bisogno una marca da bollo.
common_errors.right: Ho bisogno di una marca da bollo.
common_errors.why: Avere bisogno always takes di.
Qual è is a truncated form, not an elision, so it takes no apostrophe (quale è is possible but stiff).

units.culture: Italian offices usually want the original and a photocopy of every document, a marca da bollo bought beforehand at a tabaccheria, and often an appointment booked online. Each comune's website lists exactly what to bring, and the list can differ from one comune to the next, so check before you queue.
recycles: a2-05: Ho il quarantasette. Tocca a me?
units.evidence: At a counter the learner asks what to bring and whether a photocopy will do, follows a Lei instruction (compili, firmi, torni) without asking for English, and later asks how far along the application is and how long it takes, with ci vuole / ci vogliono agreeing correctly.

grammar.point: me lo, te la, ce li, ve le: the order and the vowel change
grammar.explain: When two object pronouns meet, the 'to whom' pronoun comes first and mi, ti, ci, vi change to me, te, ce, ve before lo, la, li, le or ne.

examples.en: Will you give it to me?
I'll bring it to you tomorrow.
The neighbour is lending them to us.

grammar.trap: Never mi lo or lo mi: always 'to whom' + 'what', with me, te, ce, ve.

grammar.explain: Gli, le and Le all become glie- and join the next pronoun as one word.

examples.en: I'll tell him / her / you.
I'll wrap it for you right away.
I'll bring him a glass (of it).

grammar.trap: English separates 'to him' and 'to her'; Italian uses the same glielo for him, her, you (Lei) and them, so context tells you who.

grammar.explain: Ne ('of it, of them') combines the same way, so 'give me some' or 'give me two' becomes me ne dà.

examples.it: Me ne dà ancora un etto?
examples.en: Could you give me another hundred grams?
I'll bring you two (of them).
Is there any left?

grammar.trap: With a number or amount, ne is needed: me ne dà due, not mi dà due.

grammar.point: in the passato prossimo, with agreement
grammar.explain: Lo and la shorten to l' before forms of avere, and the past participle agrees with the thing (lo, la, li, le), not with the person.

examples.it: Te l'ho data ieri, la chiave.
examples.en: I gave you the key yesterday.
I've already sent it to him.
You lent them to me.

grammar.trap: Gliel'ho data means 'I gave it (the key, feminine) to him': the -a follows la chiave, not the man.

grammar.point: with modal verbs and the infinitive
grammar.explain: With potere, dovere or volere the pair goes before the modal or is attached to the end of the infinitive as one word.

examples.it: Te lo posso portare. / Posso portartelo.
examples.en: I can bring it to you.

examples.it: Me lo può spiegare? / Può spiegarmelo?
examples.en: Could you explain it to me?
I can order it for you.

grammar.trap: Never split the pair or put it in the middle: not posso te lo portare.

grammar.explain: Reflexives like dimenticarsi and andarsene combine with ne in the same way: me ne, te ne, se ne.

examples.en: I forgot about it.
Did you remember (it)?
He left early.

grammar.trap: English 'I forgot about it' has no pronoun before the verb; Italian needs me ne, because ne replaces 'di + the thing'.

vocabulary.en: it to him / her / you / them

pronunciation: The gl in glielo, gliela and gliel'ho is the soft 'lli' sound of 'million', said with the tongue flat against the palate, never a hard g + l.
A combined pronoun has no stress of its own and leans on the verb: me lo DÀ, te lo POR-to, glie-lo DI-co.

common_errors.why: Before lo, la, li, le or ne, mi becomes me.
The 'to whom' pronoun comes first, and gli joins lo as one word.
Glielo is one word, and lo shortens to l' before ho.
The participle agrees with la chiave, which is feminine.

common_errors.right: Me ne dà due, per favore.
common_errors.why: With a number you need ne ('of them'), and mi becomes me before it.

units.culture: Gift wrapping is free and expected: in almost any shop you can say 'È un regalo' and they'll make a pacchetto, often with ribbon, at no charge. Before Christmas some shops even have a separate queue just for wrapping.
