grammar.explain: Take the stem and add -assi, -essi or -issi (parlassi, prendessi, partissi), with the same endings for every verb (-ssi, -ssi, -sse, -ssimo, -ste, -ssero); the key irregulars are fossi, dessi, stessi, facessi, dicessi, bevessi.

examples.en: if I had time
if I were you
if we could

grammar.trap: Keep the double s: avessi, potessi, not avesi.

grammar.point: se + congiuntivo imperfetto, then the conditional
grammar.explain: For something unreal or unlikely now, put the se-clause in the imperfect subjunctive and the result in the present conditional.

examples.it: Se avessi più tempo, studierei di più.
examples.en: If I had more time, I'd study more.

examples.it: Se abitassi in campagna, avrei un orto.
examples.en: If I lived in the country, I'd have a vegetable garden.
What would you do if you won?

grammar.trap: Never the conditional after se: se avessi, not se avrei, even though English 'would' tempts you.

grammar.point: real or unreal: se + present vs se + imperfect subjunctive
grammar.explain: If the condition can easily happen, use the present (se piove, resto a casa); if it's imagined or unlikely, use the imperfect subjunctive (se piovesse, resterei a casa).

examples.en: If I have time, I'll come.
If I had time, I'd come.

grammar.trap: The choice is about how likely you think it is, not about grammar rules: both are correct, but they mean different things.

grammar.explain: To say what you'd like someone else to do, use vorrei che + the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.it: Vorrei che tu venissi con me.
examples.en: I'd like you to come with me.

examples.it: Vorrei che fosse tutto più semplice.
examples.en: I wish it were all simpler.

grammar.trap: After vorrei che the verb is the imperfect subjunctive, not the present: vorrei che tu venissi, not che tu venga.

grammar.explain: Magari! on its own means 'if only!', and magari + imperfect subjunctive means 'I wish...'.

examples.en: Will we win? — If only!
If only I had more time!

grammar.trap: With the indicative, magari just means 'maybe' (magari vengo domani = maybe I'll come tomorrow).

pronunciation: Hold the double s of the imperfect subjunctive: a-VES-si, FOS-si, po-TES-si. A single s turns it into a different, wrong form.
The conditional 'we' form has a double m, the future a single one: fa-REM-mo (we'd do) vs fa-RE-mo (we'll do). Hold the mm when you mean 'would'.

common_errors.why: The se-clause takes the imperfect subjunctive, never the conditional.

common_errors.wrong: Se fossi in te, chiedo alla padrona.
common_errors.right: Se fossi in te, chiederei alla padrona.
common_errors.why: An unreal condition needs the conditional in the result.

common_errors.wrong: Vorrei che tu vieni con me.
common_errors.right: Vorrei che tu venissi con me.
common_errors.why: Vorrei che takes the imperfect subjunctive.
'If I were you' is the fixed phrase se fossi in te.

common_errors.wrong: Se sarei ricco, comprerei una casa.
common_errors.right: Se fossi ricco, comprerei una casa.
common_errors.why: After se: fossi, not sarei.

units.culture: Italians play the lotteries a lot: a big Superenalotto jackpot is national news, and 'cosa faresti se vincessi?' is a classic bar conversation. The other classic dream is the orto. Many town-dwellers rent a small vegetable plot from the comune (an orto urbano) or tend one at a relative's house in the country.
recycles: a2-11: condizionale presente (vorrei, dovresti, al posto tuo prenderei)
a2-09: se + present for real conditions
b1-08: subjunctive after conjunctions and impersonals
b1-04: la padrona di casa, l'affitto, il contratto
units.evidence: In a 'what would you do if...' conversation, the learner builds several unreal conditions with se + imperfect subjunctive and the conditional, never says se + conditional, gives at least one piece of 'se fossi in te' advice, and uses magari or vorrei che naturally.
sources: P2 U8 (periodo ipotetico type 2; forms from U7)
P2 U7 (congiuntivo imperfetto forms; vorrei che glielo dessi tu; magari)
Proudfoot U20 (imperfect subjunctive, vorrei che), U22 (conditions; se fossi in te)
EGSI ch.29 (never se + conditional)

units.title: Places with a past: the history you hear
units.can_do: Follow what a guide or custodian tells you about a place's history, and ask about it.
situations: visiting a church with a custodian
a guided tour of an old town
an older local telling a legend

frames.it: Quando è stata costruita questa chiesa?
frames.en: When was this church built?

frames.it: Fu costruita nel Trecento e restaurata nell'Ottocento.
frames.en: It was built in the 1300s and restored in the 1800s.

frames.it: Chi ha dipinto questo affresco?
frames.en: Who painted this fresco?

frames.it: Michelangelo nacque a Caprese nel 1475.
frames.en: Michelangelo was born in Caprese in 1475.

frames.it: C'era una volta...
frames.en: Once upon a time...

frames.it: Si possono fare foto?
frames.en: Can you take photos?

frames.it: È vietato entrare con le spalle scoperte.
frames.en: Entry with bare shoulders is not allowed.

frames.it: Il Cinquecento è il sedicesimo secolo, vero?
frames.en: The Cinquecento is the sixteenth century, right?

model_exchanges.situation: visiting a church with the custodian

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Scusi, quando è stata costruita questa chiesa?
lines.en: Excuse me, when was this church built?

lines.speaker: custode
lines.it: Fu costruita nel Trecento e restaurata nell'Ottocento.
lines.en: It was built in the 1300s and restored in the 1800s.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: E chi ha dipinto questo affresco?
lines.en: And who painted this fresco?

lines.speaker: custode
lines.it: Un allievo di Giotto. Per accendere la luce, metta un euro qui.
lines.en: A pupil of Giotto. To turn the light on, put a euro in here.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Si possono fare foto?
lines.en: Can you take photos?

lines.speaker: custode
lines.it: Sì, ma senza flash. E durante la messa le visite non sono permesse.
lines.en: Yes, but no flash. And visits aren't allowed during mass.

model_exchanges.situation: a guided walk round the old town

lines.speaker: guida
lines.it: Questa piazza nacque nel Medioevo come mercato. Nel Cinquecento una famiglia di banchieri la trasformò.
lines.en: This square began in the Middle Ages as a market. In the 1500s a family of bankers transformed it.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Scusi, il Cinquecento è il sedicesimo secolo, vero?
lines.en: Sorry, the Cinquecento is the sixteenth century, right?

lines.speaker: guida
lines.it: Esatto: sono gli anni dal 1500 al 1599.
lines.en: Exactly: it's the years from 1500 to 1599.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: E di chi era quel palazzo?
lines.en: And whose was that palazzo?

lines.speaker: guida
lines.it: Di un ricco mercante. Morì senza figli e lasciò tutto alla città.
lines.en: A rich merchant's. He died without children and left everything to the town.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Che storia!
lines.en: What a story!

model_exchanges.situation: an older local tells a legend

lines.speaker: anziano
lines.it: Conosce la leggenda del ponte?
lines.en: Do you know the legend of the bridge?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: No, me la racconta?
lines.en: No, will you tell me?

lines.speaker: anziano
lines.it: C'era una volta un costruttore che non riusciva a finire il ponte. Allora fece un patto con il diavolo.
lines.en: Once upon a time there was a builder who couldn't finish the bridge. So he made a pact with the devil.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: E cos'è successo?
lines.en: And what happened?

lines.speaker: anziano
lines.it: Il diavolo finì il ponte in una notte, ma in cambio voleva l'anima del primo passante. La mattina dopo il costruttore ci fece passare un cane!
lines.en: The devil finished the bridge in one night, but in exchange he wanted the soul of the first person to cross. The next morning the builder sent a dog across!

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Ma dai! Povero cane!
lines.en: No way! Poor dog!

grammar.explain: Guides, labels and books tell history in the passato remoto; you mainly need to recognise the 'he / she / it' form, which ends in a stressed vowel (costruì, morì, trasformò) or is a short irregular form (fu, ebbe, fece, nacque, disse, dipinse), and the 'they' form in -rono (costruirono, vissero).

examples.en: It was built in the 1300s.

examples.it: Michelangelo nacque nel 1475 e morì nel 1564.
examples.en: Michelangelo was born in 1475 and died in 1564.
Giotto painted the chapel.

grammar.trap: Costruì (built) is not the future costruirà; and when you speak you can keep using the passato prossimo: chi ha dipinto questo affresco?

grammar.point: 'was built', 'was painted': essere + participle (as a chunk)
grammar.explain: For 'was built' or 'was painted', Italian uses essere plus a past participle that agrees with the building or picture, and introduces the person who did it with da.

examples.it: Quando è stata costruita la chiesa?
examples.en: When was the church built?

examples.it: Il quadro è stato dipinto da Caravaggio.
examples.en: The painting was painted by Caravaggio.
It was restored in the 1800s.

grammar.trap: 'By' is da, not per: dipinto da Giotto. And the participle agrees: la chiesa è stata costruita.

grammar.point: centuries: il Trecento, il Quattrocento, il Cinquecento
grammar.explain: Italians name the centuries after 1200 by their hundreds: il Duecento = the 1200s, il Trecento = the 1300s, il Quattrocento = the 1400s, il Cinquecento = the 1500s, up to il Novecento = the 1900s.

examples.en: a fourteenth-century fresco
in the 1400s (the fifteenth century)
in the sixteenth century

grammar.trap: Il Trecento is the 1300s, not the 300s, and it's the fourteenth century, not the 'thirteenth'.

grammar.point: si può / si possono for what's allowed
grammar.explain: Ask what's allowed with si può + infinitive; when a plural noun follows, the verb is si possono.

examples.en: Can you go in?
Can you take photos?

examples.it: Non si può usare il flash.
examples.en: You can't use the flash.

grammar.trap: With a plural object the verb is plural: si possono fare foto. You'll often hear si può fare foto in speech.

pronunciation: Final stress carries the meaning in the passato remoto: parlò (he spoke) vs parlo (I speak), morì (he died). Lean on the last vowel: mo-RÌ, co-stru-Ì, tra-sfor-MÒ.
Hold the double consonants in affresco (af-FRES-co) and cappella (cap-PEL-la). In Trecento and Cinquecento, c before e is a 'ch' sound: tre-CHEN-to, cin-que-CHEN-to.

common_errors.why: The person who did it is introduced by da.

common_errors.wrong: La chiesa è stato costruito nel Trecento.
common_errors.right: La chiesa è stata costruita nel Trecento.
common_errors.why: Both stata and costruita agree with la chiesa.
Trecento already names the century; don't add secolo.
The participle of nascere is nato.

units.culture: Churches are working places of worship. Cover shoulders and knees, keep your voice down, and don't wander round during mass unless you're attending. The lights for frescoes in side chapels are often coin-operated, and many churches close over lunch.
recycles: b1-06: narrative tenses and the trapassato
b1-09: Lei commands (metta un euro qui) and polite questions
b1-07: penso che sia... about dates and artists
units.evidence: On a visit or a tour, the learner follows a guide's passato remoto narration (fu, nacque, morì, costruirono) well enough to ask a relevant follow-up question, asks when something was built or who painted it, places a century correctly (il Quattrocento = the 1400s), and asks what's allowed with si può / si possono.
sources: P2 U4 (passato remoto, regular and irregular; history, legends and fairy tales: C'era una volta...; centuries and Roman numerals)
P2 U9 (art, museums, restoration; the passive with essere)
Proudfoot U11 (passato remoto for recognition only), U15 (the passive)
P3 U18, U27 (history and art)
EGSI ch.31 ('by' = da)

units.title: Expectations and surprises
units.can_do: Say what you used to think about life here and how it turned out, using the past forms of the subjunctive.
functions: express surprise at how things turned out
situations: looking back on your first months with a friend
running into someone you thought had left town
telling a neighbour what surprised you

frames.it: Credevo che fosse più facile trovare casa.
frames.en: I thought finding a place would be easier.

frames.it: Non pensavo che gli uffici chiudessero così presto.
frames.en: I didn't think offices closed so early.

frames.it: Pensavo che fossi già partito!
frames.en: I thought you'd already left!
frames.note: partito / partita agrees with the person you're talking to.

frames.it: Avevo l'impressione che tutti si conoscessero.
frames.en: I had the impression that everyone knew each other.

frames.it: Mi sembrava che parlassero troppo in fretta.
frames.en: It seemed to me they spoke too fast.

frames.it: Non mi aspettavo che fossero così gentili.
frames.en: I didn't expect them to be so kind.

frames.it: Era normale che all'inizio non capissi niente.
frames.en: It was normal that I didn't understand anything at first.

frames.it: Sapevo che era difficile, ma non così tanto.
frames.en: I knew it was hard, but not this hard.
frames.note: sapere states a fact, so the indicative follows.

frames.it: Ti facevo più tranquillo!
frames.en: I took you for a calmer type!
frames.note: Colloquial for 'credevo che tu fossi più tranquillo'.

model_exchanges.situation: A friend asks how the first months went

lines.speaker: friend
lines.it: Allora, com'è stato l'inizio qui?
lines.en: So, how was it at the start here?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Più difficile di quanto pensassi. Credevo che fosse facile trovare casa.
lines.en: Harder than I thought. I thought finding a place would be easy.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.it: E invece?
lines.en: And it wasn't?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Invece ci ho messo tre mesi! E non pensavo che gli uffici chiudessero all'una.
lines.en: It took me three months! And I didn't think offices closed at one.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.it: Eh, benvenuto in Italia. E con la lingua?
lines.en: Well, welcome to Italy. And the language?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: All'inizio mi sembrava che tutti parlassero troppo in fretta. Adesso va meglio.
lines.en: At first it seemed to me everyone spoke too fast. It's better now.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.it: Si vede! Parli benissimo.
lines.en: It shows! You speak really well.

model_exchanges.situation: Running into a neighbour who thought you'd gone

lines.speaker: neighbour
lines.it: Oh, ma sei ancora qui? Pensavo che fossi già partito per le vacanze!
lines.en: Oh, you're still here? I thought you'd already left on holiday!

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: No, parto domani. Credevi che me ne fossi andato senza salutare?
lines.en: No, I leave tomorrow. Did you think I'd gone without saying goodbye?

lines.speaker: neighbour
lines.it: Be', non ti vedevo da giorni.
lines.en: Well, I hadn't seen you for days.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Ho lavorato tanto. Ma non immaginavo che qualcuno se ne accorgesse!
lines.en: I've been working a lot. But I didn't imagine anyone would notice!

lines.speaker: neighbour
lines.it: Qui ci accorgiamo di tutto, caro mio!
lines.en: Round here we notice everything, my friend!

model_exchanges.situation: Comparing stereotypes with reality

lines.speaker: A
lines.it: Prima di venire, cosa pensavi degli italiani?
lines.en: Before you came, what did you think of Italians?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Pensavo che mangiassero la pasta tutti i giorni.
lines.en: I thought they ate pasta every day.

lines.speaker: A
lines.it: E non è vero?
lines.en: And isn't it true?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Be', è vero! Ma non pensavo che cenassero così tardi.
lines.en: Well, it is! But I didn't think people had dinner so late.

lines.speaker: A
lines.it: E i gesti?
lines.en: And the gestures?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Credevo che fosse uno stereotipo, invece li fate davvero!
lines.en: I thought it was a stereotype, but you really do them!

grammar.point: congiuntivo imperfetto after a past main verb
grammar.explain: When the verb of thinking, feeling or seeming is in the past (credevo, pensavo, mi sembrava, era normale), the verb after che goes into the imperfect subjunctive: -assi, -essi, -issi, with fossi, avessi, facessi, dessi, stessi, dicessi.

examples.en: I thought it was closed.
I thought you spoke English.
It seemed to me he was in a hurry.

grammar.trap: English 'I thought it was' gives no signal, so learners say 'credevo che era'. You'll hear that in casual speech, but say 'credevo che fosse'.

grammar.explain: If the thing you thought about had already happened before that past moment, use fossi / avessi + past participle.

examples.en: I thought you'd already left.
I thought they'd already closed.

examples.it: Avevo l'impressione che ci fossimo persi.
examples.en: I had the feeling we'd got lost.

grammar.trap: Choose essere or avere exactly as in the passato prossimo, and with essere make the participle agree (fossi partita, fossero arrivati).

grammar.explain: A present main verb takes the present subjunctive and a past main verb takes the imperfect (same time) or pluperfect (earlier) subjunctive.

examples.it: Penso che venga. / Pensavo che venisse.
examples.en: I think he's coming. / I thought he was coming.

examples.it: Penso che sia venuto. / Pensavo che fosse venuto.
examples.en: I think he came. / I thought he had come.

grammar.trap: Mixing the two: 'pensavo che venga' sounds wrong to an Italian ear.

grammar.explain: After sapevo che, ero sicuro che, ho scoperto che the indicative stays, while non mi aspettavo che takes the subjunctive and, with the same subject, di + infinitive.

examples.en: I knew it was hard.

examples.it: Ho scoperto che il martedì è chiuso.
examples.en: I found out it's closed on Tuesdays.

examples.it: Non mi aspettavo di trovare lavoro così presto.
examples.en: I didn't expect to find work so soon.

grammar.trap: Once the subjunctive is learned, learners put it after every che; facts you knew stay in the indicative.

pronunciation: Hold the double s of the imperfect subjunctive: fosse, capissi, parlassero, avessi. A single s ('fose') is hard to recognise.
In the noi and loro forms the stress falls on the syllable before -ss-: parlàssimo, capìssero, fòssero; never on the ending.

common_errors.why: A past verb of thinking takes the imperfect subjunctive in careful speech; the indicative is casual.

common_errors.wrong: Pensavo che tu sei già partito.
common_errors.why: Something earlier than a past moment takes the pluperfect subjunctive.
Past main verb, so the subjunctive moves into the past too.
sapere introduces a fact: indicative.

common_errors.wrong: Non mi aspettavo che io trovassi lavoro.
common_errors.right: Non mi aspettavo di trovare lavoro.
common_errors.why: Same subject in both parts: di + infinitive.

units.culture: Many offices, small shops and some pharmacies close for lunch (roughly 12:30–13:00 to 15:30–16:00), and many public offices are open to the public only in the morning on most days; check the 'orari al pubblico' before you go.
recycles: b1-07 (Penso che sia... now moved into the past)
units.evidence: Talking about their first months or about stereotypes, the learner pairs a past verb of thinking with the imperfect or pluperfect subjunctive (credevo che fosse, pensavo che fossi già partito) without pausing, and keeps sapevo che + indicative.
sources: P2 U7 (congiuntivo imperfetto and trapassato; sequence of tenses; 'Credevo che volesse vivere in centro!')
P2 U5 (stereotypes about Italians)
P2 U11 ('Ti facevo più...' = 'Credevo che tu fossi...')
Proudfoot U20–U21
P3 U19 (congiuntivo imperfetto in past contexts)

units.title: Where and how to live: city, country, environment
units.can_do: Discuss city and country life and environmental habits, describe the home you're looking for, and argue what people should do.
situations: telling an estate agent what you're looking for
neighbours talking about traffic, noise and a new cycle lane
a friend dreaming of moving to the country

frames.it: Cerco una casa che abbia un po' di verde.
frames.en: I'm looking for a house with a bit of green space.

frames.it: C'è un quartiere che sia tranquillo ma vicino al centro?
frames.en: Is there a neighbourhood that's quiet but close to the centre?

frames.it: Sarebbe meglio che tutti usassimo meno la macchina.
frames.en: It would be better if we all used the car less.

frames.it: Parla come se fosse il sindaco.
frames.en: He talks as if he were the mayor.

frames.it: Magari avessi un balcone!
frames.en: If only I had a balcony!

frames.it: Nonostante il traffico, preferisco vivere in centro.
frames.en: Despite the traffic, I prefer living in the centre.

frames.it: Nonostante sia caro, ne vale la pena.
frames.en: Even though it's expensive, it's worth it.

frames.it: In campagna si vive meglio, ma senza macchina è dura.
frames.en: Life's better in the country, but without a car it's tough.

frames.it: Qui l'umido si porta giù il lunedì e il giovedì.
frames.en: Here food waste goes down on Mondays and Thursdays.

model_exchanges.situation: Telling an estate agent what you're looking for

lines.speaker: agent
lines.it: Allora, che cosa cerca esattamente?
lines.en: So, what exactly are you looking for?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Cerco un appartamento che abbia un balcone o un po' di verde.
lines.en: I'm looking for a flat with a balcony or a bit of green.

lines.speaker: agent
lines.it: In centro è difficile. Le andrebbe bene la periferia?
lines.en: That's hard in the centre. Would the outskirts suit you?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Preferirei di no. Nonostante il traffico, mi piace vivere in centro.
lines.en: I'd rather not. Despite the traffic, I like living in the centre.

lines.speaker: agent
lines.it: Ho un bilocale con un terrazzino, ma è al quarto piano senza ascensore.
lines.en: I have a two-room flat with a small terrace, but it's on the fourth floor with no lift.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Magari avessi vent'anni di meno! Andiamo a vederlo comunque.
lines.en: If only I were twenty years younger! Let's go and see it anyway.

model_exchanges.situation: Neighbours talking about traffic and rubbish

lines.speaker: neighbour
lines.it: Hai visto? Vogliono chiudere la piazza alle macchine.
lines.en: Have you seen? They want to close the square to cars.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Era ora! Sarebbe meglio che tutti usassimo meno la macchina.
lines.en: About time! It would be better if we all used the car less.

lines.speaker: neighbour
lines.it: Sì, ma il signor Russo dice che è una follia. Parla come se fosse il sindaco!
lines.en: Yes, but Mr Russo says it's madness. He talks as if he were the mayor!

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Lui parla sempre così. E la nuova pista ciclabile?
lines.en: He always talks like that. And the new cycle lane?

lines.speaker: neighbour
lines.it: Bella. Ah, ricordati: qui l'umido si porta giù il lunedì e il giovedì.
lines.en: Nice. Oh, remember: here food waste goes down on Mondays and Thursdays.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Grazie! Non sapevo che ci fosse un calendario.
lines.en: Thanks! I didn't know there was a schedule.

model_exchanges.situation: A friend dreaming of the country

lines.speaker: friend
lines.it: Tu dove vivresti, in città o in campagna?
lines.en: Where would you live, in town or in the country?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: In campagna si vive meglio, ma senza macchina è dura.
lines.en: Life's better in the country, but without a car it's tough.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.it: Io ho un orto dai miei nonni. Se potessi, mi trasferirei lì.
lines.en: I have a vegetable garden at my grandparents'. If I could, I'd move there.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Magari avessi un orto anch'io!
lines.en: I wish I had a vegetable garden too!

grammar.point: subjunctive in a relative clause for something wished for
grammar.explain: When you describe something you're looking for and don't yet know exists, the verb after che goes into the subjunctive; for something real and known, it stays indicative.

examples.it: Cerco una casa che abbia il riscaldamento autonomo.
examples.en: I'm looking for a house with its own heating.

examples.it: Abito in una casa che ha un bel giardino.
examples.en: I live in a house that has a lovely garden.
Is there anyone who speaks English?

grammar.trap: English uses the same 'that has' for both; Italian marks the wished-for one with abbia, sia, possa.

grammar.explain: After a conditional main verb (sarebbe meglio, sarebbe bello, vorrei) the verb after che goes into the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.it: Sarebbe meglio che tu prendessi l'autobus.
examples.en: It would be better if you took the bus.

examples.it: Sarebbe bello se ci fosse più verde.
examples.en: It would be nice if there were more green space.

grammar.trap: Saying 'sarebbe meglio che usiamo': the conditional pulls the subjunctive into the past form.

grammar.point: come se and magari + congiuntivo imperfetto
grammar.explain: come se (as if) and magari (if only) take the imperfect subjunctive whatever the tense of the rest of the sentence, or the pluperfect subjunctive for something earlier (come se non fosse successo niente; magari l'avessi saputo!).

examples.it: Mi tratta come se fossi un turista.
examples.en: He treats me as if I were a tourist.
If only I had more time!

grammar.trap: magari with the indicative means 'maybe': 'Magari vengo domani' is 'Maybe I'll come tomorrow', not a wish.

grammar.explain: nonostante (despite, although) takes a noun directly or a whole clause in the subjunctive.

examples.en: Despite the rain, we went out.

examples.it: Nonostante sia caro, ne vale la pena.
examples.en: Although it's expensive, it's worth it.

grammar.trap: English 'despite being' tempts learners into 'nonostante essendo'; use a subjunctive clause or anche se + indicative.

grammar.point: impersonal si for people in general
grammar.explain: si + third-person singular verb means 'people / you / one', and an adjective after si è goes plural.

examples.en: Life's better in the country.

examples.it: In centro si è più vicini a tutto.
examples.en: In the centre you're closer to everything.

grammar.trap: The adjective after 'si è' is plural (si è stanchi), even though the verb is singular.

pronunciation: In central and southern Italy a word after a, da, è, che, se is often said with a doubled first consonant: 'a casa' sounds like 'a ccasa', 'da me' like 'da mme'. Northerners don't do it; both are correct, and knowing it helps you hear the words.
The double s of the imperfect subjunctive again: fosse, avessi, usassimo, prendessi.

common_errors.wrong: Cerco una casa che ha un balcone.
common_errors.right: Cerco una casa che abbia un balcone.
common_errors.why: You don't have a particular house in mind yet: subjunctive in the relative clause.

common_errors.wrong: Parla come se è il sindaco.
common_errors.right: Parla come se fosse il sindaco.
common_errors.why: come se always takes the imperfect (or pluperfect) subjunctive.

common_errors.wrong: Sarebbe meglio che usiamo meno la macchina.
common_errors.right: Sarebbe meglio che usassimo meno la macchina.
common_errors.why: A conditional main verb takes the imperfect subjunctive.
nonostante takes a noun or a subjunctive clause, not an infinitive or gerund.
A wish with magari takes the imperfect subjunctive; with the indicative it means 'maybe'.

units.culture: Rubbish is sorted at home into umido (food), plastica e metalli, carta, vetro and indifferenziato, and every comune sets its own rules: many collect door to door on fixed days, others use street bins. Ask a neighbour or get the comune's calendar; fines for wrong sorting do happen.
recycles: b1-04 (comparatives: più luminoso, meno rumoroso; flat vocabulary)
b2-01 (congiuntivo imperfetto after a past verb)
units.evidence: Describing the home or neighbourhood they want, the learner uses 'che abbia / che sia' for what they're looking for, and come se, magari and sarebbe meglio che with the imperfect subjunctive, while keeping the indicative for what they already have.
sources: P2 U7 (city vs country, housing ads, environment forum; subjunctive in relatives, come se, magari, nonostante, 'Sarebbe meglio che tutti noi smettessimo di usare le automobili')
P3 U13 (environment; subjunctive in relative clauses)
Proudfoot U19 (restricted relative clauses: 'Cerco ... che non costi troppo')
P2 U0 (impersonal si: 'si vive meglio')

units.title: Regrets and what might have been
units.can_do: Talk about what you should have done, what would have happened, and what you'd do differently.
situations: explaining why you missed a friend's party

frames.it: Avrei dovuto prenotare prima.
frames.en: I should have booked earlier.

frames.it: Se l'avessi saputo, sarei venuto anch'io.
frames.en: If I'd known, I'd have come too.
frames.note: venuto / venuta agrees with the speaker.

frames.it: Se avessi studiato l'italiano da giovane, adesso lo parlerei meglio.
frames.en: If I'd studied Italian when I was young, I'd speak it better now.

frames.it: Sarei venuta volentieri, ma avevo già un impegno.
frames.en: I'd gladly have come, but I already had plans.

frames.it: Potevi dirmelo!
frames.en: You could have told me!

frames.it: Magari non l'avessi mai comprata!
frames.en: I wish I'd never bought it!

frames.it: Pazienza, sarà per la prossima volta.
frames.en: Never mind, another time.

frames.it: Se lo sapevo, non venivo.
frames.en: If I'd known, I wouldn't have come.
frames.note: Colloquial; the written form is 'Se l'avessi saputo, non sarei venuto'.

model_exchanges.situation: Explaining why you missed a friend's party

lines.speaker: friend

lines.speaker: friend
lines.it: Peccato! Se fossi venuto, ti avrei fatto conoscere mio cugino.
lines.en: Shame! If you'd come, I'd have introduced you to my cousin.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Se l'avessi saputo, avrei spostato l'impegno!
lines.en: If I'd known, I'd have moved my plans!

lines.speaker: friend
lines.it: Pazienza, sarà per la prossima volta.
lines.en: Never mind, another time.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Senz'altro. La prossima volta non me la perdo.

lines.it: Allora, la bici nuova?

lines.speaker: newcomer

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Potevi dirmelo prima!

lines.speaker: newcomer

lines.en: You're right. I should have looked into it more.

lines.speaker: A
lines.it: Hai qualche rimpianto?
lines.en: Do you have any regrets?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Non molti. Però se avessi studiato l'italiano da giovane, adesso lo parlerei meglio.
lines.en: Not many. But if I'd studied Italian when I was young, I'd speak it better now.

lines.speaker: A
lines.it: Ma lo parli benissimo!
lines.en: But you speak it really well!

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Grazie. E se fossi venuto qui prima, avrei avuto più tempo per imparare.
lines.en: Thanks. And if I'd come here earlier, I'd have had more time to learn.

grammar.explain: avrei / sarei + past participle means 'would have', and with dovere and potere it gives 'should have' and 'could have'.

examples.en: I should have booked earlier.
I could have asked.
I'd gladly have come.

grammar.trap: English 'should have done' tempts learners into 'dovrei avere fatto'; Italian puts the past on dovere: avrei dovuto fare.

grammar.point: se + congiuntivo trapassato, then condizionale passato
grammar.explain: For something that didn't happen in the past, use se + avessi / fossi + participle, then avrei / sarei + participle.

examples.en: If I'd known, I'd have come.

examples.it: Se fossimo partiti prima, saremmo arrivati in tempo.
examples.en: If we'd left earlier, we'd have arrived on time.

grammar.trap: Never the conditional after se: 'se avrei saputo' is the classic mistake.

grammar.explain: When a past 'if' has an effect now, the se part is past (congiuntivo trapassato) and the result is the present conditional.

examples.it: Se avessi studiato da giovane, adesso parlerei meglio.
examples.en: If I'd studied when I was young, I'd speak better now.

examples.it: Se avessi preso l'ombrello, adesso non sarei bagnato.
examples.en: If I'd taken the umbrella, I wouldn't be wet now.

grammar.trap: Putting the result in the past ('avrei parlato') when you mean now.

grammar.explain: In everyday speech Italians often use the imperfect in both halves of a past 'if' sentence; understand it, but use the full forms yourself for now.

examples.en: If I'd known, I wouldn't have come.

examples.it: Se partivi prima, arrivavi in tempo.
examples.en: If you'd left earlier, you'd have been on time.

grammar.trap: Hearing 'se lo sapevo' and thinking it's about a habit; it's a past 'if'.

grammar.point: potevi / dovevi + infinitive as a reproach
grammar.explain: The imperfect of potere and dovere + infinitive is the everyday way to say 'you could / should have'.

examples.en: You could have warned me!
You should have told me before.

grammar.trap: It's a reproach: say it to friends, not to an official or the landlady.

vocabulary.en: to make a mistake, get wrong

pronunciation: Conditional vs future: avremmo (we would have) has a long mm, avremo (we will have) a short m; the same with saremmo / saremo and potremmo / potremo. The double consonant is the only difference you hear.
avrei, sarei, dovrei: stress the e (av-RÈ-i), and keep e and i as two clear vowels, not an English 'ay'.

common_errors.why: After se, the subjunctive; the conditional goes in the other half.
'Should have' is the past conditional of dovere + infinitive.
venire takes essere, in the conditional too.

common_errors.wrong: Se avessi studiato da giovane, adesso avrei parlato meglio.
common_errors.right: Se avessi studiato da giovane, adesso parlerei meglio.
common_errors.why: The result is about now: present conditional.
With essere, the participle agrees with the speaker.

units.culture: Italians soften a refusal or a no-show with the past conditional and a reason ('Sarei venuto volentieri, ma...'), and the host usually answers 'Pazienza, sarà per la prossima volta'. A flat 'non potevo' with no reason can sound abrupt.
recycles: b1-02 (combined pronouns: me l'hai chiesto, non me la perdo)
units.evidence: Explaining a missed event or a bad choice, the learner says avrei dovuto / sarei venuto and builds a full 'se + avessi saputo → avrei...' sentence, including a mixed one with a present result, without putting the conditional after se.
sources: P2 U8 (types 1–3 and mixed hypotheticals)
P1B U11 (condizionale composto)
Proudfoot U21 (regrets; Nando and the mechanic: 'Magari non l'avessi mai portata da lui!'), U22 (Carla and Maria: 'Sarei venuta se...', 'Pazienza!'), U12 (colloquial imperfect: 'Potevi telefonarmi')
P3 U24 ('Se lo sapevo, venivo')

units.title: Tech, contracts and customer service
units.can_do: Explain a technical problem, follow troubleshooting steps, and press your case with a phone or internet company.
situations: calling customer service about home internet
cancelling a contract in a phone shop
a friend helping you with an app

frames.it: Da quando ho cambiato operatore, non ho più rete in casa.
frames.en: Since I changed provider, I've had no signal at home.

frames.it: Ha provato a spegnere e riaccendere il modem?
frames.en: Have you tried turning the modem off and on again?

frames.it: Ci ho già provato tre volte.
frames.en: I've already tried three times.

frames.it: Non ci capisco niente.
frames.en: I can't make head or tail of it.

frames.it: Quanto ci mettete a mandare un tecnico?
frames.en: How long will it take you to send a technician?

frames.it: Vorrei disdire il contratto senza penali.
frames.en: I'd like to cancel the contract without penalties.

frames.it: Se non risolvete il problema entro venerdì, faccio reclamo.
frames.en: If you don't fix the problem by Friday, I'll file a complaint.

frames.it: Me ne occupo io.
frames.en: I'll take care of it.
frames.note: You can say it too, offering to handle something.

frames.it: Ne ho sentito parlare, ma non l'ho mai usato.
frames.en: I've heard of it, but I've never used it.

model_exchanges.situation: Calling customer service about home internet

lines.speaker: operator
lines.it: Servizio clienti, sono Marco. Come posso aiutarla?
lines.en: Customer service, Marco speaking. How can I help you?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Buongiorno. Da quando ho cambiato operatore, la fibra non funziona.
lines.en: Good morning. Since I changed provider, the fibre hasn't worked.

lines.speaker: operator
lines.it: Ha provato a spegnere e riaccendere il modem?
lines.en: Have you tried turning the modem off and on again?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Sì, ci ho già provato tre volte. La luce rimane rossa.
lines.en: Yes, I've already tried three times. The light stays red.

lines.speaker: operator
lines.it: Allora apro una segnalazione e Le mando un tecnico. Me ne occupo io.
lines.en: Then I'll open a fault report and send you a technician. I'll take care of it.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Quanto ci mettete?
lines.en: How long will it take you?

lines.speaker: operator
lines.it: Di solito tre o quattro giorni lavorativi.
lines.en: Usually three or four working days.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Se non risolvete entro venerdì, faccio reclamo.
lines.en: If you don't fix it by Friday, I'll file a complaint.

model_exchanges.situation: Cancelling a contract in a phone shop

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Buongiorno, vorrei disdire il contratto.
lines.en: Good morning, I'd like to cancel my contract.

lines.speaker: shop assistant
lines.it: Mi dispiace. Posso chiederle perché?
lines.en: I'm sorry to hear that. May I ask why?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Non ho mai rete in casa. Ci ho pensato bene: cambio operatore.
lines.en: I never have signal at home. I've thought it over: I'm changing provider.

lines.speaker: shop assistant
lines.it: Se disdice prima di un anno, ci sono cinquanta euro di costi di disattivazione.
lines.en: If you cancel before a year is up, there's a fifty-euro deactivation charge.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Ma il servizio non ha mai funzionato! Non mi sembra giusto pagare.
lines.en: But the service has never worked! I don't think it's fair to pay.

lines.speaker: shop assistant
lines.it: Capisco. Ne parlo con il responsabile e La richiamo.
lines.en: I understand. I'll talk to the manager about it and call you back.

model_exchanges.situation: A friend helping with an app

lines.speaker: friend
lines.it: Hai scaricato l'app del comune?
lines.en: Have you downloaded the town council's app?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Sì, ma non ci capisco niente.
lines.en: Yes, but I can't make head or tail of it.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.it: Dammi il telefono... Ecco: devi metterci il codice fiscale, qui.
lines.en: Give me the phone... There: you need to put your tax code in here.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Ah! E la password? Me la sono dimenticata.
lines.en: Oh! And the password? I've forgotten it.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.it: Ci penso io, la reimpostiamo.
lines.en: Leave it to me, we'll reset it.

grammar.point: ci for 'it' with verbs that take a or in
grammar.explain: ci replaces 'a / in + something' and turns up in many everyday verbs: provarci (try it), pensarci (think about it, see to it), capirci (understand it), crederci (believe it), metterci (take time).

examples.en: I tried.
Leave it to me.
I don't believe it.

grammar.trap: English drops the 'it' ('I tried'); Italian needs ci. pensare a → ci penso, but pensare di (opinion) → cosa ne pensi?

grammar.point: ne for 'of / about it' with verbs that take di
grammar.explain: ne replaces 'di + something': parlarne, sentirne parlare, occuparsene (me ne occupo), averne abbastanza.

examples.en: I'll talk to the manager about it.
I'll take care of it.
I've heard of it.

grammar.trap: occuparsi di → me ne occupo, not 'lo occupo' (that would mean 'I occupy it').

grammar.explain: metterci agrees with the person or thing doing the job (quanto ci mettete?), while ci vuole / ci vogliono states the time needed in general.

examples.it: Quanto ci mettete a mandare un tecnico?
examples.en: How long will it take you to send a technician?
It takes three days.

grammar.trap: Saying 'quanto tempo ci mettono tre giorni': ci vuole / vogliono for the time, metterci for who takes it.

grammar.point: real conditions as promises or threats
grammar.explain: se + present, then present (or future) for a real condition: what you'll do if they don't act.

examples.it: Se non risolvete entro venerdì, faccio reclamo.
examples.en: If you don't fix it by Friday, I'll file a complaint.

examples.it: Se mi fa lo sconto, resto con voi.
examples.en: If you give me the discount, I'll stay with you.

grammar.trap: No 'will' after se: the present does the job in both halves.

grammar.explain: da quando + passato prossimo gives the starting point, and the situation that still continues goes in the present.

examples.it: Da quando ho cambiato operatore, non ho più rete.
examples.en: Since I changed provider, I've had no signal.

examples.it: Da quando abito qui, vado in bici.
examples.en: Since I've lived here, I've cycled.

grammar.trap: English 'I've had no signal' pushes learners into 'non ho avuto'; something still true now is present in Italian.

vocabulary.en: to take care of, deal with

pronunciation: English tech words are said the Italian way: modem is MÒ-dem, Wi-Fi is 'uài-fài', giga has a soft g ('JEE-ga'), and app has a short a.
riaccendere: the cc before e is a long 'ch', ri-at-CHEN-de-re; caricabatterie has a long tt.

common_errors.why: cancellare means delete or rub out; contracts, subscriptions and bookings are disdetti.
occuparsi di: reflexive pronoun + ne.

common_errors.wrong: Da quando ho cambiato operatore, non ho avuto rete.
common_errors.right: Da quando ho cambiato operatore, non ho più rete.
common_errors.why: The problem is still going on: present.

common_errors.wrong: Penso a questo e La richiamo.
common_errors.why: 'Think about it' is ci penso; Italian doesn't repeat 'this'.

common_errors.wrong: Se non risolverete entro venerdì, farò reclamo.
common_errors.right: Se non risolvete entro venerdì, faccio reclamo.
common_errors.why: Not wrong, but stiff on the phone; the present is the everyday choice.

units.culture: To cancel a phone, internet or utility contract you usually send a formal disdetta (by PEC, registered letter or the provider's online form), often with 30 days' notice. Ask for the 'numero della pratica' and keep it. By law you can cancel or switch provider at any time without penalties (penali), but the contract can still charge deactivation costs (costi di disattivazione) and any remaining instalments on a modem or phone.
recycles: a2-14 (Pronto..., La richiamo; SIM and giga vocabulary)
a2-13 (da + present for something that isn't working)
b2-03 (conditional to soften a complaint: non mi sembra giusto)
b1-02 (combined pronouns: me la sono dimenticata)
units.evidence: On a service call the learner explains what's wrong with da quando + present, uses ci and ne without hesitation (ci ho provato, ne parlo, me ne occupo), understands the agent's troubleshooting, and states a real condition as a firm request.
sources: P2 U8 (tech troubleshooting dialogue: 'Hai provato a spegnere e a riaccendere il pc?'; phone deals: canone mensile, 'non hai rete'; uses of ci and ne)
P2 U0 (ci vuole / ci vogliono vs metterci)
P3 U16 (internet vocabulary), U21 (ci and ne: ci penso, ci conto)
Proudfoot Appendix 4.4–4.5 (ci and ne)
gap: customer-service calls and cancelling contracts (P2 §5, P3 §5)

units.title: Rules, signs and procedures: the passive
units.can_do: Understand and explain rules, signs and procedures: what is done, what must be done, and what isn't allowed.
situations: a ticket inspector on the bus
notices in your building's entrance hall
rules in a church, museum or shop

frames.it: Il biglietto va convalidato prima di salire.
frames.en: The ticket must be validated before boarding.

frames.it: La domanda deve essere presentata entro il 30 giugno.
frames.en: The application must be submitted by 30 June.

frames.it: Qui si accettano solo contanti.
frames.en: Only cash is accepted here.

frames.it: Come si fa a rinnovare il permesso?
frames.en: How do you go about renewing the permit?

frames.it: Le domande vengono esaminate in ordine di arrivo.
frames.en: Applications are processed in order of arrival.

frames.it: I documenti vanno consegnati in originale e in copia.
frames.en: The documents must be handed in as originals and copies.

frames.it: Si prega di non toccare la merce.
frames.en: Please do not touch the goods.

frames.it: È vietato fumare in tutto l'edificio.
frames.en: Smoking is prohibited throughout the building.

frames.it: Spingere. / Tirare.
frames.en: Push. / Pull.
frames.note: Signs and instructions use the infinitive.

model_exchanges.situation: Asking how to renew a residence permit

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Buongiorno, come si fa a rinnovare il permesso di soggiorno?
lines.en: Good morning, how do you go about renewing a residence permit?

lines.speaker: clerk
lines.it: La domanda va presentata alla posta con il kit, almeno sessanta giorni prima della scadenza.
lines.en: The application must be submitted at the post office with the kit, at least sixty days before it expires.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: E i documenti vanno portati in originale?
lines.en: And do the documents have to be brought as originals?

lines.speaker: clerk
lines.it: Originale e fotocopia. Le domande vengono esaminate in ordine di arrivo.
lines.en: Original and photocopy. Applications are processed in order of arrival.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Quindi non si può prendere un appuntamento?
lines.en: So you can't book an appointment?

lines.speaker: clerk
lines.it: L'appuntamento in questura per le impronte viene fissato dalla posta: lo trova sulla ricevuta.
lines.en: The questura appointment for fingerprints is set by the post office: you'll find it on the receipt.

model_exchanges.situation: A ticket inspector on the bus

model_exchanges.situation: Explaining the building notices to a new neighbour

lines.speaker: new neighbour
lines.it: Scusi, cosa vuol dire quell'avviso?
lines.en: Excuse me, what does that notice mean?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Dice che le biciclette non vanno lasciate nell'androne.
lines.en: It says bikes mustn't be left in the entrance hall.

lines.en: And the sign on the front door?

grammar.explain: essere (in any tense) + past participle makes the passive, the participle agrees with the subject, and the doer is introduced by da.

examples.it: La chiesa è stata restaurata nel 2010.
examples.en: The church was restored in 2010.

examples.it: Il modulo è firmato dal direttore.
examples.en: The form is signed by the director.

grammar.trap: 'By' is da, not per; and the participle agrees (la domanda è stata accettata).

grammar.explain: In simple tenses (present, imperfect, future) venire can replace essere, especially for how things are regularly done.

examples.it: Le domande vengono esaminate in ordine di arrivo.
examples.en: Applications are processed in order of arrival.

examples.it: Il pane viene sfornato alle sette.
examples.en: The bread comes out of the oven at seven.

grammar.trap: Never venire in compound tenses: 'è venuto costruito' is wrong; say 'è stato costruito'.

grammar.point: andare + past participle = must be done
grammar.explain: andare + participle means something has to be done, and the participle agrees with the subject.

examples.en: The ticket must be validated.

examples.it: I documenti vanno consegnati in copia.
examples.en: The documents must be handed in as copies.

grammar.trap: It has nothing to do with going: 'va convalidato' is not 'goes to be validated'.

grammar.explain: dovere / potere + essere + participle says what must or can be done.

examples.it: La domanda deve essere presentata entro giugno.
examples.en: The application must be submitted by June.

examples.it: La tassa può essere pagata online.
examples.en: The fee can be paid online.

grammar.trap: Keep essere as an infinitive and make the participle agree: 'deve essere presentata', not 'deve presentata'.

grammar.explain: si + verb agrees with the noun that follows (si accetta la carta, si accettano carte), while with no object the verb stays singular (si entra, come si fa a...).

examples.en: Only cash is accepted here.

examples.it: Da qui si entra solo con il biglietto.
examples.en: You can only get in here with a ticket.

grammar.trap: 'Si vende case' is wrong: case is plural, so si vendono case.

grammar.point: the infinitive on signs and in instructions
grammar.explain: Notices, forms and instructions use the infinitive as an impersonal command: spingere, non fumare, compilare in stampatello.

examples.en: Fill in in block capitals.
Do not speak to the driver.

grammar.trap: On a sign 'Non toccare' isn't a rude tu; it's addressed to nobody in particular.

pronunciation: In third-person plurals the stress stays early: vèngono, si accèttano, vànno, esàminano; never stress the -no ending (ven-GO-no is wrong).
Read signs with the stress in the right place: vie-TÀ-to, ob-bli-ga-TÒ-rio (with a long bb), con-sen-TÌ-to.

common_errors.why: With si passivante the verb agrees with the plural noun.
venire is only for simple tenses; compound tenses use essere.

common_errors.wrong: La domanda va presentato entro giugno.
common_errors.right: La domanda va presentata entro giugno.
common_errors.why: The participle agrees with the subject.

common_errors.wrong: La chiesa è stata costruita per Bernini.
common_errors.right: La chiesa è stata costruita da Bernini.
common_errors.why: The doer in a passive is introduced by da.

common_errors.right: Devo convalidare il biglietto? / Il biglietto va convalidato?
common_errors.why: Either an active modal + infinitive, or andare + participle.

units.culture: City bus and tram tickets are bought before you board (tabaccheria, edicola, machine or app) and must be validated as soon as you get on; inspectors fine on the spot, and 'I didn't know' rarely works. Paper regional train tickets also need validating, while digital ones usually carry a set date or need an online check-in.
recycles: b1-01 (offices: la pratica, lo sportello; Lei instructions: compili, firmi)
b1-13 (è stata costruita as a chunk; si può / si possono)
units.evidence: Asked how something works (a permit, a ticket, a building rule), the learner explains it with va + participle, deve essere + participle and si + verb with correct agreement, and reads a notice aloud and says what it means.
sources: P2 U9 (passive with essere, venire and andare; with modals; si passivante; 'Il biglietto va convalidato prima di salire sul treno')
P2 U11 (signs and infinitive instructions: 'Si prega la gentile clientela di non toccare la merce esposta'; 'Compilare e firmare il modulo')
Proudfoot U15 (processes and procedures)
EGSI ch.31 (active and passive voice)
P3 U12–U13 (passive with modals; andare / venire)
P3 U22 (permesso di soggiorno, presentare domanda)

units.title: Art, craft and the stories of things
units.can_do: Talk about a work of art or a handmade object: who made it, how and when, and what you think of it.
functions: follow narration in the literary past
ask the maker how it's done
situations: a guide in a church or chapel

frames.it: Questo affresco è stato attribuito a Giotto.
frames.en: This fresco has been attributed to Giotto.

frames.it: Il campanile fu completato dopo la morte dell'architetto.
frames.en: The bell tower was completed after the architect's death.

frames.it: Lo dipinse un allievo del maestro.
frames.en: A pupil of the master painted it.

frames.it: Come viene fatta questa ceramica?
frames.en: How is this pottery made?

frames.it: Prima viene modellata a mano, poi viene cotta nel forno.
frames.en: First it's shaped by hand, then it's fired in the kiln.

frames.it: Quello che mi colpisce è la luce.
frames.en: What strikes me is the light.

frames.it: È un capolavoro, anche se non è il mio genere.
frames.en: It's a masterpiece, even if it's not my thing.

frames.it: È un pezzo unico o ne fate altri uguali?
frames.en: Is it a one-off, or do you make others like it?

model_exchanges.situation: In a ceramics workshop

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Che belli questi piatti! Come viene fatta questa ceramica?
lines.en: These plates are lovely! How is this pottery made?

lines.speaker: craftswoman
lines.it: Prima viene modellata a mano, poi viene cotta nel forno una prima volta.
lines.en: First it's shaped by hand, then it's fired in the kiln once.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: E i colori?
lines.en: And the colours?

lines.speaker: craftswoman
lines.it: Dopo la prima cottura il pezzo viene smaltato, poi viene dipinto a mano e cotto una seconda volta.
lines.en: After the first firing the piece is glazed, then it's painted by hand and fired a second time.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: È un pezzo unico o ne fate altri uguali?
lines.en: Is it a one-off, or do you make others like it?

lines.speaker: craftswoman
lines.it: Ogni pezzo è unico: non ce ne sono due uguali.
lines.en: Every piece is unique: no two are the same.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Allora lo prendo. Me lo può incartare?
lines.en: Then I'll take it. Could you wrap it for me?

model_exchanges.situation: With a guide in a church

lines.speaker: guide
lines.it: Questa cappella fu affrescata all'inizio del Trecento.
lines.en: This chapel was frescoed in the early 1300s.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Da chi è stata dipinta?
lines.en: Who was it painted by?

lines.speaker: guide
lines.it: È attribuita a Giotto, ma alcuni studiosi pensano che l'abbia dipinta un suo allievo.
lines.en: It's attributed to Giotto, but some scholars think one of his pupils painted it.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Quello che mi colpisce sono i colori. Sono originali?
lines.en: What strikes me is the colours. Are they original?

lines.speaker: guide
lines.it: Sì, ma l'affresco è stato restaurato negli anni Novanta.
lines.en: Yes, but the fresco was restored in the nineties.

model_exchanges.situation: At an exhibition with a friend

lines.speaker: friend
lines.it: Allora, ti piace?
lines.en: So, do you like it?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: È un grande artista, ma questo quadro non è il mio genere.
lines.en: He's a great artist, but this painting isn't my thing.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.it: Davvero? Per me è un capolavoro.
lines.en: Really? For me it's a masterpiece.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Lo so. Quello che non mi convince sono i colori: troppo scuri.
lines.en: I know. What doesn't convince me is the colours: too dark.

grammar.point: venire + participle for how things are made
grammar.explain: To describe the steps of a process, Italian uses venire + past participle in the present, agreeing with the thing being made.

examples.it: La ceramica viene modellata a mano.
examples.en: The pottery is shaped by hand.

examples.it: I piatti vengono dipinti uno per uno.
examples.en: The plates are painted one by one.

grammar.trap: The participle agrees: la ceramica viene cotta, i piatti vengono cotti.

grammar.explain: Guides, labels and books tell history in the passato remoto; recognise it and use a few set forms (fu, nacque, morì, dipinse, costruirono).

examples.it: Michelangelo nacque nel 1475 e morì a Roma.
examples.en: Michelangelo was born in 1475 and died in Rome.

examples.it: La chiesa fu costruita nel Trecento.
examples.en: The church was built in the 1300s.

grammar.trap: For your own past use the passato prossimo; 'ieri visitai il museo' sounds bookish in most of Italy (though normal speech in parts of the South).

grammar.point: quello che / ciò che as the subject
grammar.explain: 'What' at the start of a sentence ('What strikes me is...') is quello che (or ciò che), and the verb essere agrees with what follows.

examples.it: Quello che mi piace è la luce.
examples.en: What I like is the light.

examples.it: Quello che non mi convince sono i colori.
examples.en: What doesn't convince me is the colours.

grammar.trap: Starting with 'Cosa mi piace è...' is wrong: cosa is for questions.

grammar.explain: A few adjectives mean something different before and after the noun: un grande artista (a great artist) / un artista grande (a big artist); un vecchio amico (an old friend) / un amico vecchio (an elderly friend); un pezzo unico (a one-off) / l'unico pezzo (the only piece).

examples.en: He's a great painter.

examples.it: Questo è l'unico pezzo che mi resta.
examples.en: This is the only piece I have left.

grammar.trap: Putting grande after the noun when you mean 'great'.

vocabulary.en: kind, style ('il mio genere' = my thing)

pronunciation: Passato remoto forms stressed on the last vowel must keep that stress: completò, restaurò, morì. Without it, completò (it completed) turns into completo (complete).
Watch sc: scultura and scuro are 'sk', but scena and lasciò are 'sh'.

common_errors.wrong: Cosa mi piace è la luce.
common_errors.right: Quello che mi piace è la luce.
common_errors.why: 'What' as a subject is quello che / ciò che; cosa is for questions.

common_errors.wrong: Questa ceramica è venuta fatta a mano.
common_errors.right: Questa ceramica è stata fatta a mano. / viene fatta a mano.
common_errors.why: venire as a passive auxiliary is only used in simple tenses.
After the noun grande means 'big'; 'great' goes before.

common_errors.wrong: Il quadro è dipinto per Caravaggio.
common_errors.right: Il quadro è dipinto da Caravaggio.
common_errors.why: The doer is introduced by da.
For your own recent past, the passato prossimo is the spoken norm.

units.culture: State museums are free on the first Sunday of the month ('domenica al museo'), so expect crowds. Churches ask for covered shoulders and quiet during Mass. In a craft workshop (bottega) it's welcome to ask how a piece is made before buying, and handmade pieces are rarely bargained over.
recycles: b1-13 (passato remoto for recognition; centuries: il Trecento)
units.evidence: In a gallery or workshop the learner asks how and by whom something was made, describes the steps with venire + participle, follows a guide's passato remoto without losing the thread, and gives an opinion beginning 'Quello che mi colpisce è...'.
sources: P2 U9 (art, restoration, museums; the passive; attribuire)
P2 U4 (passato remoto)
P3 U27 (art vocabulary: bottega, tela, capolavoro; adjective position), U16 (adjective position changes meaning)
Proudfoot U15 (processes with venire), U2 (nuova macchina / macchina nuova)
EGSI ch.46 (quello che / ciò che)

units.title: Passing it on: what people said
units.can_do: Report what someone said, asked, promised or told you to do.
situations: passing on a plumber's promise to your landlady
telling a friend what a new neighbour asked you
relaying a text message from a friend
repeating the landlady's rules to a visitor

frames.it: L'idraulico ha detto che sarebbe passato domani mattina.
frames.en: The plumber said he'd come by tomorrow morning.
frames.note: 'domani' stays because it's still tomorrow; if that day is past, say 'il giorno dopo'.

frames.it: Mi ha chiesto se mi trovavo bene in Italia.
frames.en: She asked me whether I was getting on well in Italy.

frames.it: Mi ha chiesto da quanto tempo abitavo qui.
frames.en: He asked me how long I'd been living here.

frames.it: La padrona di casa mi ha detto di non lasciare le bici nell'androne.
frames.en: The landlady told me not to leave bikes in the entrance hall.

frames.it: Ha promesso che me l'avrebbe restituito.
frames.en: He promised he'd give it back to me.

frames.it: Ha detto che il giorno dopo sarebbe stato chiuso.
frames.en: She said it would be closed the next day.

frames.it: Ha detto che l'aveva già pagato.
frames.en: She said she'd already paid it.

frames.it: Dice che non ce la fa.
frames.en: He says he can't make it.

model_exchanges.situation: Passing on a plumber's promise to your landlady

lines.speaker: landlady
lines.it: Allora, è venuto l'idraulico?
lines.en: So, did the plumber come?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: No. Ieri ha telefonato e ha detto che sarebbe passato stamattina, ma non si è visto.
lines.en: No. Yesterday he rang and said he'd come by this morning, but he didn't turn up.

lines.speaker: landlady
lines.it: Tipico! E non ha detto perché?
lines.en: Typical! And he didn't say why?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Ha detto che aveva un'emergenza. Mi ha chiesto se andava bene giovedì.
lines.en: He said he had an emergency. He asked me if Thursday was all right.

lines.speaker: landlady
lines.it: Gli dica di chiamare me, glielo spiego io!
lines.en: Tell him to call me, I'll explain it to him!

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Va bene, glielo dico.
lines.en: All right, I'll tell him.

model_exchanges.situation: Telling a friend about meeting the new neighbour

lines.speaker: friend
lines.it: Com'è la nuova vicina?
lines.en: What's the new neighbour like?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Simpatica! Mi ha chiesto da quanto tempo abitavo qui e se mi trovavo bene.
lines.en: Nice! She asked me how long I'd been living here and whether I was happy here.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.it: E tu?
lines.en: And you?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Le ho detto che mi trovavo benissimo. Poi mi ha detto di passare da lei quando volevo.
lines.en: I told her I was very happy here. Then she told me to drop by whenever I wanted.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.it: Che carina!
lines.en: How sweet of her!

model_exchanges.situation: Relaying a message from a friend

lines.speaker: A
lines.it: Hai sentito Luca? Viene stasera?
lines.en: Have you heard from Luca? Is he coming tonight?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Mi ha scritto adesso. Dice che non ce la fa, è ancora in ufficio.
lines.en: He's just texted me. He says he can't make it, he's still at the office.

lines.speaker: A
lines.it: Peccato. E domani?
lines.en: Shame. And tomorrow?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Dice che ti chiama domani mattina.
lines.en: He says he'll call you tomorrow morning.

grammar.point: tense shifts after a past reporting verb
grammar.explain: After ha detto / ha promesso the present becomes imperfetto, the passato prossimo becomes trapassato, and the future becomes the condizionale passato.

examples.it: 'Sono stanco.' → Ha detto che era stanco.
examples.en: 'I'm tired.' → He said he was tired.

examples.it: 'Ho già pagato.' → Ha detto che aveva già pagato.
examples.en: 'I've already paid.' → She said she'd already paid.

examples.it: 'Passerò domani.' → Ha detto che sarebbe passato.
examples.en: 'I'll come by tomorrow.' → He said he'd come by.

grammar.trap: English 'he said he would come' leads to 'ha detto che verrebbe'; Italian uses the past conditional: sarebbe venuto.

grammar.explain: Yes/no questions are reported with se and others with the question word, with the imperfetto in speech (the subjunctive in careful writing: se mi trovassi bene).

examples.it: Mi ha chiesto se avevo fretta.
examples.en: She asked me if I was in a hurry.
He wanted to know how much it cost.

grammar.trap: No 'che' before se or the question word: 'mi ha chiesto che se...' is wrong.

grammar.explain: A reported order or request is dire / chiedere a qualcuno di (non) + infinitive.

examples.en: He told me to wait.

examples.it: Ci hanno detto di non preoccuparci.
examples.en: They told us not to worry.

grammar.trap: Don't keep the imperative or the present: 'mi ha detto che non lascio' means something else.

grammar.explain: When the moment has passed, domani becomes il giorno dopo, ieri il giorno prima, oggi quel giorno, qui lì, and 'my' and 'I' become 'his / her' and 'he / she'.

examples.it: 'Torno domani.' → Ha detto che tornava il giorno dopo.
examples.en: 'I'll be back tomorrow.' → He said he'd be back the next day.

examples.it: 'Ti chiamo.' → Ha detto che mi avrebbe chiamato.
examples.en: 'I'll call you.' → She said she'd call me.

grammar.trap: Shift only if the time has passed: if 'domani' is still tomorrow, keep domani.

grammar.point: no shift after a present reporting verb
grammar.explain: With dice che, scrive che, chiede se, nothing shifts: keep the tense of the original words.

examples.it: Dice che non ce la fa.
examples.en: He says he can't make it.
She writes that she'll arrive at eight.

grammar.trap: Applying the past shifts to 'dice che' ('dice che non ce la faceva') changes the meaning.

vocabulary.en: to be happy, get on well (somewhere)

pronunciation: 'Gliel'ho detto' (I told him / her) runs together as one word with the stress on the participle: glie-lo-DET-to, with the soft 'gl' of figlio.
Hold the bb of the conditional: sarebbe, avrebbe, verrebbe; a short b ('sarebe') is hard to recognise.

common_errors.right: Ha detto che sarebbe venuto domani.
common_errors.why: A future seen from the past is the past conditional.
After a past reporting verb, the present shifts to the imperfetto.

common_errors.wrong: Mi ha detto che non lascio le bici nell'androne.
common_errors.right: Mi ha detto di non lasciare le bici nell'androne.
common_errors.why: A reported command is di + infinitive.

common_errors.wrong: (last week) Ha detto che arriva domani.
common_errors.right: Ha detto che sarebbe arrivato il giorno dopo.
common_errors.why: Both the tense and the time word shift when the day has passed.

common_errors.wrong: Mi ha chiesto che se mi trovavo bene.
common_errors.right: Mi ha chiesto se mi trovavo bene.
common_errors.why: No che before se in a reported question.

units.culture: When a tradesman says 'passo domani' it often means 'in the next few days'. A polite call to check ('Volevo solo sapere se passa oggi...') is normal, not pushy, and passing on exactly what he said to the landlord or the amministratore is how repairs get done.
recycles: b1-02 (combined pronouns: me l'avrebbe restituito, glielo dico)
units.evidence: Passing on a message, the learner shifts tenses after a past verb (future to sarebbe + participle, present to imperfetto), turns commands into di + infinitive, shifts domani to il giorno dopo only when the day has passed, and keeps everything unshifted after dice che.
sources: P2 U10 (reported speech: statements, questions, commands; time and pronoun shifts; no shift after a present verb)
P1B U11 (future in the past)
Proudfoot U21 ('L'idraulico ha promesso che sarebbe venuto domani mattina'), U20 ('La signora ci ha chiesto se ci trovassimo bene in Italia')
EGSI ch.29 (future-in-the-past trap)
P3 U29 (reported speech; indirect questions with subjunctive or indicative)

units.title: Neighbourhood news: crime, scams and outrage
units.can_do: Talk about local news, warn someone about a scam, report a crime, and react with outrage or indifference.
situations: local news over coffee at the bar
a neighbour warning you about a scam
a heated chat about a local decision

frames.it: Hai sentito dei furti in via Mazzini?
frames.en: Have you heard about the burglaries in via Mazzini?

frames.it: Hanno fatto la denuncia ai carabinieri.
frames.en: They reported it to the carabinieri.

frames.it: Attenzione ai finti tecnici del gas!
frames.en: Watch out for fake gas engineers!

frames.it: Pare che siano entrati dal balcone.
frames.en: Apparently they got in through the balcony.

frames.it: A quanto ne so, l'hanno già arrestato.
frames.en: As far as I know, they've already arrested him.

frames.it: Che faccia tosta!
frames.en: What nerve!

frames.it: È il colmo!
frames.en: That's the last straw!

frames.it: E allora? / E con ciò?
frames.en: So what?

model_exchanges.situation: Local news over coffee at the bar

lines.speaker: barista
lines.it: Hai sentito dei furti in via Mazzini?
lines.en: Have you heard about the burglaries in via Mazzini?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: No! Cos'è successo?
lines.en: No! What happened?

lines.speaker: barista
lines.it: Sono entrati in tre appartamenti. Pare che siano passati dal balcone.
lines.en: They broke into three flats. Apparently they came in over the balcony.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: E hanno preso qualcosa?
lines.en: And did they take anything?

lines.speaker: barista
lines.it: Di tutto. Il colmo è che hanno lasciato il computer perché era troppo vecchio!
lines.en: Everything. The best part is they left the computer because it was too old!

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Che faccia tosta! Hanno fatto la denuncia?
lines.en: What nerve! Have they reported it?

lines.speaker: barista
lines.it: Sì, ai carabinieri. A quanto ne so, ne hanno già preso uno.
lines.en: Yes, to the carabinieri. As far as I know, they've already caught one.

model_exchanges.situation: A neighbour warns you about a scam

lines.speaker: neighbour
lines.it: Senta, stia attento: girano dei finti tecnici del gas.
lines.en: Listen, be careful: there are fake gas engineers going around.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Davvero? Come fanno?
lines.en: Really? How do they do it?

lines.speaker: neighbour
lines.it: Suonano, dicono che c'è una fuga e chiedono di entrare. Alla signora del terzo piano hanno rubato i gioielli.
lines.en: They ring, say there's a leak and ask to come in. They stole the jewellery of the lady on the third floor.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Ma è terribile! E come si riconoscono?
lines.en: That's terrible! And how do you recognise them?

lines.speaker: neighbour
lines.it: Quelli veri avvisano prima, con un cartello nell'androne. Se qualcuno suona senza preavviso, non apra e chiami il 112.
lines.en: The real ones give notice first, with a notice in the entrance hall. If someone rings without warning, don't open and call 112.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Grazie dell'avviso.
lines.en: Thanks for the warning.

model_exchanges.situation: Indifference to a local row

lines.speaker: friend
lines.it: Hai letto? Il comune ha rifatto la piazza e la gente è furiosa.
lines.en: Have you read it? The council has redone the square and people are furious.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: E allora? A me piace com'è venuta.
lines.en: So what? I like how it's turned out.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.it: Dicono che sia costata un milione!
lines.en: They say it cost a million!

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: E con ciò? Prima era un parcheggio, adesso c'è una piazza.
lines.en: So what? Before it was a car park, now there's a square.

grammar.point: hearsay with dicono che, pare che, sembra che + subjunctive
grammar.explain: To pass on news you haven't checked, use dicono che, pare che or sembra che with the subjunctive (past forms for past events).

examples.it: Pare che siano entrati dal balcone.
examples.en: Apparently they got in through the balcony.

examples.it: Dicono che sia costata un milione.
examples.en: They say it cost a million.

grammar.trap: With ha detto che (a specific person's words) use reported speech with the indicative; dicono che (rumour) prefers the subjunctive.

grammar.explain: Where English uses a passive ('my bike was stolen'), Italian prefers a third-person plural with no subject: hanno rubato, l'hanno arrestato, mi hanno rubato la bici.

examples.en: My bike's been stolen.
He's already been arrested.

grammar.trap: 'Io sono stato rubato' is wrong: rubare takes the thing, and the person is an indirect object (mi hanno rubato...).

grammar.explain: ne appears in set phrases about knowing and quantity: a quanto ne so, non ne so niente, ne hanno preso uno.

examples.it: A quanto ne so, è chiuso.
examples.en: As far as I know, it's closed.
I don't know anything about it.

grammar.trap: You'll also hear a quanto so and per quanto ne so; a quanto ne so is the most common.

grammar.explain: Outrage: Che faccia tosta! È il colmo! Ma è assurdo! È una vergogna! Indifference: E allora? E con ciò? Non mi interessa affatto.

examples.en: It's a disgrace!
I'm not interested at all.

grammar.trap: 'Chi se ne frega!' (who cares) is coarse: understand it, but don't say it to strangers or older people.

vocabulary.en: police report ('fare la denuncia' = to report a crime)
carabiniere (military police officer); 'i carabinieri' = the force
the limit ('è il colmo' = that's the last straw)

pronunciation: Long consonants carry the meaning: truffa (long ff), scippo (long pp, and sc + i is 'sh'), and furto (theft) is a different word from frutto (fruit).
carabinieri stresses -niè-: ca-ra-bi-NIÈ-ri; questura is kwe-STU-ra.

common_errors.right: Mi hanno rubato il portafoglio. / Mi hanno derubato.
common_errors.why: rubare takes the thing stolen; the victim is mi (indirect) or derubato.
'About it' is ne before the verb; esso is almost never used for things in speech.

common_errors.wrong: I carabinieri ha arrestato il ladro.
common_errors.right: I carabinieri hanno arrestato il ladro.
common_errors.why: carabinieri is plural, so the verb is too.

common_errors.wrong: Pare che sono entrati dal balcone.
common_errors.right: Pare che siano entrati dal balcone.
common_errors.why: pare che introduces hearsay: subjunctive.

common_errors.wrong: Ho fatto una denuncia contro il furto.
common_errors.right: Ho fatto la denuncia del furto.
common_errors.why: You report the theft (denuncia di); 'contro' is for a person you accuse.

units.culture: Italy has two main national police forces, the Polizia di Stato and the Carabinieri (a military corps), plus the municipal Polizia locale (still called vigili) for traffic and local rules. You can report a theft at a questura, a commissariato or a carabinieri station, and 112 is the single emergency number. Scams on older people often use fake technicians or fake police: real ones never ask you to hand over money or gold.
recycles: b2-07 (reported speech: ha detto che, mi ha chiesto se)
a2-13 (Mi hanno rubato il portafoglio; Dove posso fare la denuncia?)
b1-11 (Non ci posso credere! Ma dai!)
b1-09 (Lei imperatives: stia attento, non apra, chiami)
units.evidence: Hearing or telling local news, the learner passes on rumours with pare che / dicono che + subjunctive, uses 'hanno rubato / l'hanno arrestato' for unknown doers, and picks a fitting reaction (outrage or indifference) in the right register.
sources: P2 U10 (burglary chat: 'Il colmo è che...', 'Pensa che faccia tosta!', 'A quanto ne so, ha già fatto la denuncia in questura'; scams with fake technicians; indifference: 'E con ciò?', 'E allora?', 'Ma chi se ne frega!')
P3 U23 (legality: sporgere / presentare denuncia)
P1B U9 (pickpocket)
Proudfoot U19 ('Dicono che lei abbia...': hearsay with the subjunctive)
SLANG ('Non me ne frega niente' marked coarse in small-books notes §3)

units.title: Belonging: being a foreigner here
units.can_do: Talk about migration and integration from your own experience and others', including Italy's own emigration, and hold your view in a discussion.
situations: being asked where you're really from
a discussion about immigration with a friend
meeting other foreigners at a language school
an older Italian telling you about relatives who emigrated

frames.it: All'inizio mi sentivo un po' straniero, ma adesso mi sento a casa.
frames.en: At first I felt a bit like a foreigner, but now I feel at home.
frames.note: straniero / straniera agrees with the speaker.

frames.it: Ogni tanto ho nostalgia di casa.
frames.en: Sometimes I'm homesick.

frames.it: Pur vivendo qui da anni, ho ancora un accento straniero.
frames.en: Although I've lived here for years, I still have a foreign accent.

frames.it: Non è che non mi piaccia, è che mi manca la mia famiglia.
frames.en: It's not that I don't like it, it's that I miss my family.

frames.it: Ho incontrato qualche pregiudizio, ma non per questo penso che gli italiani siano chiusi.
frames.en: I've met some prejudice, but that doesn't make me think Italians are closed-minded.

frames.it: Tanti italiani sono emigrati in America all'inizio del Novecento.
frames.en: Many Italians emigrated to America in the early 1900s.

frames.it: L'integrazione passa dal lavoro, dalla scuola e dalla cucina.
frames.en: Integration comes through work, school and food.

frames.it: Ma di dov'è, di preciso?
frames.en: But where are you from, exactly?

model_exchanges.situation: Being asked where you're really from

lines.speaker: older woman
lines.it: Lei parla bene! Ma di dov'è, di preciso?
lines.en: You speak well! But where are you from, exactly?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Sono americano, ma vivo qui da tre anni.
lines.en: I'm American, but I've lived here for three years.

lines.speaker: older woman
lines.it: E si trova bene? Non Le manca casa?
lines.en: And do you like it here? Don't you miss home?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Ogni tanto ho nostalgia, soprattutto a Natale. Ma ormai mi sento a casa.
lines.en: Sometimes I'm homesick, especially at Christmas. But by now I feel at home.

lines.speaker: older woman
lines.it: Mio nonno è emigrato in America nel 1920. Non è mai tornato.
lines.en: My grandfather emigrated to America in 1920. He never came back.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Allora siamo pari: lui è andato là, io sono venuto qua!
lines.en: Then we're even: he went there, I came here!

model_exchanges.situation: A discussion about immigration

lines.speaker: friend
lines.it: Secondo te gli italiani sono razzisti?
lines.en: Do you think Italians are racist?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Non direi. Ho incontrato qualche pregiudizio, ma non per questo penso che siano tutti chiusi.
lines.en: I wouldn't say so. I've met some prejudice, but that doesn't make me think they're all closed-minded.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.it: Per uno straniero che arriva dall'Africa, però, è diverso.
lines.en: For a foreigner arriving from Africa, though, it's different.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Questo è vero. Io sono stato fortunato: pur essendo straniero, non mi sono mai sentito di troppo.
lines.en: That's true. I've been lucky: even though I'm a foreigner, I've never felt unwelcome.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.it: Secondo me l'integrazione passa dal lavoro e dalla scuola.
lines.en: I think integration comes through work and school.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: E dalla cucina! Il mio vicino mi ha insegnato a fare il ragù.
lines.en: And food! My neighbour taught me to make ragù.

model_exchanges.situation: Meeting another foreigner at a language school

lines.speaker: student
lines.it: Tu da quanto sei qui?
lines.en: How long have you been here?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Da due anni. E tu?
lines.en: Two years. And you?

lines.speaker: student
lines.it: Sei mesi. Non è che non mi piaccia, ma la burocrazia mi fa impazzire.
lines.en: Six months. It's not that I don't like it, but the bureaucracy drives me mad.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Ti capisco! All'inizio mi sentivo perso anch'io.
lines.en: I know what you mean! At first I felt lost too.

lines.speaker: student
lines.it: Pur studiando tutti i giorni, non capisco ancora i colleghi quando parlano veloce.
lines.en: Even though I study every day, I still don't understand my colleagues when they talk fast.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Ci vuole tempo. Vedrai che tra un anno ti sentirai a casa.
lines.en: It takes time. You'll see, in a year you'll feel at home.

grammar.explain: pur + gerund means 'although / even though' when the subject is the same in both parts of the sentence.

examples.it: Pur vivendo qui da anni, ho ancora l'accento.
examples.en: Although I've lived here for years, I still have the accent.
Although she was tired, she went out.

grammar.trap: Only with the same subject; with different subjects use anche se + indicative or benché + subjunctive.
