grammar.trap: 'Fare' and 'dare' are fine in speech but sound flat in a formal letter: an office rilascia una ricevuta, and an applicant presenta una domanda.

vocabulary.en: to carry out, to make (a payment)
to send a reminder, to chase

pronunciation: Read abbreviations in full when you read a letter aloud: art. 3 is articolo tre, c.a. is cortese attenzione; PEC is said as a word, pek.
Altresì stresses the last syllable, al-tre-SÌ; qualora stresses the middle, qua-LO-ra.

common_errors.why: Qualora always takes the subjunctive.

common_errors.wrong: Non avendo ricevuto risposta, la pratica è stata chiusa.
common_errors.right: Non avendo ricevuto risposta, ho sollecitato l'ufficio.
common_errors.why: The gerund's subject must be the main verb's subject.
Suddetto agrees with its noun.
'In accordance with' a legal text is ai sensi di; in accordo con is a calque.

units.culture: A self-declaration (autocertificazione) replaces most certificates, and public offices must accept it. For anything you may need to prove later (a deposit, a cancellation, a complaint), send a raccomandata con ricevuta di ritorno, or a PEC if both sides have one: an ordinary email carries little legal weight.
recycles: Resto in attesa di un Suo cortese riscontro (b2-11)
units.evidence: The learner fills in a self-declaration and drafts a complaint or reminder that uses qualora + subjunctive, a gerund with the right subject and two or three fixed connectors, and can explain in plain Italian what a clause in a lease or notice requires.
sources: P3 U26 ex.9 (bureaucratic letter: con la presente, a fronte di, suddetto, sono a richiederVi, altresì)
P3 U14 (nominalisation)
P3 U15 (gerundio composto; participio assoluto)
P2 U2 (formal letters)
gap: PEC, autocertificazione (P3 §5)

units.title: Media, rumour and how news is told
units.can_do: Follow and discuss news, gossip and media coverage, telling fact from claim.

frames.it: Secondo alcune fonti, il sindaco si sarebbe dimesso.
frames.en: According to some sources, the mayor has reportedly resigned.
frames.note: The conditional marks an unconfirmed claim, like English 'reportedly'.

frames.it: Il ministro avrebbe incontrato i sindacati in segreto.
frames.en: The minister allegedly met the unions in secret.

frames.it: La notizia non è stata ancora confermata.
frames.en: The news hasn't been confirmed yet.

frames.it: Ha dichiarato che non si sarebbe ricandidato.
frames.en: He declared he wouldn't stand again.

frames.it: Sarà anche vero, ma io non ci credo.
frames.en: It may well be true, but I don't believe it.

frames.it: Corre voce che chiudano il mercato coperto.
frames.en: Rumour has it they're closing the covered market.

frames.it: È una bufala che gira sui social.
frames.en: It's a hoax going round social media.

frames.it: Non solo non ha smentito, ma ha anche rilanciato.
frames.en: Not only did he not deny it, he upped the stakes.

frames.it: Il titolo diceva una cosa, l'articolo tutt'altra.
frames.en: The headline said one thing, the article something quite different.

model_exchanges.situation: the news over coffee at the bar

lines.speaker: barista
lines.it: Ha letto? Secondo il giornale, il sindaco si sarebbe dimesso.
lines.en: Have you read it? According to the paper, the mayor has reportedly resigned.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Davvero? Ieri sera al telegiornale ha dichiarato che non si sarebbe ricandidato, ma di dimissioni non parlava nessuno.
lines.en: Really? Last night on the news he said he wouldn't stand again, but nobody was talking about resigning.

lines.speaker: barista
lines.it: Eh, corre voce che ci sia sotto un'inchiesta.
lines.en: Well, rumour has it there's an investigation behind it.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Sarà anche vero, ma finché non lo confermano, io non ci credo.
lines.en: It may well be true, but until they confirm it, I don't believe it.

lines.speaker: barista
lines.it: Fa bene. Qui le voci girano più veloci dei giornali.
lines.en: Quite right. Round here rumours travel faster than the papers.

model_exchanges.situation: a rumour in a neighbourhood chat group

lines.speaker: amica
lines.it: Hai visto? Dicono che chiudano il mercato coperto per farci un parcheggio!
lines.en: Have you seen? They say they're closing the covered market to put a car park there!

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Dove l'hai letto?
lines.en: Where did you read that?

lines.speaker: amica
lines.it: Sul gruppo del quartiere. L'hanno condiviso tutti.
lines.en: In the neighbourhood group. Everyone shared it.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Mah, è una bufala che gira da mesi. Il comune l'ha già smentita.
lines.en: Well, it's a hoax that's been going round for months. The council has already denied it.

lines.speaker: amica
lines.it: Però il consigliere non solo non ha smentito, ma ha anche rilanciato con un post.
lines.en: But the councillor not only didn't deny it, he upped the stakes with a post.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Appunto: è in campagna elettorale. Prima di condividere, controlla la fonte.
lines.en: Exactly: he's campaigning. Before you share, check the source.

grammar.explain: News reports use the conditional (present or past) to pass on claims the writer hasn't verified.

examples.en: The mayor has reportedly resigned.

examples.it: Secondo i medici, il farmaco ridurrebbe i sintomi.
examples.en: According to doctors, the drug reportedly reduces symptoms.

grammar.trap: This conditional doesn't mean 'would': si sarebbe dimesso here means 'has (reportedly) resigned', not 'would have resigned'.

grammar.explain: After a past reporting verb, a future becomes the condizionale passato.

examples.it: Ha dichiarato che non si sarebbe ricandidato.
examples.en: He declared he wouldn't stand again.

examples.it: Avevano promesso che il mercato sarebbe rimasto aperto.
examples.en: They'd promised the market would stay open.

grammar.trap: English 'would' after a past verb is the past conditional in Italian: 'non si ricandiderebbe' is wrong here.

grammar.explain: Sarà anche… / avrà anche…, ma grants a point before you push back.

examples.it: Sarà anche vero, ma non ci credo.
examples.en: It may well be true, but I don't believe it.

examples.it: Avrà anche ragione, ma il tono era sbagliato.
examples.en: He may be right, but his tone was wrong.

grammar.trap: This sarà has nothing to do with the future: it means 'it may well be'.

grammar.point: corre voce / si dice che + subjunctive
grammar.explain: Phrases that pass on rumour take the subjunctive; the indicative presents the claim as fact.

examples.it: Corre voce che chiudano il mercato.
examples.en: Rumour has it they're closing the market.

examples.it: Si dice che sia stato lui.
examples.en: People say it was him.

grammar.trap: In casual speech you'll hear dicono che chiudono; at C1 choose the subjunctive when you want to keep your distance.

grammar.point: correlatives: non solo… ma anche; né… né
grammar.explain: Correlative pairs link two parts of equal weight.

examples.it: Non solo non ha smentito, ma ha anche rilanciato.
examples.en: Not only did he not deny it, he upped the stakes.

examples.it: Non l'hanno né confermato né smentito.
examples.en: They've neither confirmed nor denied it.

grammar.trap: When né… né follows the verb, the verb still needs non: non l'hanno né confermato né smentito.

vocabulary.en: to raise the stakes; to push a story further

pronunciation: Conditional endings have a long bb: sarebbe, avrebbe, avrebbero; a single b sounds like a mistake.
Telegiornale is te-le-gior-NA-le; pettegolezzo is pet-te-go-LEZ-zo, with a long ts.

common_errors.wrong: Ha detto che non si ricandiderebbe.
common_errors.right: Ha detto che non si sarebbe ricandidato.
common_errors.why: Future seen from the past is the condizionale passato.

common_errors.wrong: Secondo il giornale, il sindaco si è dimesso. (passing on an unconfirmed claim)
common_errors.right: Secondo il giornale, il sindaco si sarebbe dimesso.
common_errors.why: The conditional keeps your distance from a claim you haven't checked.

common_errors.wrong: Non l'hanno né confermato o smentito.
common_errors.right: Non l'hanno né confermato né smentito.
common_errors.why: The pair is né… né.
Anche sits right after sarà in this fixed concession.

units.culture: Local news travels through the bar, the edicola and neighbourhood WhatsApp or Facebook groups as much as through the local edition of a national daily. Hoaxes are called bufale; for anything about local services, the comune's own website and its official social accounts are the quickest way to check.
recycles: A quanto ne so, l'hanno già arrestato. (b2-08)
Ha detto che il giorno dopo sarebbe stato chiuso. (b2-07)
units.evidence: Retelling a news item or rumour, the learner chooses between indicative (fact) and conditional or subjunctive (claim), uses the condizionale passato for a future reported from the past, and concedes with sarà anche… ma.
sources: P3 U11 (TV; Carosello)
P3 U12 (gossip; passive)
P3 U16 (future in the past; non solo… ma anche)
P2 U9–U10 (headlines; reported speech)
Proudfoot U17, U20, U21 (conditional for rumour)
P3 transcripts §3 (journalistic conditional)

units.title: The neighbourhood and the environment
units.can_do: Take part in neighbourhood and environmental discussions: building meetings, local rules, waste, and what should be done.
situations: a dispute about noise or rubbish

frames.it: All'assemblea condominiale si è deciso di rifare la facciata.
frames.en: At the residents' meeting it was decided to redo the façade.

frames.it: Propongo che le spese vengano divise in base ai millesimi.
frames.en: I propose the costs be split according to each flat's share.

frames.it: Mi oppongo: non c'è nessuno che possa garantire i tempi.
frames.en: I object: there's nobody who can guarantee the timing.

frames.it: Cerchiamo qualcuno che si occupi del giardino.
frames.en: We're looking for someone to look after the garden.

frames.it: Il signore del terzo piano, al quale ho già scritto due volte, continua a fare rumore di notte.
frames.en: The man on the third floor, whom I've already written to twice, keeps making noise at night.

frames.it: I rifiuti ingombranti vanno portati all'isola ecologica.
frames.en: Bulky waste has to be taken to the recycling centre.

frames.it: Le spiagge dovrebbero essere ripulite ogni settimana.
frames.en: The beaches should be cleaned every week.

frames.it: Chi non rispetta il regolamento verrà multato.
frames.en: Anyone who breaks the rules will be fined.

frames.it: Il comune, il cui bilancio è in rosso, non ha fondi.
frames.en: The council, whose budget is in the red, has no funds.

model_exchanges.situation: a residents' meeting about the façade

lines.speaker: amministratore
lines.it: Passiamo al terzo punto: il preventivo per la facciata.
lines.en: Let's move on to item three: the quote for the façade.

lines.speaker: condomina
lines.it: Io sono contraria. Abbiamo appena pagato l'ascensore.
lines.en: I'm against it. We've just paid for the lift.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Capisco, però i lavori vanno fatti prima che cada qualche pezzo. Propongo che le spese vengano divise in due rate.
lines.en: I understand, but the work has to be done before bits start falling off. I propose the costs be split into two instalments.

lines.speaker: amministratore
lines.it: Mi sembra ragionevole. Mettiamo ai voti?
lines.en: That seems reasonable. Shall we vote?

lines.speaker: condomina
lines.it: Va bene, ma cerchiamo un'impresa che dia garanzie sui tempi.
lines.en: All right, but let's find a firm that guarantees the timing.

lines.speaker: amministratore
lines.it: Approvato a maggioranza: si è deciso di rifare la facciata in primavera.
lines.en: Approved by majority: it's been decided to redo the façade in spring.

model_exchanges.situation: a neighbour complains about rubbish by the door

lines.speaker: vicino
lines.it: Scusi, quel divano davanti al portone è suo?
lines.en: Excuse me, is that sofa in front of the main door yours?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: No, ma l'ho visto anch'io. I rifiuti ingombranti vanno portati all'isola ecologica, oppure si prenota il ritiro a domicilio.
lines.en: No, but I've seen it too. Bulky waste has to be taken to the recycling centre, or you book a collection from your home.

lines.speaker: vicino
lines.it: Lo so, lo so. È del signore del secondo piano, al quale l'ho già detto mille volte.
lines.en: I know, I know. It belongs to the man on the second floor, whom I've already told a thousand times.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Allora segnaliamolo all'amministratore. Chi non rispetta il regolamento rischia una multa.
lines.en: Then let's report it to the building manager. Anyone who breaks the rules risks a fine.

lines.speaker: vicino
lines.it: Ha ragione. Gli scrive Lei? Lei scrive meglio di me!
lines.en: You're right. Will you write to him? You write better than I do!

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Va bene, ci penso io.
lines.en: All right, I'll do it.

grammar.explain: Il quale (la quale, i quali, le quali) can replace cui after a preposition to make clear who you mean; il cui means 'whose', and its article agrees with the thing owned.

examples.it: Il signore, al quale ho scritto, non ha risposto.
examples.en: The man, whom I wrote to, hasn't replied.

examples.it: Il comune, il cui bilancio è in rosso, non ha fondi.
examples.en: The council, whose budget is in the red, has no funds.

examples.it: Una vicina, la cui figlia studia a Bologna, mi ha aiutato.
examples.en: A neighbour whose daughter studies in Bologna helped me.

grammar.trap: In il cui the article matches the thing owned, not the owner (la città, il cui sindaco…), and 'che il suo bilancio' is never right.

grammar.point: subjunctive in relatives that set a requirement
grammar.explain: When you describe a person or thing you're looking for, rather than one that exists, the relative clause takes the subjunctive.

examples.it: Cerchiamo qualcuno che si occupi del giardino.
examples.en: We're looking for someone to look after the garden.

examples.it: Non c'è nessuno che possa garantire i tempi.
examples.en: There's nobody who can guarantee the timing.

examples.it: Abbiamo trovato un giardiniere che lavora bene.
examples.en: We've found a gardener who works well. (exists: indicative)

grammar.trap: English gives no signal; in Italian the subjunctive is what tells your listener the person isn't found yet.

grammar.point: the passive with modals, venire and andare
grammar.explain: Rules are stated with dovere / potere + essere + participle, with venire (often in the future) and with andare + participle.

examples.en: The beaches should be cleaned.

examples.it: Chi non rispetta il regolamento verrà multato.
examples.en: Anyone who breaks the rules will be fined.

examples.it: I rifiuti vanno portati all'isola ecologica.
examples.en: Waste has to be taken to the recycling centre.

grammar.trap: Venire works only in simple tenses: 'è venuto multato' is wrong; say è stato multato.

grammar.point: si in decisions; propongo che + subjunctive
grammar.explain: Meetings report decisions with si (si è deciso di…) and make proposals with propongo che + subjunctive.

examples.it: Si è deciso di rifare la facciata.
examples.en: It was decided to redo the façade.

examples.it: Propongo che le spese vengano divise.
examples.en: I propose the costs be split.

grammar.trap: Si in compound tenses takes essere: si è deciso, never si ha deciso.

vocabulary.en: each flat's share of a building (in thousandths)
to look after, to deal with

pronunciation: Condomino stresses the second syllable, con-DÒ-mi-no, unlike English 'condominium'; amministratore keeps both doubles, am-mi-ni-stra-TO-re.
Isola stresses the first syllable, Ì-so-la; ecologica is e-co-LÒ-gi-ca.

common_errors.wrong: Il comune che il suo bilancio è in rosso…
common_errors.right: Il comune, il cui bilancio è in rosso…
common_errors.why: 'Whose' is il cui (article agreeing with bilancio).

common_errors.wrong: Cerchiamo qualcuno che si occupa del giardino.
common_errors.right: Cerchiamo qualcuno che si occupi del giardino.
common_errors.why: Nobody specific yet, so the subjunctive.

common_errors.wrong: Si ha deciso di rifare la facciata.
common_errors.right: Si è deciso di rifare la facciata.
common_errors.why: Si constructions take essere in compound tenses.

common_errors.wrong: I rifiuti ingombranti vanno portato all'isola ecologica.
common_errors.right: I rifiuti ingombranti vanno portati all'isola ecologica.
common_errors.why: The participle agrees with rifiuti.

units.culture: In a condominio, shared costs are decided at the assemblea condominiale and split by millesimi; tenants usually pay day-to-day running costs and owners the major works, though owners often vote on both. Sorting rules and collection days are set by each comune and enforced with fines, so get the local calendar (and the number for bulky-waste collection) as soon as you move in.
recycles: b2-12 (holding your own in a discussion)
units.evidence: In a meeting or a dispute, the learner proposes with propongo che + subjunctive, states a requirement with a subjunctive relative (qualcuno che si occupi), cites a rule with va / vanno + participle or verrà + participle, and uses il quale / il cui to say exactly who is meant.
sources: P3 U13 (environment; il quale / il cui; subjunctive in relatives; passive with modals; andare / venire)
P2 U7 (environment; raccolta differenziata)
Proudfoot U19 (restricted relative clauses)
gap: condominium meetings (P3 §5)

units.title: Food, wine and the craft of producers
units.can_do: Talk with producers, wine sellers and cooks about origin, method and quality, and discuss Made in Italy and its imitations.
situations: a wine tasting at a cantina

frames.it: Da dove provengono questi pomodori?
frames.en: Where do these tomatoes come from?

frames.it: È un olio extravergine del frantoio qui vicino, spremuto a freddo.
frames.en: It's extra-virgin olive oil from the mill nearby, cold-pressed.

frames.it: La stagionatura dura almeno ventiquattro mesi.
frames.en: It's aged for at least twenty-four months.

frames.it: Senza conservanti né coloranti.
frames.en: No preservatives or colourings.

frames.it: Questo vino, pur essendo giovane, è già molto equilibrato.
frames.en: This wine, though young, is already very balanced.

frames.it: Ha un retrogusto amarognolo che mi piace molto.
frames.en: It has a slightly bitter aftertaste that I really like.

frames.it: Il primo assaggio è stato un po' deludente, ma poi si è aperto.
frames.en: The first taste was a bit disappointing, but then it opened up.

frames.it: All'estero vendono un sacco di prodotti che sembrano italiani senza esserlo.
frames.en: Abroad they sell loads of products that look Italian without being so.

frames.it: Per un vero buongustaio, la differenza si sente.
frames.en: For a real gourmet, you can taste the difference.

model_exchanges.situation: a tasting at a small cantina

lines.speaker: produttrice
lines.it: Questo è il nostro rosso giovane, vendemmia dell'anno scorso.
lines.en: This is our young red, from last year's harvest.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Pur essendo giovane, è già molto equilibrato. Che vitigno è?
lines.en: Though it's young, it's already very balanced. What grape is it?

lines.speaker: produttrice
lines.it: Sangiovese in purezza, da vigne di trent'anni.
lines.en: Pure Sangiovese, from thirty-year-old vines.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Ha un retrogusto leggermente amaro. È normale?
lines.en: It has a slightly bitter aftertaste. Is that normal?

lines.speaker: produttrice
lines.it: Sì, sono i tannini. Tra un paio d'anni si ammorbidisce.
lines.en: Yes, that's the tannins. In a couple of years it'll soften.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Allora ne prendo due bottiglie: una da bere subito e una da dimenticare in cantina.
lines.en: Then I'll take two bottles: one to drink now and one to forget in the cellar.

model_exchanges.situation: a cheese producer at a market stall

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Da dove proviene questo pecorino?
lines.en: Where does this pecorino come from?

lines.speaker: formaggiaio
lines.it: Da un caseificio a dieci chilometri da qui. Latte crudo, lavorazione artigianale.
lines.en: From a dairy ten kilometres from here. Raw milk, made by hand.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: E quanto dura la stagionatura?
lines.en: And how long is it aged?

lines.speaker: formaggiaio
lines.it: Questo almeno dodici mesi. Quello lì, stagionato in grotta, ventiquattro.
lines.en: This one at least twelve months. That one there, aged in a cave, twenty-four.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: All'estero si trova un sacco di formaggio che sembra italiano senza esserlo.
lines.en: Abroad you find loads of cheese that looks Italian without being so.

lines.speaker: formaggiaio
lines.it: Eh, lo so. Ma per un vero buongustaio la differenza si sente. Assaggi!
lines.en: Oh, I know. But for a real gourmet you can taste the difference. Try some!

grammar.point: present participles as adjectives and nouns
grammar.explain: Forms in -ante / -ente work as adjectives (deludente, rinfrescante) or as nouns (i conservanti, i coloranti).

examples.it: Il primo assaggio è stato deludente.
examples.en: The first taste was disappointing.
products from Puglia
without preservatives

grammar.trap: Don't use them for English -ing actions: 'the man selling cheese' is l'uomo che vende il formaggio, not l'uomo vendente.

grammar.explain: A past participle describes the result of a process and agrees with its noun.

examples.en: cold-pressed oil
aged pecorino, smoked mozzarella

grammar.trap: It agrees like any adjective: ricotta stagionata, pomodori secchi, not ricotta stagionato.

grammar.explain: Pur + gerund means 'although' when both parts share a subject; senza + infinitive means 'without -ing'.

examples.en: Though it's young, it's balanced.
They look Italian without being so.

grammar.trap: 'Without being' is senza essere, never senza essendo.

grammar.explain: Producers name each step with a noun made from a verb: stagionare → la stagionatura, lavorare → la lavorazione, invecchiare → l'invecchiamento.

examples.en: The ageing takes two years.

examples.it: La lavorazione è ancora a mano.
examples.en: It's still made by hand.

grammar.trap: The ending isn't predictable (-tura, -zione, -mento), so learn each noun with its article.

pronunciation: Gn in vigna, vigneto and vitigno is the 'ny' sound of 'canyon', always held long: vi-TI-gno.
Caseificio has five syllables, ca-se-i-FI-cio; prelibatezza is pre-li-ba-TEZ-za with a long ts.

common_errors.why: In a neutral question the preposition and question word come first; the other order is only an echo question.
Senza takes the infinitive; lo stands for 'Italian'.
The participle agrees with the noun.
It's one fixed word, extravergine.

units.culture: DOP, IGP, DOC and DOCG on a label are legal guarantees of origin and method, and 'Italian sounding' products abroad imitate them with flags and Italian names. At markets and cantine it's normal to ask where something comes from and how it's made, and producers enjoy explaining; ask before tasting, and if you've tasted a lot, buy something.
units.evidence: At a stall or tasting, the learner asks about origin and method, describes a product with agreeing participles (stagionato, spremuto a freddo) and present participles (deludente), and gives a balanced judgement with pur + gerund.
sources: P3 U14 (Made in Italy; Italian Sounding; present and past participles; nominalisation)
P1B U8 culture (DOP)
P2 U9 (nouns from verbs)
P2 U11 (participles)

units.title: History and memory
units.can_do: Tell history and family memory in the literary past, and discuss contested history as a debate.

frames.it: Garibaldi sbarcò a Marsala nel 1860.
frames.en: Garibaldi landed at Marsala in 1860.

frames.it: Il 17 marzo 1861 fu proclamato il Regno d'Italia.
frames.en: The Kingdom of Italy was proclaimed on 17 March 1861.

frames.it: Dopo che ebbero firmato l'armistizio, le truppe si ritirarono.
frames.en: After they had signed the armistice, the troops withdrew.

frames.it: Mio nonno partì per l'Argentina nel 1949 e non tornò più.
frames.en: My grandfather left for Argentina in 1949 and never came back.

frames.it: Mia nonna raccontava che durante la guerra non c'era niente da mangiare.
frames.en: My grandmother used to say that during the war there was nothing to eat.

frames.it: Se non fossero emigrati, oggi non avrei parenti in Argentina.
frames.en: If they hadn't emigrated, I wouldn't have relatives in Argentina today.

frames.it: Quando tornò dopo dieci anni, successe un quarantotto.
frames.en: When he came back after ten years, all hell broke loose.
frames.note: Succedere (or fare) un quarantotto comes from the uprisings of 1848.

frames.it: Secondo alcuni storici, la questione meridionale nacque con l'Unità.
frames.en: According to some historians, the Southern Question was born with Unification.

frames.it: È una versione dei fatti, non l'unica.
frames.en: It's one version of events, not the only one.

model_exchanges.situation: an older neighbour's memories

lines.speaker: signora
lines.it: Mio padre partì per l'America nel '49, con una valigia di cartone.
lines.en: My father left for America in '49, with a cardboard suitcase.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: E Lei rimase qui con Sua madre?
lines.en: And you stayed here with your mother?

lines.speaker: signora
lines.it: Sì. Dopo che fu partito, mia madre mandò avanti la bottega da sola. Non c'era niente, ma ce la cavavamo.
lines.en: Yes. After he had gone, my mother ran the shop on her own. There was nothing, but we got by.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Anche la famiglia di mia nonna emigrò. Se non fossero partiti, chissà dove sarei nato.
lines.en: My grandmother's family emigrated too. If they hadn't left, who knows where I'd have been born.

lines.speaker: signora
lines.it: Eh, la storia ci porta dove vuole. Quando tornò mio padre, dopo dieci anni, successe un quarantotto: tutto il paese in piazza!
lines.en: Well, history takes us where it likes. When my father came back after ten years, all hell broke loose: the whole village in the square!

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Che bella storia. Me la racconterà ancora?
lines.en: What a lovely story. Will you tell it to me again?

model_exchanges.situation: a debate at a Risorgimento museum

lines.speaker: amico
lines.it: Qui al museo raccontano l'Unità come una festa. A casa mia, al Sud, la raccontano diversamente.
lines.en: Here at the museum they tell Unification as a celebration. At home, in the South, they tell it differently.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: In che senso?
lines.en: In what sense?

lines.speaker: amico
lines.it: Secondo alcuni storici, la questione meridionale nacque proprio con l'Unità: tasse, leva obbligatoria, brigantaggio.
lines.en: According to some historians, the Southern Question was born with Unification itself: taxes, conscription, brigandage.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: E secondo altri?
lines.en: And according to others?

lines.speaker: amico
lines.it: Che il Sud era già povero prima. È un dibattito ancora aperto.
lines.en: That the South was already poor before. It's still an open debate.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Quindi quella del museo è una versione dei fatti, non l'unica.
lines.en: So the museum's is one version of events, not the only one.

grammar.explain: For history and family stories set long ago, books and many speakers use the passato remoto; learn the common irregular forms.

examples.it: sbarcò, partì, tornò, fu, ebbe, nacque, venne, fece, disse, successe
examples.en: landed, left, returned, was, had, was born, came, did, said, happened
Garibaldi landed at Marsala in 1860.

grammar.trap: Watch the person: partì is he/she left, partii is I left. In everyday speech in much of Italy the passato prossimo still covers recent events.

grammar.explain: In written narrative, after dopo che, (non) appena or quando with a passato remoto in the main clause, the earlier action is ebbi / fui + past participle.

examples.it: Dopo che ebbero firmato l'armistizio, le truppe si ritirarono.
examples.en: After they had signed the armistice, the troops withdrew.

examples.it: Appena fu arrivato, scrisse alla moglie.
examples.en: As soon as he had arrived, he wrote to his wife.

grammar.trap: You only need to recognise it; when you speak, say dopo aver firmato or dopo che avevano firmato.

grammar.explain: Se + congiuntivo trapassato imagines a past that didn't happen; the result can be past (condizionale passato) or present (condizionale).

examples.it: Se non fossero emigrati, oggi non avrei parenti in Argentina.
examples.en: If they hadn't emigrated, I wouldn't have relatives in Argentina today.

examples.it: Se fossero rimasti, la storia della famiglia sarebbe stata diversa.
examples.en: If they'd stayed, the family's story would have been different.

grammar.trap: Never the conditional after se: 'se non sarebbero emigrati' is wrong.

grammar.explain: Passato remoto for the events, imperfetto for background and habits, trapassato for what had happened before.

examples.it: Mia nonna raccontava che durante la guerra non c'era niente da mangiare.
examples.en: My grandmother used to say there was nothing to eat during the war.

examples.it: Quando tornò, il paese era cambiato.
examples.en: When he came back, the village had changed.

grammar.trap: Remoto vs imperfetto works exactly like passato prossimo vs imperfetto: events against background.

vocabulary.en: for all hell to break loose

pronunciation: Regular third-person remoto forms stress the final vowel: sbarcò, partì, tornò; without it, sbarco means 'I land'.
The plural remoto stresses before -ro: par-TÌ-ro-no, tor-NA-ro-no, NAC-que-ro.

common_errors.why: A single completed event takes the remoto (or prossimo), not the imperfetto.
Se takes the congiuntivo trapassato for a past that didn't happen.
Partii is 'I left'; he left is partì.

common_errors.right: Dopo aver firmato l'armistizio… / Dopo che ebbero firmato l'armistizio…
common_errors.why: Dopo needs a past infinitive or a full clause.

units.culture: Italian history is still argued over at the table: the Risorgimento, the Southern Question, Fascism and the Resistance mean different things in different families and regions. Ask and listen first, and offer your own view as one view (secondo me, secondo alcuni storici). 25 April (Liberation Day) and 2 June (Republic Day) are public holidays with local ceremonies.
units.evidence: Retelling a family memory or a piece of history, the learner keeps events in the passato remoto (or prossimo) and background in the imperfetto, builds a correct se + congiuntivo trapassato counterfactual, and frames a contested claim as one view.
sources: P3 U18 (passato remoto; trapassato remoto; Leonardo biography)
P3 U20 (Risorgimento; the Southern Question as a debate; congiuntivo trapassato; succedere un quarantotto)
P2 U4 (passato remoto; Garibaldi; trapassato remoto)
Proudfoot U12 (trapassato remoto: recognise only)

units.title: Faith, festivals and traditions
units.can_do: Take part in festivals and religious life as a guest, understand traditions and superstitions, and offer the right wishes.

frames.it: Che siate felici!
frames.en: May you be happy!

frames.it: Viva gli sposi!
frames.en: Here's to the bride and groom!

frames.it: Ci tengo a ringraziarvi per l'invito.
frames.en: I really want to thank you for the invitation.

frames.it: Magari fosse sempre così!
frames.en: If only it were always like this!

frames.it: Voglia il cielo che non piova durante la processione!
frames.en: Heaven grant it doesn't rain during the procession!

frames.it: Non ci credo, ma per scaramanzia tocco ferro.
frames.en: I don't believe in it, but I touch wood just in case.
frames.note: Italians touch iron (ferro), not wood.

frames.it: Dammi retta: vacci presto, sennò non trovi posto.
frames.en: Listen to me: go early, or you won't find a spot.

frames.it: Ne vale la pena, anche se c'è una folla pazzesca.
frames.en: It's worth it, even if there's a huge crowd.

frames.it: Il corteo storico sfila per il centro.
frames.en: The historical parade marches through the centre.

frames.it: Che la Madonna ti accompagni.
frames.en: May Our Lady go with you.

model_exchanges.situation: a neighbour invites you to the patron-saint festa

lines.speaker: vicina
lines.it: Domenica c'è la festa del patrono. Vieni a vedere la processione?
lines.en: On Sunday it's the patron saint's festa. Are you coming to see the procession?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Volentieri! A che ora passa?
lines.en: Gladly! What time does it come past?

lines.speaker: vicina
lines.it: Esce dalla chiesa alle sei. Dammi retta: vacci presto, sennò non trovi posto in piazza.
lines.en: It leaves the church at six. Listen to me: go early, or you won't find a spot in the square.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: E dopo c'è anche la sagra?
lines.en: And afterwards is there the food festival too?

lines.speaker: vicina
lines.it: Sì, e i fuochi a mezzanotte. Voglia il cielo che non piova, come l'anno scorso!
lines.en: Yes, and fireworks at midnight. Heaven grant it doesn't rain, like last year!

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Tocchiamo ferro!
lines.en: Touch wood!

lines.speaker: vicina
lines.it: Ecco, vedo che stai diventando dei nostri!
lines.en: There you go, I can see you're becoming one of us!

model_exchanges.situation: congratulating a couple at their wedding

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Ci tengo a ringraziarvi per l'invito: è il mio primo matrimonio italiano.
lines.en: I really want to thank you for the invitation: it's my first Italian wedding.

lines.speaker: sposo
lines.it: Grazie a te di essere venuto! Hai preso i confetti?
lines.en: Thank you for coming! Have you had some sugared almonds?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Sì, cinque, come mi hanno spiegato. Che siate felici!
lines.en: Yes, five, as they explained to me. May you be happy!

lines.speaker: sposa
lines.it: Grazie! Magari fosse sempre così, tutti insieme.
lines.en: Thank you! If only it were always like this, everyone together.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Viva gli sposi!
lines.en: Here's to the bride and groom!

grammar.explain: To wish something for someone, Italian uses che + present subjunctive, magari + imperfect subjunctive, or set formulas such as voglia il cielo che.

examples.en: May you be happy!
If only it were always like this!

examples.it: Voglia il cielo che non piova!
examples.en: Heaven grant it doesn't rain!

grammar.trap: There's no verb for 'may' here, just che + subjunctive; and magari + subjunctive is a wish ('if only'), while magari on its own often means 'maybe'.

grammar.explain: With tu, noi and voi, pronouns attach to the imperative, and after da', di', fa', sta' and va' the consonant doubles; with Lei they go before.

examples.it: Dammi retta. / Vacci presto. / Fammi sapere.
examples.en: Listen to me. / Go early. / Let me know.

examples.it: Non andarci da solo. / Non ci andare da solo.
examples.en: Don't go there on your own.
Go early, madam.

grammar.trap: Lei imperatives never take attached pronouns: ci vada, not vadaci.

grammar.explain: Several everyday expressions are built with ci or ne and can't be translated word for word.

examples.en: I really want to thank you.
It's worth it.
I can't take any more.

grammar.trap: Tenerci needs a before an infinitive: ci tengo a dirtelo, not ci tengo di dirtelo.

vocabulary.en: to care about, to really want to

pronunciation: Wishes carry a strong stress on the verb and fall at the end: che SIA-te FE-li-ci!; ma-GA-ri FOS-se…
S before a voiced consonant sounds like z: sbandieratori is zban-die-ra-TO-ri, and the same in sbarcare and sbagliare.

common_errors.why: A wish takes the subjunctive.

common_errors.wrong: Magari è sempre così! (as a wish)
common_errors.why: 'If only' is magari + imperfect subjunctive.
With Lei the pronoun goes before the verb.
Italians touch iron.

units.culture: As a guest at a church wedding, baptism or festa, nobody expects you to be religious, only to respect the moment: dress modestly in church, stay quiet during mass and follow what others do. Guests at weddings and baptisms receive confetti, in an odd number (usually five), in a bomboniera; the usual gift is money in a card or something from the couple's list.
units.evidence: At a festa or a family celebration, the learner offers a fitting wish with che + subjunctive or magari, uses ci tengo a and ne vale la pena naturally, and gives or follows advice with imperatives that carry pronouns.
sources: P3 U21 (religion and superstition; imperative with pronouns; ci / ne)
P3 U23 (optative: che siate felici, voglia il cielo, magari)
P3 U30 (festivals; corteo storico; sbandieratori)
P1a U5 culture (Christmas)
Proudfoot U18 (confetti at baptisms)

units.title: Theatre, cinema and music
units.can_do: Discuss performances, films and music in depth, recounting what artists said and how a work was made.
functions: describe a performance and its effect

frames.it: Il regista ha detto che non avrebbe mai girato un seguito.
frames.en: The director said he would never shoot a sequel.

frames.it: Ci ha chiesto se avessimo mai visto Pirandello in dialetto.
frames.en: He asked us whether we'd ever seen Pirandello in dialect.

frames.it: Era talmente bravo che il pubblico si è alzato in piedi.
frames.en: He was so good that the audience stood up.

frames.it: Il film era così lento da far addormentare mezza sala.
frames.en: The film was so slow it sent half the audience to sleep.

frames.it: Non appena si è aperto il sipario, è calato il silenzio.
frames.en: As soon as the curtain rose, silence fell.

frames.it: Per poco non perdevo l'inizio!
frames.en: I nearly missed the beginning!
frames.note: Colloquial imperfetto; also per poco non ho perso l'inizio. The non doesn't make it negative.

frames.it: Non me ne vado finché non finiscono gli applausi.
frames.en: I'm not leaving until the applause ends.

frames.it: Questo ruolo gli calza come un guanto.
frames.en: This role fits him like a glove.

frames.it: Lo danno in lingua originale con i sottotitoli?
frames.en: Is it showing in the original language with subtitles?

model_exchanges.situation: leaving the theatre with a friend

lines.speaker: amica
lines.it: Allora, ti è piaciuto?
lines.en: So, did you like it?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Moltissimo. Il protagonista era talmente bravo che alla fine il pubblico si è alzato in piedi.
lines.en: Very much. The lead was so good that at the end the audience stood up.

lines.speaker: amica
lines.it: Quel ruolo gli calza come un guanto. Ma tu sei arrivato all'ultimo momento!
lines.en: That role fits him like a glove. But you got here at the last minute!

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Lo so, per poco non perdevo l'inizio. Non appena mi sono seduto, si è aperto il sipario.
lines.en: I know, I nearly missed the beginning. As soon as I sat down, the curtain went up.

lines.speaker: amica
lines.it: E il secondo atto? A me è sembrato un po' lungo.
lines.en: And the second act? It felt a bit long to me.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Un po', ma non tanto da annoiarmi.
lines.en: A bit, but not so much that I got bored.

model_exchanges.situation: passing on a director's interview

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Hai letto l'intervista al regista? Ha detto che non avrebbe mai girato un seguito.
lines.en: Did you read the interview with the director? He said he'd never shoot a sequel.

lines.speaker: amico
lines.it: Lo dicono tutti! E cos'altro ha detto?
lines.en: They all say that! What else did he say?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Che aveva scelto attori non professionisti perché voleva facce vere. E ha chiesto ai giornalisti se avessero mai visto un film senza musica.
lines.en: That he'd chosen non-professional actors because he wanted real faces. And he asked the journalists whether they'd ever seen a film without music.

lines.speaker: amico
lines.it: Che provocatore. Lo danno in lingua originale?
lines.en: What a provocateur. Is it showing in the original language?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Sì, è in siciliano con i sottotitoli.
lines.en: Yes, it's in Sicilian with subtitles.

grammar.point: reported speech with all its shifts
grammar.explain: After a past reporting verb, shift every tense, person and time word back: present → imperfetto, passato prossimo → trapassato, future → condizionale passato, domani → il giorno dopo.

examples.it: «Non girerò mai un seguito.» → Ha detto che non avrebbe mai girato un seguito.
examples.en: 'I'll never shoot a sequel.' → He said he'd never shoot a sequel.

examples.it: «Ho scelto attori non professionisti.» → Ha detto che aveva scelto attori non professionisti.
examples.en: 'I chose non-professional actors.' → He said he'd chosen non-professional actors.

grammar.trap: The commonest slip is the future: 'ha detto che girerebbe' is wrong.

grammar.explain: Reported yes/no and wh- questions take the subjunctive in careful speech and writing (the indicative in casual speech), with se for yes/no.

examples.it: Ci ha chiesto se avessimo mai visto Pirandello.
examples.en: He asked us whether we'd ever seen Pirandello.

examples.it: Mi domando perché abbiano tagliato quella scena.
examples.en: I wonder why they cut that scene.

grammar.trap: A reported yes/no question needs se, not che: mi ha chiesto se avessi visto…

grammar.point: result clauses: talmente… che, così… da
grammar.explain: Talmente / così / tanto… che + indicative states a result; così… da + infinitive does the same more compactly.

examples.it: Era talmente bravo che il pubblico si è alzato.
examples.en: He was so good that the audience stood up.

examples.it: Era così lento da far addormentare la sala.
examples.en: It was so slow it sent the audience to sleep.

grammar.trap: Che takes a full clause, da an infinitive: così stanco che non riuscivo or così stanco da non riuscire, never così stanco che non riuscire.

grammar.explain: After per poco, finché, a meno che and some comparisons, Italian adds a non that doesn't make the sentence negative.

examples.en: I nearly missed the beginning. (I didn't miss it)

examples.it: Resto finché non finiscono gli applausi.
examples.en: I'm staying until the applause ends.

examples.it: Costava più di quanto non pensassi.
examples.en: It cost more than I thought.

grammar.trap: Don't hear it as a negative: per poco non perdevo means you made it in time.

grammar.explain: Fixed similes and adjective pairs make a description vivid.

examples.it: calzare come un guanto; chiaro come il sole
examples.en: fit like a glove; crystal clear

examples.it: La sala era piena zeppa. Ero stanco morto.
examples.en: The hall was packed. I was dead tired.

grammar.trap: They're fixed: piena zeppa, not molto zeppa, and English similes rarely translate word for word.

vocabulary.en: they're showing (from dare: a film, a play)

pronunciation: Applausi has a long pp, ap-PLAU-si; sipario has a single p, si-PA-rio.
Tournée is said as in French, tur-NÉ; regista is re-JI-sta, with a soft g.

common_errors.wrong: Ha detto che non girerebbe mai un seguito.
common_errors.right: Ha detto che non avrebbe mai girato un seguito.
common_errors.why: A future reported from the past is the condizionale passato.
The fixed structure is per poco non; without non it sounds wrong.

common_errors.wrong: Era così lento che far addormentare la sala.
common_errors.right: Era così lento da far addormentare la sala.
common_errors.why: Da + infinitive, or che + a full clause.

common_errors.wrong: Ci ha chiesto che avevamo visto Pirandello.
common_errors.right: Ci ha chiesto se avessimo visto Pirandello.
common_errors.why: A reported yes/no question is introduced by se.

units.culture: Most films in Italian cinemas are dubbed; look for 'v.o.' or 'versione originale sottotitolata' if you want the original. Theatres sell season tickets (abbonamenti) for a series of shows, the cheapest seats are high up in the galleria or loggione, and at the opera loud approval and booing (i fischi) are both part of the tradition.
recycles: Mi sembra di averlo già letto. (b2-10)
units.evidence: Recounting a show or an interview, the learner shifts tenses, persons and time words correctly (including the condizionale passato), reports questions with se + subjunctive, and uses a result clause or a pleonastic non without hesitation.
sources: P3 U25 (cinema; subjunctive after conjunctions)
P3 U27 (negation; pleonastic non; result clauses)
P3 U28 (theatre; implicit clauses)
P3 U29 (music; reported speech; indirect questions; similes and intensified adjectives)

units.title: How Italians really talk: dialect, markers and idioms
units.can_do: Follow fast colloquial and regional speech, recognise dialect features, and use discourse markers and idioms naturally.

frames.it: È l'accento che ti frega!
frames.en: It's the accent that gives you away!
frames.note: Informal; with strangers say È l'accento che ti tradisce.

frames.it: Non è che non voglia venire, è che sono stanco morto.
frames.en: It's not that I don't want to come, it's that I'm dead tired.

frames.it: Insomma, diciamo che non è andata benissimo.
frames.en: Well, let's say it didn't go brilliantly.

frames.it: Ce l'hai con me?
frames.en: Are you angry with me?

frames.it: Ce l'ho messa tutta, ma non ce l'ho fatta.
frames.en: I gave it my all, but I didn't make it.

frames.it: Non te la prendere, scherzava.
frames.en: Don't take it personally, he was joking.

frames.it: Ormai è andata: me ne devo fare una ragione.
frames.en: It's done now: I'll have to come to terms with it.

frames.it: Me la sono vista brutta.
frames.en: I had a close call.

frames.it: A Roma dicono «daje!» per dire «dai!».
frames.en: In Rome they say 'daje!' for 'come on!'.

frames.it: Nun ce pensà, daje!
frames.en: Don't think about it, come on! (Roman)

model_exchanges.situation: consoling a friend after a bad day, Roman style

lines.speaker: amico
lines.it: Allora, com'è andato il colloquio?
lines.en: So, how did the interview go?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Mah, insomma… diciamo che non è andato benissimo. Ce l'ho messa tutta, ma non ce l'ho fatta.
lines.en: Well… let's say it didn't go brilliantly. I gave it my all, but I didn't make it.

lines.speaker: amico
lines.it: Ma va', non te la prendere. Ne trovi un altro.
lines.en: Come off it, don't take it to heart. You'll find another one.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Lo so. È che quando sono nervoso perdo le parole.
lines.en: I know. It's just that when I'm nervous I lose my words.

lines.speaker: amico
lines.it: E vabbè, capita a tutti. Nun ce pensà, daje! Stasera offro io.
lines.en: Oh well, it happens to everyone. Don't think about it, come on! Tonight's on me.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Daje!
lines.en: Go on, then!

model_exchanges.situation: a Roman greengrocer at the market

lines.speaker: fruttivendolo
lines.it: Che ve do, signò? 'Ste fragole so' bbone oggi!
lines.en: What can I get you, madam? These strawberries are good today! (Roman)

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Scusi, non ho capito bene: «so' bbone»?
lines.en: Sorry, I didn't quite catch that: 'so' bbone'?

lines.speaker: fruttivendolo
lines.it: Ah, scusi! Sono buone, buonissime. Qui parliamo così.
lines.en: Ah, sorry! They're good, very good. That's how we talk here.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Ho capito! Allora ne prendo mezzo chilo. Lei è romano da generazioni?
lines.en: Got it! Then I'll take half a kilo. Have you been Roman for generations?

lines.speaker: fruttivendolo
lines.it: Romano de Roma! E Lei di dov'è? È l'accento che La frega, sa!
lines.en: Roman born and bred! And where are you from? It's the accent that gives you away, you know!

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Eh, lo so. Ci sto lavorando!
lines.en: Ah, I know. I'm working on it!

grammar.explain: To focus one element, Italian uses è + X + che (or è + X + a + infinitive), and non è che… è che… to correct an assumption.

examples.it: È l'accento che ti frega. / È l'accento a fregarti.
examples.en: It's the accent that gives you away.

examples.it: Non è che non voglia, è che sono stanco.
examples.en: It's not that I don't want to, it's that I'm tired.
When is it you're leaving?

grammar.trap: English does this with voice stress ('it's the ACCENT'); Italian needs the structure, and after non è che the subjunctive.

grammar.explain: A set of everyday verbs carry fixed pronouns (ce la, se la, ne) and must be learned whole.

examples.it: avercela con: Ce l'hai con me?
examples.en: be angry with: Are you angry with me?

examples.it: farcela / mettercela tutta: Ce l'ho messa tutta, ma non ce l'ho fatta.
examples.en: make it / give it your all: I gave it my all, but I didn't make it.

examples.it: prendersela: Non te la prendere. / vedersela brutta: Me la sono vista brutta.
examples.en: take offence: Don't take it badly. / have a close call: I had a close call.

examples.it: farsene una ragione: Me ne devo fare una ragione.
examples.en: come to terms with it: I have to come to terms with it.

grammar.trap: The pronouns change with the person, and the participle agrees with la: ce l'ho fatta, me la sono vista brutta.

grammar.explain: Markers like ecco, diciamo, cioè, insomma, appunto, mah, vabbè and che ne so organise and soften speech; recognise them all and use a few naturally.

examples.it: Insomma, diciamo che non è andata benissimo.
examples.en: Well, let's say it didn't go brilliantly.

examples.it: Cioè, voglio dire… / Appunto! / Mah, non saprei.
examples.en: I mean… / Exactly! / Hmm, I'm not sure.

grammar.trap: Appunto means 'exactly, just what I said', not 'by the way'; and repeating one marker in every sentence sounds nervous.

grammar.explain: Regional speech changes sounds and short words; you only need to recognise them.

examples.it: Roman: nun = non, pe' = per, er = il, 'sto = questo, mo' = adesso, daje = dai
examples.en: Roman forms and their standard Italian
Neapolitan forms and their standard Italian

grammar.trap: Don't imitate a dialect with strangers: it can sound like mockery. Use a word or two only with friends who use them with you.

vocabulary.en: to take offence, to take it badly
to come to terms with it
vocabulary.form: me ne devo fare una ragione

pronunciation: Roman speech shortens rr (tera for terra), doubles some b's and g's between vowels (robba, bbono) and turns l before a consonant into r (sordi for soldi, er for il); recognise these, don't copy them.
Markers carry the meaning in their tune: mah falls and drags (doubt), eh rises (agreement or 'you see?'), appunto stresses -PUN- firmly.

common_errors.why: The idiom is avercela con.
The participle agrees with la in ce l'ho fatta.

common_errors.wrong: Non è che non voglio venire.
common_errors.right: Non è che non voglia venire.
common_errors.why: Non è che introduces a denied reason: subjunctive.
The idiom is fixed with la.

units.culture: Almost every Italian speaks regional Italian with a local accent, and many also speak or understand a dialect; being asked 'di dove sei?' is curiosity about place, not suspicion. People enjoy hearing a foreigner pick up a local word, but they switch to standard Italian with strangers and in offices, and you should too.
recycles: Sono alla frutta! / Vabbè, lascia stare. (b2-13)
units.evidence: In fast informal talk the learner follows a Roman or other regional speaker after at most one request to repeat, uses two or three markers (insomma, diciamo, appunto) where they fit, and handles pronominal idioms with the right agreement.
sources: P3 U26 (dialects; clefts; pronominal idioms; Romanesco → Italian)
P3 transcripts §3 (ecco, diciamo, cioè, insomma, appunto, mah, vabbè, che ne so)
SLANG (Rome items, corrected glosses: small-books notes §3)
P2 U3 (farcela, cavarsela, prendersela)

units.title: Society in debate: legality, migration, belief
units.can_do: Debate social questions at length and with precision: build an argument, generalise and qualify, and use every kind of subordinate clause.

frames.it: Chiunque abbia vissuto qui sa che la legalità si costruisce dal basso.
frames.en: Anyone who has lived here knows that legality is built from the ground up.

frames.it: Coloro che pagano il pizzo non lo fanno certo per scelta.
frames.en: Those who pay protection money certainly don't do it by choice.

frames.it: Non è un problema del Sud, bensì di tutto il Paese.
frames.en: It's not a problem of the South, but of the whole country.

frames.it: Ci si abitua a tutto, eppure certe cose non vanno accettate.
frames.en: You get used to anything, and yet some things mustn't be accepted.

frames.it: Ciò che conta non è la provenienza, ma il rispetto reciproco.
frames.en: What matters isn't where you come from, but mutual respect.

frames.it: Ammesso che sia vero, cosa cambierebbe?
frames.en: Assuming it's true, what would change?

frames.it: Dovunque si vada, si trova qualcuno che fa la differenza.
frames.en: Wherever you go, you find someone who makes a difference.

frames.it: Bisogna garantire la laicità dello Stato, nonché il rispetto di tutte le fedi.
frames.en: We must guarantee a secular state, as well as respect for all faiths.

frames.it: Pertanto direi che la questione va affrontata a livello nazionale.
frames.en: Therefore I'd say the issue must be tackled nationally.

model_exchanges.situation: a serious discussion with a friend

lines.speaker: amica
lines.it: Secondo me la mafia è un problema del Sud. Qui al Nord non ci riguarda.
lines.en: In my view the mafia is a southern problem. Up here in the North it doesn't concern us.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Non sono d'accordo: non è un problema del Sud, bensì di tutto il Paese. Gli appalti truccati ci sono anche qui.
lines.en: I don't agree: it's not a problem of the South, but of the whole country. There are rigged contracts here too.

lines.speaker: amica
lines.it: Ammesso che sia vero, cosa possiamo fare noi?
lines.en: Assuming that's true, what can we do?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Parecchio. Chiunque compri nei negozi che rifiutano il pizzo fa già qualcosa.
lines.en: Quite a lot. Anyone who shops at businesses that refuse to pay protection money is already doing something.

lines.speaker: amica
lines.it: Sì, ma coloro che pagano non lo fanno certo per scelta.
lines.en: Yes, but those who pay certainly don't do it by choice.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Appunto. Pertanto direi che la questione va affrontata a livello nazionale, non lasciata ai commercianti.
lines.en: Exactly. Therefore I'd say the issue must be tackled nationally, not left to shopkeepers.

model_exchanges.situation: a guest on a local radio programme about integration

lines.speaker: conduttore
lines.it: Lei vive in Italia da qualche anno. Ci si integra facilmente?
lines.en: You've lived in Italy for some years. Is it easy to integrate?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Ci si abitua a tutto, eppure certe cose restano difficili: la burocrazia, soprattutto.
lines.en: You get used to anything, and yet some things stay hard: bureaucracy above all.

lines.speaker: conduttore
lines.it: E il rapporto con gli italiani?
lines.en: And relations with Italians?

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Ottimo. Ciò che conta, secondo me, non è la provenienza, ma il rispetto reciproco.
lines.en: Excellent. What matters, in my view, isn't where you come from, but mutual respect.

lines.speaker: conduttore
lines.it: C'è chi dice che gli stranieri tolgano lavoro agli italiani.
lines.en: Some people say foreigners take jobs away from Italians.

lines.speaker: newcomer
lines.it: Posto che il lavoro manchi davvero, la causa non sono certo gli stranieri, bensì un'economia che cresce poco.
lines.en: Even assuming work really is scarce, the cause certainly isn't foreigners, but an economy that grows very little.

grammar.explain: 'Whoever', 'whatever' and 'wherever' take the subjunctive.

examples.it: Chiunque abbia vissuto qui lo sa.
examples.en: Anyone who has lived here knows it.

examples.it: Dovunque si vada, si trova qualcuno che aiuta.
examples.en: Wherever you go, you find someone who helps.
Whatever they decide, we'll talk about it.

grammar.trap: Chiunque is singular: chiunque abbia, never chiunque abbiano.

grammar.point: colui che, coloro che, ciò che
grammar.explain: Formal Italian uses colui che (he who), colei che (she who), coloro che (those who) and ciò che (what), where everyday speech says chi, quelli che, quello che.

examples.it: Coloro che pagano il pizzo non lo fanno per scelta.
examples.en: Those who pay protection money don't do it by choice.

examples.it: Ciò che conta è il rispetto.
examples.en: What matters is respect.

examples.it: Chi paga non lo fa per scelta.
examples.en: Whoever pays doesn't do it by choice.

grammar.trap: Chi takes a singular verb even when it means 'those who': chi paga, not chi pagano.

grammar.point: the three si's, and ci si
grammar.explain: Si can mean 'people, you' (impersonal), make a passive (si costruisce), or be reflexive; a reflexive verb used impersonally needs ci si.

examples.it: La legalità si costruisce dal basso.
examples.en: Legality is built from the ground up. (passive)
You get used to anything. (impersonal reflexive)
People live well here. (impersonal)

grammar.trap: Never si si abitua or si ci abitua: it's always ci si abitua.

grammar.explain: Bensì (but rather, after a negative), eppure (and yet), pertanto (therefore), tuttavia (however), ossia (that is) and nonché (as well as) give an argument its structure.

examples.it: Non del Sud, bensì di tutto il Paese.
examples.en: Not of the South, but of the whole country.

examples.it: È difficile, eppure si può fare.
examples.en: It's hard, and yet it can be done.
Therefore I'd say that…

grammar.trap: Bensì only follows a negative: 'grave, bensì risolvibile' is wrong; use ma there.

grammar.explain: Ammesso che and posto che ('assuming that', 'even granting that') concede a premise and take the subjunctive.

examples.it: Ammesso che sia vero, cosa cambierebbe?
examples.en: Assuming it's true, what would change?

examples.it: Posto che il lavoro manchi davvero…
examples.en: Even assuming work really is scarce…

grammar.trap: Don't confuse them with dato che / visto che ('since'), which state a fact and take the indicative: dato che è vero…

pronunciation: Connectors ending in an accent carry the stress on the last syllable: ben-SÌ, non-CHÉ, per-CIÒ, poi-CHÉ; swallowing it makes them hard to catch.
In a long argument, pause briefly after the connector (Pertanto, | direi che…): it marks the structure and buys you thinking time.

common_errors.wrong: Chiunque hanno vissuto qui lo sa.
common_errors.right: Chiunque abbia vissuto qui lo sa.
common_errors.why: Chiunque is singular and takes the subjunctive.
Impersonal + reflexive is ci si.

common_errors.wrong: È un problema grave, bensì risolvibile.
common_errors.right: È un problema grave, ma risolvibile.
common_errors.why: Bensì only follows a negative.
Ammesso che takes the subjunctive.
Coloro is plural; only chi takes the singular.

units.culture: Italians discuss the mafia, migration and the Church openly and with strong views, and many have personal stakes in them. Associations like Libera (anti-mafia, with a day of remembrance on 21 March) and Addiopizzo (businesses that refuse protection money) are part of civic life. In debate, conceding a point before disagreeing (ammesso che…, d'altra parte…) is seen as good manners, not weakness.
recycles: Non per questo penso che siano tutti chiusi. (b2-09)
units.evidence: In an extended discussion the learner builds a three-step argument (premise with ammesso che, contrast with bensì or eppure, conclusion with pertanto), uses chiunque / coloro che / ci si correctly, and qualifies generalisations instead of stating them flatly.
sources: P3 U22 (si impersonale / passivante / riflessivo; immigration and integration)
P3 U23 (mafia and legality; chiunque / qualunque + subjunctive; colui che)
P3 U30 (clause types; bensì, eppure, pertanto, tuttavia, ossia, nonché)
P3 U21 (religion)
P3 U28 (ci si)

grammar_inventory.title: Fuori grammar inventory: Italian A1–C1
grammar_inventory.author: Magda
grammar_inventory.about: Every grammar point in the A1–C1 outline (outline.json), at the unit where the outline teaches it, grouped by part of speech and in teaching order within each group (outline unit order). A handful of points the outline implies but never names are added at the unit that first needs them. use = "say" means the learner produces it at that unit; "understand" means recognise only (it is produced at a later unit or never). explain is one plain English sentence; trap is the mistake English speakers make.

points.point: noun gender and the indefinite article: un caffè, uno spritz, una spremuta, un'aranciata
points.explain: 'A/an' is un for most masculine words, uno before s + consonant or z, una for feminine words and un' for feminine words starting with a vowel.
points.trap: Only feminine words take an apostrophe: un amico, but un'amica.

points.point: the definite article: il, lo, l', la, i, gli, le (lo / gli before s + consonant and z)
points.explain: 'The' changes with gender, number and the first sound of the next word: il pane, lo zucchero, l'acqua, la pasta, i panini, gli spaghetti, le mele.
points.trap: Italian uses 'the' where English doesn't, with general and abstract nouns (il caffè è buono = coffee is good).

points.point: un po' di for 'some'; del / della as a chunk (vorrei del pane)
points.explain: Un po' di + noun is the easy way to say 'some'; del/della + noun (the partitive) also means 'some'.
points.trap: In a negative sentence 'any' disappears: non ho pane, not non ho del pane.

points.point: partitive dropped in negatives and often in questions
points.explain: In negatives the partitive disappears (non ho pane) and in questions it's optional (hai (del) pane?).
points.trap: English 'any' tempts non ho del pane.

points.point: days need no preposition: lunedì = this Monday, il lunedì = on Mondays
points.explain: A day on its own means this coming one (lunedì), and with the article it means every week (il lunedì).
points.trap: There is no word for 'on': on Monday is just lunedì.

points.point: nouns are masculine or feminine; most -o are masculine, most -a feminine, -e can be either
points.explain: Every noun has a gender, usually shown by its ending, and you learn each noun with its article.
points.trap: Nouns in -e (la chiave, il giornale) give no clue, so learn the article with the word; il problema and la mano break the pattern.

points.point: plurals: due cappuccini, due cornetti; words ending in an accent don't change (due caffè, due tè)
points.explain: Masculine -o becomes -i, feminine -a becomes -e, -e becomes -i, and words ending in an accented vowel or a consonant don't change.
points.trap: Adding -s for the plural (due cappuccinos) is the English reflex; foreign words like bar and film never add -s.

points.point: euro never changes: due euro
points.explain: Euro has the same form in the singular and plural.
points.trap: Don't add -s or -i: due euros and due euri are both wrong.

points.point: plurals of produce (le pesche, le zucchine)
points.explain: Fruit and vegetables are usually asked for in the plural: le pesche, le albicocche, le zucchine.
points.trap: Words in -ca/-ga add an h in the plural to keep the hard sound (pesca → pesche, albicocca → albicocche).

points.point: irregular plurals: l'uomo/gli uomini, la mano/le mani, l'uovo/le uova, il braccio/le braccia
points.explain: A few common nouns have irregular plurals, some changing gender: le uova, le braccia, le dita.
points.trap: Regular-looking plurals (gli uovi) are wrong.

points.point: altered nouns: -ino, -etto, -one, -accio
points.explain: Suffixes change size or tone: -ino/-etto (small, nice), -one (big), -accio (bad): casetta, librone, giornataccia.
points.trap: Some look altered but aren't (tavolino is a coffee table; mattone is a brick).

points.point: nouns whose meaning changes with gender (il capitale / la capitale, il fine / la fine)
points.explain: A few nouns change meaning with gender: il capitale (money) / la capitale (city), il fine (aim) / la fine (end).
points.trap: The article carries the meaning, so a wrong article changes what you say.

points.point: feminine job titles and the debate around them (la ministra, la sindaca, l'avvocata)
points.explain: Feminine forms of job titles are increasingly used (la sindaca, la ministra), though some people still prefer the masculine.
points.trap: Choose consistently and follow what the person prefers.

points.point: nominal style
points.explain: Bureaucratic Italian turns verbs into nouns (il pagamento effettuato, la presentazione della domanda).
points.trap: Overusing it in speech or friendly emails sounds stiff.

points.point: nominalisation (la stagionatura, la lavorazione)
points.explain: Nouns from verbs with -tura, -zione, -mento name processes: stagionare → la stagionatura.
points.trap: The suffix isn't predictable; learn each pair.

points.point: nationality adjectives agree: americano / americana; inglese for both
points.explain: Adjectives ending in -o change to -a for a woman; adjectives ending in -e stay the same for both.
points.trap: English adjectives never change; Italians notice at once if a woman says sono americano.

points.point: numbers 0–100, then cento, duecento, mille, duemila (ventuno, ventotto drop a vowel)
points.explain: Tens join units in one word, dropping the final vowel before uno and otto (ventuno, trentotto); mille becomes -mila in the plural.
points.trap: Italian writes a comma for decimals and a point for thousands (4,50 €; 1.000), the reverse of English.

points.point: questo / quello again: quelle lì
points.explain: Quello/quella/quelli/quelle lì point to things further away; they agree with the noun.
points.trap: The ending must match what you mean: quelle lì for apricots (feminine plural).

points.point: ordinal numbers for floors: al primo, al terzo piano
points.explain: Ordinals (primo, secondo, terzo...) agree with the noun and floors take al: abito al terzo piano.
points.trap: Il primo piano is one floor above the ground floor (piano terra): the British 'first floor', the American 'second floor'.

points.point: possessives take the article: il mio, la mia, i miei, le mie; il loro
points.explain: Possessives agree with the thing owned, not the owner, and normally take the article: la mia casa, i miei amici.
points.trap: Suo means both 'his' and 'her': his car is la sua macchina.

points.point: no article with one family member (mia madre, tuo fratello), but the article comes back in the plural and with loro (i miei figli, la loro figlia)
points.explain: With a single unmodified family member you drop the article (mia sorella), but you keep it in the plural, with loro and with endearments (la mia mamma).
points.trap: Learners either always or never use the article; partners aren't family here (il mio compagno).

points.point: describing adjectives and their agreement
points.explain: Describing adjectives go after the noun and agree in gender and number: una ragazza alta, dei capelli neri.
points.trap: Hair is plural (i capelli), so adjectives describing it are plural too.

points.point: bello, buono and grande before nouns; position changes nuance
points.explain: A few common adjectives (bello, buono, grande, piccolo, nuovo, vecchio) often go before the noun; most others follow it.
points.trap: Colour and nationality adjectives always follow the noun (una macchina rossa).

points.point: colours agree (rosso / rossa) except blu, rosa, viola
points.explain: Colour adjectives agree with the noun, but blu, rosa, viola, beige and others don't change.
points.trap: Colours follow the noun (una giacca blu, never una blu giacca).

points.point: quello and bello before nouns change like the article: quel maglione, quegli stivali, un bel cappotto
points.explain: Before a noun, quello and bello take the same endings as the article: quel/quello/quell'/quei/quegli, bel/bello/bell'/bei/begli.
points.trap: Learners say quello maglione or quelli stivali; follow the article (il → quel, gli → quegli).

points.point: comparisons: più / meno ... di; (così) ... come
points.explain: Più/meno + adjective + di compares two things (più caro di); (così)... come or (tanto)... quanto says 'as... as'.
points.trap: 'Than' is di (+ article): più grande della mia, not che la mia.

points.point: superlatives: il più ... di (trap: 'in town' = della città), -issimo, migliore / peggiore
points.explain: 'The most' is il più + adjective + di; -issimo means 'very'; buono/cattivo have migliore/peggiore.
points.trap: 'The best in town' is la migliore della città, not in città; più buono is fine in speech but don't say più migliore.

points.point: comparisons with di vs che (più luminoso dell'altro; più bello che comodo)
points.explain: Use di before a noun or pronoun, and che when comparing two adjectives, verbs or phrases: più bello che comodo.
points.trap: Learners use di everywhere (più leggere di scrivere should be più leggere che scrivere).

points.point: relative and absolute superlatives; irregular forms (migliore, il peggiore, ottimo, pessimo)
points.explain: Il più... di is 'the most... in', ottimo/pessimo mean 'excellent/terrible', and maggiore/minore are 'older/younger' for siblings.
points.trap: Double comparatives like più migliore or più ottimo are wrong.

points.point: comparisons in use
points.explain: Comparatives and superlatives help you weigh options: il treno è più comodo del pullman.
points.trap: 'Than' before a noun is di + article (del pullman).

points.point: centuries: il Trecento = the 1300s, il Quattrocento = the 1400s
points.explain: Italian names centuries from 1200 to 1900 by their hundreds: il Duecento (1200s) ... il Novecento (1900s).
points.trap: Il Trecento is the 14th century, not the 13th.

points.point: adjective position changes meaning (un grande artista / un artista grande)
points.explain: Some adjectives change meaning with position: un grande artista (great), un artista grande (big); un vecchio amico (long-time), un amico vecchio (old).
points.trap: English has fixed adjective position, so the nuance is missed.

points.point: present participles as adjectives (avvincente, affascinante)
points.explain: Many adjectives come from present participles in -ante/-ente: avvincente, affascinante, deludente.
points.trap: English '-ing' adjectives map here, not to the gerund (un libro avvincente, not un libro avvincendo).

points.point: intensifiers: da morire, un sacco di, stanco morto, pieno zeppo
points.explain: Colloquial intensifiers boost a word: mi piace da morire, un sacco di gente, stanco morto.
points.trap: They're informal; morto agrees (stanca morta).

points.point: proprio as a generic possessive
points.explain: Proprio means 'one's own' with general subjects: ogni genitore vuole il meglio per i propri figli.
points.trap: Not to be confused with the adverb proprio ('really').

points.point: negative prefixes: in-, im-, s-, dis-
points.explain: Prefixes reverse meaning: in-/im-/il-/ir- (inutile, impossibile, illegale, irregolare), s- (scortese), dis- (disonesto).
points.trap: In- becomes im- before b/p/m and assimilates before l and r.

points.point: present participles as adjectives and nouns (provenienti, conservanti, deludente)
points.explain: Present participles work as adjectives (prodotti provenienti dalla Puglia) and nouns (i conservanti).
points.trap: They agree in number (provenienti), unlike English '-ing'.

points.point: past participles as adjectives (spremuto, stagionato)
points.explain: Past participles describe processed products and agree with the noun: olio spremuto a freddo, formaggio stagionato.
points.trap: Agreement is required: la mozzarella stagionata.

points.point: similes and intensified adjectives
points.explain: Fixed similes and intensifiers colour description: sordo come una campana, ricco sfondato, calzare come un guanto.
points.trap: They're fixed; you can't swap the comparison.

points.point: tu and Lei as two sets of chunks (Come stai? / Come sta?; Scusa / Scusi); Lei takes the 3rd-person verb
points.explain: Use tu with friends, children and people your age who use it with you, and Lei with strangers, shopkeepers and officials; Lei takes the same verb form as 'he/she'.
points.trap: English has one 'you', so learners mix the two in one sentence (Scusa, come sta?); when in doubt, use Lei.

points.point: questo and quello as pronouns (questo, quello lì) — point when you don't know the word
points.explain: Questo means 'this one' and quello 'that one'; they agree with the thing you point at.
points.trap: There's no word for 'one': say questo, not questo uno; if you don't know the gender, pointing and saying questo is fine.

points.point: mi dà...? as a fixed polite request
points.explain: Mi dà...? (literally 'do you give me...?') is the everyday polite way to ask for something at a counter.
points.trap: English 'can I have' tempts posso avere, which works but sounds translated; mi dà is what Italians say.

points.point: stressed pronouns after prepositions: con me, per te, da lui
points.explain: After a preposition use me, te, lui, lei, Lei, noi, voi, loro: vieni con me?
points.trap: Not con mi or per tu.

points.point: ne heard as a chunk (quanto ne vuole?) before it's taught at A2
points.explain: Ne means 'of it/of them' and stands for the food already mentioned: quanto ne vuole? = how much (of it) do you want?
points.trap: English drops 'of it', so ne is easy to miss when you hear it.

points.point: ti piace / Le piace; anche a me, neanche a me, a me no
points.explain: Ti piace asks a friend, Le piace asks someone you call Lei; anche a me = me too, neanche a me = me neither.
points.trap: 'Me too' after mi piace is anche a me, not anche io.

points.point: possessive pronouns after essere drop the article (è mia)
points.explain: After essere the possessive usually stands alone: è mia, sono tuoi?
points.trap: 'Mine' has no separate word; it's the same as 'my' and agrees with the thing (la borsa? è mia).

points.point: mi / ci + verb chunks (ci porta, mi consiglia), ahead of the full pronoun system
points.explain: Mi (to me) and ci (to us) go before the verb in requests: ci porta il conto? cosa mi consiglia?
points.trap: English puts 'us' after the verb; in Italian it comes first.

points.point: lo prendo / la prendo as chunks
points.explain: Lo prendo / la prendo means 'I'll take it', with lo for a masculine thing and la for a feminine one.
points.trap: 'It' must match the gender of the thing: la pizza → la prendo.

points.point: direct object pronouns lo, la, li, le before the verb (lo prendo, le preferisco); with a modal before it or attached (lo posso assaggiare / posso assaggiarlo)
points.explain: Lo, la, li, le replace a thing or person already mentioned and go before the verb, or attach to an infinitive.
points.trap: English puts 'it' after the verb; Italian puts it first, and never between the modal and infinitive (posso lo assaggiare is wrong).

points.point: ne with quantities (ne prendo tre etti; ne vorrei due)
points.explain: Ne replaces the thing when you give a quantity: ne prendo due (I'll take two of them).
points.trap: You can't leave the quantity alone (prendo due); and with 'all of them' use li: li prendo tutti.

points.point: ce l'ho / ce l'avete; ce n'è / ce ne sono
points.explain: In speech 'have it' is ce l'ho / ce l'avete, and 'there's some' is ce n'è / ce ne sono.
points.trap: Ho alone sounds incomplete when you mean 'I have it'; the ce is idiomatic, not 'there'.

points.point: direct pronouns recycled (la provo, la prendo)
points.explain: In a shop, la/lo refer to the item: la posso provare? la prendo.
points.trap: Match the noun's gender: la giacca → la, il maglione → lo.

points.point: indirect object pronouns: mi, ti, gli (to him), le (to her), Le (to you, formal), ci, vi, gli (to them)
points.explain: Indirect pronouns replace 'to someone' and go before the verb: gli telefono, le scrivo, Le dispiace?
points.trap: Gli = to him (and to them), le = to her, Le = to you formal; telefonare takes an indirect object (gli telefono, not lo telefono).

points.point: che ne pensi? as a chunk (ne = of it)
points.explain: Che ne pensi? / che ne pensa? asks 'what do you think of it?'.
points.trap: Pensare a means 'think about' (penso a te); opinions use pensare di, which ne replaces.

points.point: pronoun attached after devo (devo prenderlo)
points.explain: With a modal you can attach the pronoun to the infinitive: devo prenderlo.
points.trap: Don't place it between them (devo lo prendere).

points.point: pronouns with modals (posso cambiarla)
points.explain: The pronoun goes before the modal or attaches to the infinitive: la posso cambiare / posso cambiarla.
points.trap: Never between them, and match the gender of the item.

points.point: combined pronouns: me lo, te la, glielo / gliela (to him, her, you formal, them), ce ne, me ne
points.explain: When two pronouns meet, the indirect comes first and changes mi→me, ti→te, gli/le→glie-: me lo dai? glielo porto.
points.trap: Glielo covers 'it to him/her/you/them'; English speakers try to say gli lo or le lo.

points.point: with modals: te lo posso dare / posso dartelo
points.explain: Combined pronouns go before the modal or attach to the infinitive as one word: posso dartelo.
points.trap: Splitting them (te posso darlo) is wrong.

points.point: relative che for subjects and objects
points.explain: Che (who, which, that) links a clause to a noun, as subject or object: la banca che mi hai consigliato.
points.trap: It can never be left out, unlike English 'the bank you recommended'.

points.point: preposition + cui (con cui, di cui, in cui); dove vs in cui for places
points.explain: After a preposition the relative is cui: la persona con cui ho parlato; for places dove often replaces in cui.
points.trap: The preposition goes first, never at the end: not la persona che ho parlato con.

points.point: quello che / ciò che
points.explain: Quello che / ciò che means 'what' in the sense of 'the thing that': non capisco quello che dici.
points.trap: 'What' here isn't cosa or che alone.

points.point: relative clauses recycled
points.explain: Che and cui let you describe flats and terms precisely: l'appartamento di cui ti ho parlato.
points.trap: Keep the relative pronoun every time.

points.point: nessuno with non, and in front without it (nessuno ci ha aiutato)
points.explain: After the verb, nessuno needs non (non è venuto nessuno); at the start of the sentence it stands alone (nessuno è venuto).
points.trap: English forbids double negatives, but Italian requires non... nessuno.

points.point: indefinites: qualche + singular, alcuni, ogni, ognuno, nessuno, qualcosa di...
points.explain: Qualche (some) and ogni (every) take a singular noun; alcuni takes the plural; qualcosa di + adjective means 'something...'.
points.trap: Qualche libri and ogni giorni are typical errors; it's qualche libro, ogni giorno.

points.point: ci in full: ci provo, ci penso, ci metto, non ci capisco
points.explain: Ci stands for 'there' or for a + something already mentioned: ci penso io (I'll see to it), ci provo (I'll try).
points.trap: Ci in these phrases isn't 'us', and it can't be left out.

points.point: ne in full: ne parlo, me ne occupo, ne ho sentito parlare
points.explain: Ne stands for di + something already mentioned: ne ho sentito parlare (I've heard of it), me ne occupo io.
points.trap: English 'of it' or 'about it' usually disappears, so learners drop ne.
